title.zh: 卷一百三十九 列傳第八十九: 陸贄
title.raw: 卷一百三十九 列傳第八十九: 陸贄 Volume 139 Biographies 89: Lu Zhi

sentences.zh: 陸贄，字敬輿，蘇州嘉興人。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, styled Jingyu, was a man of Jiaxing in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, whose courtesy name was Jingyu, came from Jiaxing in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 父侃，溧陽令，以贄貴，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Kan was magistrate of Liyang; because of Zhi's eminence, [Kan] was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kan had served as magistrate of Liyang; when Zhi rose to prominence, Kan was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 贄少孤，特立不群，頗勤儒學。

translations.literal: Zhi was orphaned young, stood alone apart from the crowd, and was quite diligent in Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi lost his father while still young. He held himself apart from others and applied himself diligently to classical learning.

sentences.zh: 年十八登進士第，以博學宏詞登科，授華州鄭縣尉。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he passed the jinshi degree, also passed the Broad Learning and Grand Phrase examination, and was appointed defender of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he passed the jinshi examination and also qualified through the Broad Learning and Grand Phrase test, after which he was appointed county defender of Zheng in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 罷秩，東歸省母，路由壽州，刺史張鎰有時名，贄往謁之。

translations.literal: When his term ended he went east to visit his mother; his route passed through Shou Prefecture, whose prefect Zhang Yin had a reputation of the time, and Zhi went to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: After his term ended he traveled east to visit his mother. Passing through Shou Prefecture, he called on the prefect Zhang Yin, who was widely esteemed at the time.

sentences.zh: 鎰初不甚知，留三日，再見與語，遂大稱賞，請結忘年之契。

translations.literal: Yin at first did not know him well; after three days and two more meetings with conversation, he greatly praised and admired him and asked to form a friendship that forgot the difference in age.
translations.idiomatic: Yin did not think much of him at first, but after Zhi had stayed three days and they had spoken twice more, Yin came to admire him greatly and asked to become his friend despite the gap in their years.

sentences.zh: 及辭，遺贄錢百萬，曰：「願備太夫人一日之膳。

translations.literal: When he took leave, [Yin] gave Zhi a million in cash, saying, "May this supply one day's provisions for the Lady Dowager."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi was leaving, Yin gave him a million cash and said, "Please accept this for one day's meals for your mother."

sentences.zh: 」贄不納，唯受新茶一串而已，曰：「敢不承君厚意。

translations.literal: " Zhi did not accept it, taking only one bunch of new tea, and said, "How dare I fail to acknowledge your generous kindness."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi declined the money, accepting only a single bundle of fresh tea, and said, "I would never fail to acknowledge your generous kindness."

sentences.zh: 」又以書判拔萃，選授渭南縣主簿，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: " He also passed the examination for excellence in document review, was selected and appointed chief clerk of Weinan County, and was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: " He later passed the document-review examination with highest honors, was selected and appointed chief clerk of Weinan County, and was then promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 德宗在東宮時，素知贄名，乃召為翰林學士，轉祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Dezong was in the Eastern Palace he had long known Zhi's name; he summoned him as Hanlin academician and transferred him to vice director in the Department of Sacrificial Worship.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent, Dezong had long known Zhi's reputation. He summoned him as a Hanlin academician and later appointed him vice director of sacrificial affairs.

sentences.zh: 贄性忠盡，既居近密，感人主重知，思有以效報，故政或有缺，巨細必陳，由是顧待益厚。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was loyal and wholehearted; once he held a post near [the emperor's] person and felt the sovereign's weight of trust, he wished to repay it in some way. Whenever policies had flaws, great or small, he always submitted them; for this favor and care toward him grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was loyal to the core. Once he served close to the throne and felt the emperor's deep trust, he sought every way to repay it. Whenever he saw a flaw in policy, large or small, he spoke up; the emperor's regard for him only deepened.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，硃泚謀逆，從駕幸奉天。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, Zhu Ci plotted rebellion; [the emperor] followed the imperial procession to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, Zhu Ci plotted rebellion, and the emperor fled with the court to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 時天下叛亂，機務填委，征發指蹤，千端萬緒，一日之內，詔書數百。

translations.literal: At that time rebellion filled the realm; official business piled up; levies and dispatches pointed in every direction—thousands of threads, ten thousand ends; within a single day edicts numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion engulfed the empire, and state business piled up without end. Levies and orders flew in every direction; within a single day hundreds of edicts had to be drafted.

sentences.zh: 贄揮翰起草，思如泉註，初若不經思慮，既成之後，莫不曲盡事情，中於機會；

translations.literal: Zhi wielded the brush to draft them; thought poured like a spring. At first it seemed as though he gave no thought; after they were finished, none failed to exhaust the matter and hit the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi drafted them at the brush; ideas poured forth like a spring. At first his drafts seemed effortless, yet when finished each one fully addressed the matter and seized the moment.

sentences.zh: 胥吏簡劄不暇，同舍皆伏其能。

translations.literal: Clerks could scarcely keep up copying the documents; colleagues in the same office all acknowledged his ability.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks could barely keep up copying his drafts, and everyone in the Hanlin office marveled at his skill.

sentences.zh: 轉考功郎中，依前充職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Bureau of Appointments while continuing in his previous duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Bureau of Appointments while continuing his Hanlin duties.

sentences.zh: 嘗啟德宗曰：「今盜遍天下，輿駕播遷，陛下宜痛自引過，以感動人心。

translations.literal: He once addressed Dezong: "Now bandits cover the realm; the imperial carriage is cast about. Your Majesty should deeply reproach yourself to move men's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: He once urged Dezong, "Bandits now fill the realm and the throne is driven into exile. Your Majesty should openly blame yourself and thereby move the hearts of the people."

sentences.zh: 昔成湯以罪己勃興，楚昭以善言復國。

translations.literal: Formerly Cheng Tang through blaming himself flourished; King Zhao of Chu through good words recovered his state.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Cheng Tang revived his power by confessing his faults, and King Zhao of Chu restored his state by heeding good counsel.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能不吝改過，以言謝天下，使書詔無忌，臣雖愚陋，可以仰副聖情，庶令反側之徒，革心向化。

translations.literal: "If Your Majesty truly will not stint at changing faults and apologize to the realm in words, so that written edicts have no taboo—even though I am stupid and mean, I can upwardly match the sagely wish—perhaps the rebellious may change heart and turn to reform."
translations.idiomatic: "If Your Majesty will not hesitate to amend your ways and apologize to the realm in your edicts, holding nothing back, then even someone as dull as I can help fulfill your intent, and those who waver may turn their hearts toward loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」德宗然之。

translations.literal: " Dezong approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Dezong agreed.

sentences.zh: 故奉天所下書詔，雖武夫悍卒，無不揮涕感激，多贄所為也。

translations.literal: Thus the written edicts issued at Fengtian—even fierce soldiers—none failed to weep in gratitude; most were Zhi's compositions.
translations.idiomatic: The edicts issued at Fengtian moved even rough soldiers to tears of gratitude; most of them were drafted by Zhi.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，議欲以新歲改元。

translations.literal: That winter there was discussion of changing the reign title at the new year.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the court discussed changing the reign era at the new year.

sentences.zh: 而卜祝之流，皆以國家數鐘百六，凡事宜有變革，以應時數。

translations.literal: But diviners and prayer-officials all held that the state's fate had reached the hundred-six calamity cycle and that all affairs should have change to accord with the times' numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Diviners and ritual specialists argued that the dynasty had entered an inauspicious cycle and that reforms were needed to align with the times.

sentences.zh: 上謂贄曰：「往年群臣請上尊號『聖神文武』四字，今緣寇難，諸事並宜改更，眾欲朕舊號之中更加一兩字，其事何如？

translations.literal: The emperor said to Zhi: "In former years the ministers asked to bestow on me the honorific title of four characters 'Sagely, Divine, Martial, and Civil.' Now because of bandit calamity all affairs should be changed; the multitude wishes to add one or two characters to my old title—what of this matter?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Zhi, "Years ago the ministers asked to give me the honorific 'Sagely, Divine, Martial, and Civil.' Now, with rebellion upon us, many say everything should change, and some want to add one or two words to my old title. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」贄奏曰：「尊號之興，本非古制。

translations.literal: " Zhi memorialized: "The rise of honorific titles was never an ancient institution."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi replied, "Honorific titles were never part of ancient practice."

sentences.zh: 行於安泰之日，已累謙沖；

translations.literal: Practiced in days of peace and security, it already burdens modesty and restraint;
translations.idiomatic: Even in peaceful times they burden a ruler's humility;

sentences.zh: 襲乎喪亂之時，尤傷事體。

translations.literal: carried on in times of mourning and disorder, it especially harms the proper form of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: to adopt them in the midst of disaster is still more damaging to propriety.

sentences.zh: 今者鑾輿播越，未復宮闈，宗社震驚，尚愆禋祀，中區多梗，大憝猶存。

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage is cast about, the palace quarters not yet restored; the altars of state are shaken, sacrificial rites still neglected; the central regions have many obstructions, the great enemy still exists.
translations.idiomatic: Your carriage is still in exile, the palace unrestored, the altars unsettled, sacrifices neglected, the heartland obstructed, and the chief rebel still at large.

sentences.zh: 此乃人情向背之秋，天意去就之際，陛下宜深自懲勵，收攬群心，痛自貶損，以謝靈譴，不可近從末議，重益美名。

translations.literal: This is the season when men's hearts turn away or toward you, the juncture when Heaven's intent departs or stays. Your Majesty should deeply reproach and encourage yourself, gather all hearts, bitterly humble yourself to apologize to Heaven's punishment—you must not follow petty proposals and again increase your glorious name.
translations.idiomatic: This is the moment when the people's loyalty hangs in the balance and Heaven's favor may depart. Your Majesty should discipline yourself, win back every heart, and humble yourself before Heaven—not heed petty counsel and pile on more empty praise.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿所奏陳，雖理體甚切，然時運必須小有改跡，亦不可執滯，卿更思量。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "What you have memorialized, though its principle and form are very apt, yet the times' fortune must have some small change of trace; one also cannot be obstinate—consider further."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Your reasoning is sound, but the times demand some outward change; we cannot be rigid. Think again."

sentences.zh: 」贄曰：「古之人君稱號，或稱皇稱帝，或稱王，但一字而已。

translations.literal: " Zhi said: "Ancient rulers' titles—some called themselves August, some Emperor, some King—only a single character."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi said, "Ancient rulers called themselves Huang, Di, or Wang—a single word each."

sentences.zh: 至暴秦，乃兼皇帝二字，後代因之。

translations.literal: It reached the violent Qin, which then combined the two characters Huang and Di; later ages followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Only under the tyrannical Qin were Huang and Di combined, and later dynasties followed suit.

sentences.zh: 及昏僻之君，乃有聖劉、天元之號。

translations.literal: When it came to benighted and perverse rulers, there were titles like Sagely Liu and Heavenly Prime.
translations.idiomatic: Only muddled rulers took titles such as 'Sagely Liu' or 'Heavenly Prime.'

sentences.zh: 是知人主輕重，不在自稱，崇其號無補於徽猷；

translations.literal: From this one knows that a ruler's weight lies not in what he calls himself; elevating his title does not aid his fine governance;
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's stature does not depend on what he calls himself; grand titles do nothing for good government;

sentences.zh: 損其名不傷其德美。

translations.literal: diminishing his title does not harm his virtue and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: and reducing one's title does not diminish one's virtue.

sentences.zh: 然而損之有謙光稽古之善，崇之獲矜能納諂之譏，得失不侔，居然可辨。

translations.literal: Yet to diminish it has the good of modest radiance and examining antiquity; to elevate it gains the reproach of pride, ability to accept flattery—the gain and loss are not equal; plainly they can be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Humility wins the praise of antiquity, while inflation invites the charge of pride and flattery—the difference is obvious.

sentences.zh: 況今時遭迍否，事屬傾危，尤宜懼思，以自貶抑。

translations.literal: Moreover, now the time meets obstruction and denial; affairs belong to tipping peril—you should especially fear and reflect, to humble yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in perilous times, you should all the more reflect in fear and humble yourself.

sentences.zh: 必也俯稽術數，須有變更。

translations.literal: If you must bow to examine numerology and fate, there must be change.
translations.idiomatic: If you must bow to divination and change something,

sentences.zh: 與其增美稱而失人心，不若黜舊號以祗天戒。

translations.literal: rather than increase glorious titles and lose men's hearts, better to dismiss the old title to respect Heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: better to strip away your old title and heed Heaven's warning than add flattering words and lose the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 天時人事，理必相符，人既好謙，天亦助順。

translations.literal: Heaven's seasons and human affairs—principle surely must correspond; if men already love modesty, Heaven also aids compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and humanity must align: when men love humility, Heaven aids those who yield.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能斷自宸鑒，煥發德音，引咎降名，深示刻責，惟謙與順，一舉而二美從之。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly can decide from the imperial mirror, issue radiant virtuous words, draw blame and lower your title, deeply show severe self-reproach—only modesty and compliance, one act and two beauties follow.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will decide from your own judgment, speak with moral clarity, confess fault, and lower your title—one act will win both humility and Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 」德宗從之，但改興元年號而已。

translations.literal: " Dezong followed this, changing only the reign title to Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: " Dezong accepted his advice and changed only the era name to Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，德宗倉皇出幸，府藏委棄，凝冽之際，士眾多寒，服禦之外，無尺縑丈帛。

translations.literal: At first, when Dezong fled in haste, treasury stores were abandoned; in freezing cold, soldiers and masses were mostly cold—apart from clothing for the person, not a foot of silk or a bolt of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong first fled in panic, the treasury was abandoned. In the bitter cold the troops had nothing beyond the clothes on their backs—not a scrap of silk or cloth.

sentences.zh: 及賊泚解圍，諸籓貢奉繼至，乃於奉天行在貯貢物於廊下，仍題曰「瓊林」、「大盈」二庫名。

translations.literal: When the bandit Ci lifted the siege, tribute from the various fiefs arrived in succession; then at the Fengtian traveling palace they stored tribute goods under the corridor, still labeling them with the two storehouse names "Qionglin" and "Daying."
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci lifted the siege, tribute from the provinces poured in. At the Fengtian palace the gifts were stored in the corridors under the labels "Qionglin" and "Daying"—the names of two private treasuries.

sentences.zh: 贄諫曰：

translations.literal: Zhi remonstrated:
translations.idiomatic: Zhi remonstrated:

sentences.zh: 「瓊林」、「大盈」，自古悉無其制，傳諸耆舊之說，皆云創自開元。

translations.literal: " 'Qionglin' and 'Daying'—from antiquity there was never such an institution; transmitted among elders' sayings, all say they were created from the Kaiyuan era."
translations.idiomatic: "The treasuries called Qionglin and Daying have no precedent in antiquity. Elders say they were created in the Kaiyuan reign."

sentences.zh: 貴臣貪權，飾巧求媚，乃言：「郡邑貢賦所用，盍各區分：賦稅當委於有司，以給經用；

translations.literal: Powerful ministers greedy for authority, adorning craft to seek favor, then said: "The uses of commandery and county tribute and levies—why not each be distinguished: taxes and levies should be entrusted to the regular offices to supply routine use;"
translations.idiomatic: Greedy courtiers, seeking favor with clever words, argued that local tribute should be split: taxes ought to go to the regular offices for state expenses,

sentences.zh: 貢獻宜歸於天子，以奉私求。

translations.literal: "tribute offerings should return to the Son of Heaven to supply private desires."
translations.idiomatic: while gifts should belong to the emperor for his private use.

sentences.zh: 」玄宗悅之。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong was pleased with this.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong was pleased.

sentences.zh: 新是二庫，蕩心侈欲，萌柢於茲，迨乎失邦，終以餌寇。

translations.literal: Newly establishing these two storehouses, dissolving the heart in extravagant desire—the sprouting root was here; when it reached losing the realm, in the end it was bait for bandits.
translations.idiomatic: These two treasuries fed extravagant desire from the start; in the end they helped bring down the dynasty and became booty for rebels.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「貨悖而入，必悖而出。

translations.literal: The Record says: "Wealth that enters perversely must exit perversely."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says, "Wealth gained unjustly is lost unjustly."

sentences.zh: 」豈其效歟！

translations.literal: " Is this not its effect!
translations.idiomatic: " Was that not exactly what happened!

sentences.zh: 陛下嗣位之初，務遵理道，敦行儉約，斥遠貪饕。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first succeeded to the throne, you strove to follow the Way of principle, earnestly practiced frugality, and repelled the greedy and gluttonous.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, you upheld right principle, practiced frugality, and kept the greedy at a distance.

sentences.zh: 雖內庫舊藏，未歸太府，而諸方曲獻，不入禁闈，清風肅然，海內丕變。

translations.literal: Although the inner treasury's old stores had not returned to the Grand Treasury, yet regional irregular offerings did not enter the forbidden quarters; pure wind was solemn, within the seas greatly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Although the inner treasury had not yet been merged with the public coffers, irregular gifts from the provinces no longer entered the palace, and the realm felt a refreshing change.

sentences.zh: 近以寇逆亂常，鑾輿外幸，既屬憂危之運，宜增儆勵之誠。

translations.literal: Recently because bandits and rebels disturbed the norm, the imperial carriage went abroad—in a time already of worry and peril, you should increase vigilant encouragement of sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Now rebellion has driven you into exile—a time of crisis when you should be all the more vigilant and sincere.

sentences.zh: 臣昨奉使軍營，出經行殿，忽睹右廓之下，榜列二庫之名，戄然若驚，不識所以。

translations.literal: Yesterday when your servant went on mission to the army camps and passed out through the traveling palace, I suddenly saw under the right corridor placards listing the two storehouses' names—startled as if in shock, not knowing the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, on my way to the army camps, I passed the traveling palace and suddenly saw placards under the right corridor naming those two treasuries. I was shocked and could not understand why.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 天衢尚梗，師旅方殷，痛心呻吟之聲，噢咻未息；

translations.literal: Heaven's highways are still obstructed, armies and hosts are just intense—the sounds of pained hearts and groaning, cries of suffering have not ceased;
translations.idiomatic: The roads are still blocked and the armies hard pressed; the wounded still groan;

sentences.zh: 忠勤戰守之效，賞賚未行。

translations.literal: the effects of loyal diligence in battle and defense—rewards and grants have not been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: those who fought loyally have yet to be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 諸道貢珍，遽私別庫，萬目所視，孰能忍情？

translations.literal: Tribute treasures from the various circuits are hastily made private in separate storehouses—ten thousand eyes are watching; who can bear it in feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Yet tribute from every circuit is set aside for private treasuries before ten thousand watching eyes. Who can bear that?

sentences.zh: 竊揣軍情，或生觖望，或忿形謗讟，或醜肆謳謠，頗含思亂之情，亦有悔忠之意。

translations.literal: Your servant privately gauges army sentiment: some may breed discontent, some show resentment in slander, some shamelessly spread songs and ballads—quite containing thoughts of disorder, also having mind to regret loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the troops may grow resentful, voice slander, or sing mocking songs—some already incline toward mutiny, others regret their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 是知氓俗昏鄙，識昧高卑，不可以尊極臨，而可以誠義感。

translations.literal: From this one knows that common folk custom is benighted and base, their knowledge dim to high and low—you cannot use supreme exaltation to face them down, but can move them with sincere righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Common soldiers are simple and cannot be ruled by lofty display alone; they respond to sincerity and justice.

sentences.zh: 頃者六師初降，百物無儲，外扞兇徒，內防危堞，晝夜不息，殆將五旬。

translations.literal: Recently when the six armies first came down, a hundred things had no stores; outwardly they repelled fierce villains, inwardly they defended perilous ramparts—day and night without rest, nearly fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial armies first reached Fengtian, supplies were empty. They fought the rebels outside and held the walls within, day and night, for nearly fifty days.

sentences.zh: 凍餓交侵，死傷相枕，畢命同力，竟夷大艱。

translations.literal: Cold and hunger together invaded; dead and wounded lay pillow to pillow; they exhausted life with united strength and finally leveled the great hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Cold and hunger ravaged them; the dead and wounded lay piled together. They gave their all and at last overcame the crisis.

sentences.zh: 良以陛下不厚其身，不私其欲，絕甘以同卒伍，輟食以啖功勞。

translations.literal: Truly because Your Majesty did not enrich his own person, did not privatize his desires, cut off sweetness to share with the ranks, stopped eating to feed the meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: This was because Your Majesty denied yourself, shared hardship with the ranks, and gave your own food to those who had earned merit.

sentences.zh: 無猛制人而不攜，懷所感也；

translations.literal: Without harsh control over men yet they did not desert—this was cherishing what moved them;
translations.idiomatic: You ruled without harshness yet none deserted you, because they felt your care;

sentences.zh: 無厚賞士而不怨，悉所無也。

translations.literal: without rich rewards for soldiers yet they did not resent—all because there was nothing to give.
translations.idiomatic: and though you could not reward them richly, they did not complain, because you had nothing to give.

sentences.zh: 今者攻圍已解，衣食已豐，而謗讟方興，軍情稍沮，豈不以勇夫常性，嗜貨矜功，其患難既與之同憂，而好樂不與之同利，茍異恬默，能無怨咨！

translations.literal: Now the siege assault is already lifted, clothing and food already abundant, yet slander rises, army sentiment somewhat discouraged—is it not because brave men's constant nature loves goods and prizes merit? They shared worry in hardship, yet in pleasure and profit do not share the benefit; if they differ and stay silent, how can there be no resentment and complaint!
translations.idiomatic: Now the siege is lifted and supplies plentiful, yet grumbling spreads and morale falters. Brave men love reward and prize their deeds: they shared your hardship, but when fortune returns they do not share the gain. How could they not murmur in discontent?

sentences.zh: 此理之常，故不足怪。

translations.literal: This is the constant of principle; thus it is not enough to wonder at.
translations.idiomatic: This is only human nature and nothing to wonder at.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「財散則民聚。

translations.literal: The Record says: "When wealth is scattered, the people gather."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says, "When wealth is dispersed, the people gather."

sentences.zh: 」豈其效歟！

translations.literal: " Is this not its effect!
translations.idiomatic: " Will that not prove true again!

sentences.zh: 陛下天資英聖，見善必遷，是將化蓄怨為銜恩，反過差為至當，促殄遺寇，永垂鴻名，大聖應機，固當不俟終日。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's Heaven-endowed nature is heroic and sagely; seeing good you surely turn—this will transform stored resentment into cherishing grace, reverse excess into utmost fitness, hasten extermination of remaining bandits, forever leave great fame; the great sage responding to opportunity surely should not wait for the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is wise and quick to amend wrongs. You can turn stored resentment into gratitude, correct this mistake at once, destroy the remaining rebels, and win lasting renown. A sage acts when the moment demands—surely you need not wait even a day.

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之，令去其題署。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this, ordering the placards removed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and ordered the placards removed.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，李懷光異志已萌，欲激怒諸軍，上表論諸軍衣糧薄，神策衣糧厚，厚薄不均，難以驅戰，意在撓沮進軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, Li Huai'guang's divergent intent had already sprouted; wishing to enrage the various armies, he submitted a memorial discussing how the various armies' clothing and grain were thin while the Shence Army's clothing and grain were thick—uneven thick and thin, hard to drive into battle—his intent was to thwart and discourage the advance of the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan, Li Huai'guang already harbored rebellious intent. He memorialized that the other armies received thin rations while the Shence troops were well supplied, claiming such inequality made campaigning impossible—his aim was to stall the advance.

sentences.zh: 李晟密奏，恐其有變，上憂之，遣贄使懷光軍宣諭。

translations.literal: Li Sheng secretly memorialized, fearing he would have a change; the emperor was worried and sent Zhi to Huai'guang's army to proclaim and reassure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng secretly warned that Huai'guang might rebel. The emperor, alarmed, sent Zhi to announce the court's will to Huai'guang's camp.

sentences.zh: 使還，贄奏事曰：

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, Zhi memorialized on the matter:
translations.idiomatic: On his return Zhi reported:

sentences.zh: 賊泚稽誅，保聚宮苑，勢窮援絕，引日偷生。

translations.literal: The bandit Ci awaits execution, holding and gathering in the palace parks; his momentum exhausted, aid cut off, he prolongs days to steal life.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Zhu Ci awaits punishment, holed up in the palace grounds, his strength spent and aid gone, clinging to life day by day.

sentences.zh: 懷光總仗順之軍，乘制勝之氣，鼓行芟翦，易若摧枯。

translations.literal: Huai'guang commands armies that rely on righteousness, rides the momentum of assured victory—drumming advance to mow and cut would be easy as crushing dry wood.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang commands the loyal armies and holds the advantage; a forward march would cut Zhu Ci down as easily as breaking dry wood.

sentences.zh: 而乃寇奔不追，師老不用，諸帥每欲進取，懷光輒沮其謀。

translations.literal: Yet he does not pursue when the bandit flees; the army grows old without being used; whenever the various commanders wish to advance, Huai'guang always thwarts their plans.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he will not pursue the fleeing enemy, keeps the army idle, and whenever other commanders wish to advance, Huai'guang blocks them.

sentences.zh: 據茲事情，殊不可解。

translations.literal: According to these circumstances, it is especially incomprehensible.
translations.idiomatic: On these facts his conduct is utterly inexplicable.

sentences.zh: 陛下意在全護，委曲聽從，觀其所為，亦未知感。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's intent is to preserve and protect him, yielding and following in every turn; observing his conduct, one also does not know that he feels gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has sought to protect him and indulged his wishes, yet he shows no gratitude.

sentences.zh: 若不別為規略，漸相制持，唯以姑息求安，終恐變故難測。

translations.literal: If you do not separately devise strategy and gradually restrain each other, seeking peace only through indulgence, in the end I fear unforeseen change will be hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Unless you adopt another strategy and begin to restrain him, seeking peace through indulgence alone will end in unpredictable disaster.

sentences.zh: 此誠事機危迫之秋也，故不可以尋常容易處之。

translations.literal: This is truly the season when opportunity is perilous and pressing; thus one cannot treat it in ordinary easy fashion.
translations.idiomatic: This is a moment of urgent crisis and cannot be handled as an ordinary matter.

sentences.zh: 今李晟奏請移軍，適遇臣銜命宣慰，懷光偶論此事，臣遂泛問所宜，懷光乃云：「李晟既欲別行，某亦都不要藉。

translations.literal: Now Li Sheng memorialized requesting to move the army; it happened to meet your servant bearing orders to proclaim comfort. Huai'guang chanced to discuss this matter; your servant then broadly asked what was fitting. Huai'guang then said: "Since Li Sheng wishes to march separately, I also need none of his support."
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng has asked to move his army. On my mission I happened to hear Huai'guang mention it, and I asked what he thought. He said, "If Li Sheng wants to march separately, I need none of his help."

sentences.zh: 」臣猶慮有翻覆，因美其軍強盛。

translations.literal: " Your servant still feared he might reverse himself, and therefore praised his army's strength and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: " Still fearing he might change his mind, I praised the strength of his troops.

sentences.zh: 懷光大自矜誇，轉有輕晟之意。

translations.literal: Huai'guang greatly prided and boasted himself, turning to have mind to slight Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang swelled with pride and showed contempt for Li Sheng.

sentences.zh: 臣又從容問云：「昨發離行在之日，未知有此商量；

translations.literal: Your servant again calmly asked: "When I set out leaving the traveling palace yesterday, I did not know of this consultation;"
translations.idiomatic: I then asked calmly, "When I left the palace yesterday this move had not been discussed;

sentences.zh: 今日從此卻回，或恐聖旨顧問，事之可否，決定何如？

translations.literal: "today returning from here, I fear the sacred edict may inquire—whether the matter can be done or not, how is it decided?"
translations.idiomatic: on my return His Majesty may ask whether this is approved. What is your decision?"

sentences.zh: 」懷光已肆輕言，不可中變，遂云：「恩命許去，事亦無妨。

translations.literal: " Huai'guang had already spoken lightly and could not change midway; he then said: "If gracious command permits him to go, the matter also has no harm."
translations.idiomatic: " Having spoken rashly, he could not take it back, and said, "If the Emperor permits it, there is no harm."

sentences.zh: 」要約再三，非不詳審，雖欲追悔，固難為詞。

translations.literal: " The agreement was made again and again, not without careful examination; though he might wish to regret and pursue, it would be hard to find words.
translations.idiomatic: " He repeated his assent clearly; even if he regrets it now, he cannot easily withdraw.

sentences.zh: 伏望即以李晟表出付中書，敕下依奏，別賜懷光手詔，示以移軍事由。

translations.literal: Your servant bows hope that you immediately take Li Sheng's memorial out and deliver it to the Secretariat, issue edict down according to the memorial, separately bestow on Huai'guang a handwritten edict showing the reasons for moving the army.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to send Li Sheng's memorial to the Secretariat, approve the move by edict, and separately send Huai'guang a handwritten edict explaining the transfer.

sentences.zh: 其手詔大意云：「昨得李晟奏，請移軍城東以分賊勢。

translations.literal: The handwritten edict's main meaning would say: "Yesterday we received Li Sheng's memorial requesting to move the army east of the city to divide the bandits' momentum."
translations.idiomatic: The edict might read: "Yesterday Li Sheng memorialized asking to move his army east of the city to divide the rebel force."

sentences.zh: 朕緣未知利害，本欲委卿商量，適會陸贄從彼宣慰回，雲見卿論敘軍情，語及於此，仍言許去，事亦無妨，遂敕本軍允其所請。

translations.literal: We because we did not yet know benefit and harm originally wished to entrust you with consultation; it happened that Lu Zhi returned from proclaiming comfort there, saying he saw you discuss army sentiment, words reaching this, still saying permission to go—the matter also has no harm—thereupon we ordered your army to grant his request.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing the pros and cons, I meant to consult you. Lu Zhi has just returned from your camp and reports that in discussing the army you agreed the move would do no harm. I have therefore ordered Li Sheng's request granted."

sentences.zh: 卿宜授以謀略，分路夾攻，務使葉齊，克平寇孽。

translations.literal: You should grant him strategy, divide routes for pincer attack, strive to make leaves fall together, conquer and level the bandit brood.
translations.idiomatic: Give him your plan, attack from two sides, and together destroy the rebels."

sentences.zh: 」如此詞婉而直，理當而明，雖蓄異端，何由起怨？

translations.literal: " Thus the words would be gentle yet direct, principle fitting yet clear—even if he harbors divergent intent, how could resentment arise?
translations.idiomatic: " Such wording would be courteous yet firm; even if he harbors ill will, how could he complain?

sentences.zh: 臣初奉使諭旨，本緣糧料不均，偶屬移軍，事相諧會。

translations.literal: Your servant at first received mission to proclaim the edict, originally because of uneven grain supplies; it happened to coincide with moving the army—the matters harmoniously met.
translations.idiomatic: My mission was originally about unequal rations; the question of moving troops arose by chance and fell out favorably.

sentences.zh: 又幸懷光詭對，且無阻絕之言，機宜合並。

translations.literal: Moreover it was fortunate Huai'guang answered craftily and had no words of obstruction—the opportune moment combined.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately Huai'guang answered evasively and did not refuse outright—the opportunity aligns.

sentences.zh: 若有幽贊，一失其便，後何可追，幸垂裁察！

translations.literal: If there is hidden assistance, one loss of this opportunity—afterward how can it be pursued? I beg you to let fall judgment and examination!
translations.idiomatic: With Heaven's hidden aid, if we miss this chance it cannot be recovered. I beg Your Majesty to decide at once!

sentences.zh: 德宗初望懷光回意破賊，故晟屢奏移軍不許；

translations.literal: At first Dezong hoped Huai'guang would turn his mind and destroy the bandits; therefore when Sheng repeatedly memorialized to move the army, it was not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: At first Dezong hoped Huai'guang would repent and destroy the rebels, so he had repeatedly refused Li Sheng's request to move;

sentences.zh: 及贄縷陳懷光反狀，乃可晟之奏，遂移軍東渭橋。

translations.literal: when Zhi in detail set forth Huai'guang's rebellious signs, then he approved Sheng's memorial; thereupon the army moved to East Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: but after Zhi detailed Huai'guang's rebellious conduct, he approved Li Sheng's memorial, and the army moved to East Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 而鄜坊節度李建徽、神策行營陽惠元猶在咸陽，贄慮懷光並建徽等軍，又奏曰：

translations.literal: But Fufang military commissioner Li Jianhui and Shence mobile camp commander Yang Huiyuan were still at Xianyang; Zhi feared Huai'guang would annex Jianhui's army and the others, and memorialized again, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Li Jianhui, military commissioner of Fufang, and Yang Huiyuan of the Shence mobile camp were still at Xianyang. Fearing that Huai'guang would absorb Jianhui's forces and the others, Lu Zhi submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 懷光當管師徒，足以獨制兇寇，逗留未進，抑有他由。

translations.literal: Huai'guang was in charge of the army and was sufficient alone to suppress the vicious bandits; his delay in advancing perhaps had another cause.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang commanded sufficient forces to subdue the rebels on his own; if he lingered without advancing, there must have been some other reason.

sentences.zh: 所患太強，不資傍助。

translations.literal: What was feared was that he was too strong and did not need assistance from others.
translations.idiomatic: The concern was that he was too powerful to need outside help.

sentences.zh: 比者又遣李晟、李建徽、陽惠元三節度之眾附麗其營，無益成功，只憂生事。

translations.literal: Recently the troops of the three military commissioners Li Sheng, Li Jianhui, and Yang Huiyuan were again sent to attach to his camp; this would not help success but only breed trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court had recently sent the three commissioners Li Sheng, Li Jianhui, and Yang Huiyuan to camp alongside him. That would not aid victory; it would only create new problems.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 四軍懸壘，群帥異心，論勢力則懸絕高卑，據職名則不相統屬。

translations.literal: Four armies stood in separate camps; the commanders had differing hearts. In strength they were far apart in rank; by official title none was subordinate to the others.
translations.idiomatic: Four armies were encamped apart, and their commanders were divided in mind. In strength they stood far apart in rank; in title none was subordinate to the others.

sentences.zh: 懷光輕晟等兵微位下，而忿其制不從心。

translations.literal: Huai'guang looked down on Sheng and the others for their small troops and low rank, and resented that he could not fully control them.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang despised Sheng and the others for their weaker forces and lower rank, and resented that he could not fully command them.

sentences.zh: 晟等疑懷光養寇蓄奸，而怨其事多陵己。

translations.literal: Sheng and the others suspected Huai'guang of harboring bandits and storing treachery, and resented that his actions often overrode themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and his colleagues suspected Huai'guang of deliberately sheltering the enemy and nursing treachery, and resented his repeated encroachments on their authority.

sentences.zh: 端居則互防飛謗，欲戰則遞恐分功，齟齬不和，嫌釁遂構，俾之同處，必不兩全。

translations.literal: At rest they mutually guarded against slander; wishing to fight they each feared sharing merit. Discord and disharmony arose, suspicion and friction were built up; if made to dwell together, they would surely not both survive intact.
translations.idiomatic: In camp they would watch each other and whisper accusations; in battle each would fear the others would share the credit. Friction bred suspicion, and if forced to remain together, neither side could come out intact.

sentences.zh: 強者惡積而後亡，弱者勢危而先覆，覆亡之禍，翹足可期。

translations.literal: The strong would accumulate hatred and afterward perish; the weak, their situation perilous, would first be overthrown. The calamity of overthrow and destruction could be awaited with foot lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The stronger party would accumulate enmity and eventually be destroyed; the weaker would fall first in their precarious position. Disaster could be expected at any moment.

sentences.zh: 舊寇未平，新患方起，憂嘆所切，實堪疚心。

translations.literal: The old bandits were not yet subdued; new troubles were just arising. The worry and sighing that cut deep were truly enough to afflict the heart.
translations.idiomatic: The old enemy was not yet subdued, and a new threat was rising—an anxiety that truly wrung the heart.

sentences.zh: 太上消慝於未萌，其次救失於始兆，況乎事情已露，禍難垂成，委而不謀，何以制亂？

translations.literal: The highest removes misdeeds before they sprout; next is to remedy loss at the first sign. How much more when the matter is already exposed and calamity is about to be complete—if one entrusts and does not plan, how can one control disorder?
translations.idiomatic: The best course is to dispel evil before it takes root; the next is to correct a fault at the first warning. When the danger is already visible and disaster near at hand, how can we fail to act and still expect to master the turmoil?

sentences.zh: 李晟見機慮變，先請移軍就東，建徽、惠元，勢轉孤弱，為其吞噬，理在必然。

translations.literal: Li Sheng, seeing the opportunity and considering change, first requested to move the army eastward. Jianhui and Huiyuan, their power turning isolated and weak, would be swallowed by him—in principle this was inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng, reading the situation, had already asked to move east. Once isolated, Jianhui and Huiyuan would inevitably be absorbed by Huai'guang.

sentences.zh: 他日雖有良圖，亦恐不能自拔，拯其危急，唯在此時。

translations.literal: Another day, even if there were a good plan, one would still fear being unable to extricate oneself. To rescue their urgent peril, only at this time.
translations.idiomatic: Even later a good plan might come too late to save them. Only now can their danger be averted.

sentences.zh: 今因李晟願行，便遣合軍同往，托言晟兵素少，慮為賊泚所邀，藉此兩軍，叠為掎角。

translations.literal: Now, taking advantage of Li Sheng's wish to go, send the united armies together, using the pretext that Sheng's troops have always been few and fearing interception by the rebel Zhu Ci, borrow these two armies, mutually layered as pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Take Li Sheng's willingness to move as pretext, and order Jianhui and Huiyuan to march with him, claiming that Sheng's forces are too small and might be cut off by Zhu Ci, so that the two armies could support each other as pincers.

sentences.zh: 仍先諭旨，密使促裝，詔書至營，即日進路。

translations.literal: Moreover, first convey the imperial intent and secretly have them hasten preparations; when the edict reaches camp, that very day they set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor should first send secret orders to prepare for departure, so that when the edict reaches camp the armies march the same day.

sentences.zh: 懷光意雖不欲，然亦計無所施。

translations.literal: Huai'guang in mind though unwilling, yet also had no stratagem to apply.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang would dislike it, but he would have no way to prevent it.

sentences.zh: 是謂先人有奪人之心，疾雷不及掩耳者也。

translations.literal: This is what is called having seized the initiative before others, and thunder too swift for hands to cover ears.
translations.idiomatic: That would be to strike first, like thunder before one can cover one's ears.

sentences.zh: 夫制軍馭將，所貴見情，離合疾徐，各有宜適。

translations.literal: In controlling armies and driving generals, what is prized is discerning sentiment; separating and joining, fast and slow, each has its suitable fit.
translations.idiomatic: In commanding armies and generals, one must read their disposition; when to unite, when to divide, when to hurry or delay—each has its proper time.

sentences.zh: 當離者合之則召亂，當合者離之則寡功；

translations.literal: Those who should be separated—uniting them summons disorder; those who should be united—separating them yields little achievement;
translations.idiomatic: Uniting those who should be kept apart invites chaos; separating those who should fight together yields little success;

sentences.zh: 當疾而徐則失機，當徐而疾則漏策。

translations.literal: When one should be swift but is slow, one loses opportunity; when one should be slow but is swift, one misses the plan.
translations.idiomatic: acting too slowly when speed is needed loses opportunity; acting too hastily when deliberation is needed spoils the plan.

sentences.zh: 得其要，契其時，然後舉無敗謀，措無危勢。

translations.literal: Obtaining the essential and matching the time—then one's moves have no failing plans, and one's dispositions have no dangerous situations.
translations.idiomatic: Only by grasping the essentials and acting at the right moment can every move succeed without dangerous entanglements.

sentences.zh: 而今者屯兵而不肯為用，聚將而罔能葉心，自為鯨鯢，變在朝夕。

translations.literal: But now troops are encamped yet unwilling to be used; generals are gathered yet unable to unite hearts—they have made themselves great fish and whales; change is within morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Now troops are massed but refuse to serve, and generals gathered but unable to trust one another—they have become monsters in their own right, and revolt may come at any hour.

sentences.zh: 留之不足以相制，徒長歷階；

translations.literal: Keeping them is not enough to check each other, only vainly growing step by step;
translations.idiomatic: Keeping them together will not keep them in check; it will only let danger grow step by step;

sentences.zh: 析之各競於擅能，或成勛績。

translations.literal: Dividing them, each would compete in displaying ability, and perhaps achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: separating them would let each command independently and perhaps win merit.

sentences.zh: 事有必應，斷無可疑。

translations.literal: The matter has a necessary response; there is absolutely no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: This course must be taken; there can be no doubt.

sentences.zh: 德宗曰：「卿之所料極善。

translations.literal: Dezong said: "Your forecast is extremely good.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong said, "Your assessment is excellent.

sentences.zh: 然李晟移軍，懷光心已惆悵，若更遣建徽、惠元就東，則使得為詞。

translations.literal: However, Li Sheng moving the army—Huai'guang's heart was already melancholy; if again sending Jianhui and Huiyuan eastward, then one would give him grounds for complaint.
translations.idiomatic: But Li Sheng has already moved his army, and Huai'guang is already displeased. If we also send Jianhui and Huiyuan east, we would only give him a pretext.

sentences.zh: 且俟旬時。

translations.literal: Moreover wait a ten-day period.
translations.idiomatic: Let us wait a few more days.

sentences.zh: 」晟至東渭橋，不旬日，懷光果奪兩節度兵，建徽單騎遁而獲免，惠元中路被執，害之。

translations.literal: " When Sheng reached East Wei Bridge, within less than ten days Huai'guang indeed seized the two commissioners' troops; Jianhui fled alone on horse and escaped; Huiyuan was seized midway and killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Sheng reached East Wei Bridge; within ten days Huai'guang seized the forces of the two commissioners. Jianhui escaped alone on horseback; Huiyuan was captured en route and killed.

sentences.zh: 報至行在，人情大恐。

translations.literal: When the report reached the mobile court, people's feelings were greatly fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When news reached the imperial camp, panic spread.

sentences.zh: 翌日，移幸山南。

translations.literal: The next day, the emperor moved to Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Dezong fled to Shannan.

sentences.zh: 贄練達兵機，率如此類。

translations.literal: Zhi was well versed in military opportunity; generally it was like this sort of thing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi's grasp of military affairs was generally of this caliber.

sentences.zh: 二月，從幸梁州，轉諫議大夫，依前充學士。

translations.literal: In the second month, following on the journey of fortune to Liang Prefecture, he was transferred to Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee, continuing as before to serve as academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he accompanied the emperor to Liang Prefecture, was promoted to remonstrance and discussion grandee, and continued as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 先是，鳳翔衙將李楚琳乘涇師之亂，殺節度使張鎰，歸款硃泚。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fengxiang garrison officer Li Chulin, taking advantage of the disorder of the Jingzhou army, killed military commissioner Zhang Yin and submitted allegiance to Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fengxiang garrison officer Li Chulin had taken advantage of the mutiny of the Jingzhou forces to kill Zhang Yin, military commissioner of Fengxiang, and submit to Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 及奉天解圍，楚琳遣使貢奉，時方艱阻，不獲已，命為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: When the siege of Fengtian was lifted, Chulin sent envoys with tribute; the times were hardship and obstruction, with no choice, and he was appointed Fengxiang military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege of Fengtian was lifted, Chulin sent envoys with tribute. Because the court was in dire straits, it had no choice but to appoint him military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 然德宗忿其弒逆，心不能容，才至漢中，欲令渾瑊代為節度。

translations.literal: Yet Dezong resented his regicide and could not tolerate it in his heart; just as he reached Hanzhong, he wished to have Hun Jian replace him as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong, however, could not forgive Chulin for murdering his commander. As soon as he reached Hanzhong, he wanted Hun Jian to replace him as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 贄諫曰：「楚琳之罪，固不容誅，但以乘輿未復，大憝猶存，勤王之師，悉在畿內，急宣速告，晷刻是爭。

translations.literal: Zhi remonstrated, saying: "Chulin's crime indeed cannot escape punishment, but the imperial carriage is not yet restored, the great enemy still exists, and the armies that came to aid the king are all within the capital region—urgent proclamations and swift reports are contested by the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi remonstrated: "Chulin's crime surely deserves death, but the Emperor has not yet returned to the capital, the chief rebel still lives, and the armies that rallied to the throne are all still in the vicinity. Every moment counts for urgent dispatches.

sentences.zh: 商嶺則道迂且遙，駱谷復為賊所扼，僅通王命，唯在褒斜，此路若又阻艱，南北便成隔絕。

translations.literal: The Shangling route is circuitous and distant; Luogu is again blocked by bandits. Only for imperial commands to pass is Baoxie—if this road too is obstructed, north and south become severed.
translations.idiomatic: The Shangling road is long and roundabout, and Luogu is again held by the enemy. Baoxie is the only route by which imperial orders can pass. If that too is blocked, north and south will be cut off from each other.

sentences.zh: 以諸鎮危疑之勢，居二逆誘脅之中，恟々群情，各懷向背。

translations.literal: Given the various garrisons' perilous and doubtful position, placed between the two rebels' enticement and coercion, the clamorous crowd sentiments each harbor inclination to turn.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commands are wavering, caught between two rebel powers that tempt and threaten them. Public sentiment is unsettled, and loyalties are divided.

sentences.zh: 賊勝則往，我勝則來，其間事機，不容差跌。

translations.literal: When the bandits win they go to them; when we win they come to us—the affairs between allow no slip.
translations.idiomatic: They side with whoever wins. At such a moment there is no room for error.

sentences.zh: 儻楚琳發憾，公肆猖狂，南塞要沖，東延巨猾，則我咽喉梗而心膂分矣，其勢豈不病哉！

translations.literal: If Chulin releases resentment and openly runs wild, blocking the vital pass in the south and extending east to the great villain, then our throat is blocked and heart and backbone divided—would the situation not be afflicted!
translations.idiomatic: If Chulin takes offense and rebels openly, he will block the southern gateway and link up with the great rebel in the east. Our lifeline will be choked and our forces split—is that not a grave peril?

sentences.zh: 」上釋然開悟，乃善待楚琳使，優詔安慰其心。

translations.literal: " The emperor suddenly became enlightened, then treated Chulin's envoys well and issued a gracious edict to comfort his heart.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor saw the point and treated Chulin's envoys kindly, sending a reassuring edict to mollify him.

sentences.zh: 德宗至梁，欲以谷口已北從臣賜號曰「奉天定難功臣」，谷口已南隨扈者曰「元從功臣」，不選朝官，一例俱賜。

translations.literal: When Dezong reached Liang, he wished to give those who followed north of Gukou the title "Meritorious Officials Who Pacified Difficulty at Fengtian," and those who escorted south of Gukou the title "Original Follow Meritorious Officials," not selecting court officials but giving to all in one category.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong reached Liang, he proposed to grant the title "Meritorious Officials Who Pacified the Crisis at Fengtian" to followers north of Gukou, and "Original Follow Meritorious Officials" to those south of Gukou, without distinguishing court officials—all would receive the honor alike.

sentences.zh: 贄奏曰：「破賊扞難，武臣之效。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized, saying: "Breaking bandits and defending against difficulty are the achievements of military officers.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi memorialized: "Defeating rebels and bearing hardship are the deeds of military men.

sentences.zh: 至如宮闈近侍，班列員僚，但馳走從行而已，忽與介胄奮命之士，俱號功臣，伏恐武臣憤惋。

translations.literal: As for palace attendants and ranked officials, they merely ran along on the journey; suddenly to be called meritorious officials together with armored warriors risking their lives—I fear the military officers will be indignant.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants and civil officials merely followed on the march. To call them meritorious officials alongside armored warriors who risked their lives would surely anger the military.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Then he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Dezong dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 李晟既收京城，遣中使宣付翰林院具錄先散失宮人名字，令草詔賜渾瑊，遣於奉天尋訪，以得為限，仍量與資糧送赴行在。

translations.literal: After Li Sheng recovered the capital, he sent a palace envoy to announce to the Hanlin Academy to record the names of palace women previously scattered and lost, ordered a draft edict for Hun Jian, and sent him to Fengtian to search and retrieve them, finding them as the limit, also providing rations to send them to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Sheng recovered the capital, he sent an imperial envoy to the Hanlin Academy with orders to compile a list of palace women lost in the chaos, draft an edict for Hun Jian, and dispatch him to Fengtian to search for them and send any found, with supplies, to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 贄不時奉詔，進狀論之曰：

translations.literal: Zhi did not promptly obey the edict and submitted a memorial discussing it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi did not immediately comply. Instead he submitted a memorial arguing against the order:

sentences.zh: 頃以理道乖錯，禍亂薦鐘，陛下思咎懼災，裕人罪己，屢降大號，誓將更新。

translations.literal: Recently because the Way and principle were at odds, calamity and disorder repeatedly struck; Your Majesty reflected on guilt and feared disaster, was lenient toward people and blamed himself, repeatedly issued great proclamations, and vowed to renew.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago, because governance had gone astray, calamity piled upon calamity. Your Majesty reflected on your faults, showed mercy to the people, and took blame upon yourself, issuing great proclamations again and again and vowing a new beginning.

sentences.zh: 天下之人，垂涕相賀，懲忿釋怨，煦仁戴明，畢力同心，共平多難。

translations.literal: People throughout the realm wept tears and congratulated one another, checked anger and released resentment, warmed by benevolence and bearing enlightenment, exerting strength with one heart, together pacifying many difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: People across the realm wept with joy, set aside old grievances, and warmed to your benevolence and wisdom, joining with one heart to overcome the crisis.

sentences.zh: 止土崩於絕岸，收版蕩於橫流，殄寇清都，不失舊物。

translations.literal: Stopping earth collapse at the sheer cliff, gathering the overturned board on the crosscurrent, exterminating bandits and clearing the capital, not losing the old possessions.
translations.idiomatic: You halted the empire's collapse at the brink, gathered the realm from the flood, destroyed the rebels, and recovered the capital without losing the dynasty's heritage.

sentences.zh: 實由陛下至誠動於天地，深悔感於神人，故得百靈降康，兆庶歸德。

translations.literal: Truly it was because Your Majesty's utmost sincerity moved Heaven and Earth, deep repentance moved spirits and men—therefore the hundred spirits descended with peace and the myriad people returned in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: This was truly because Your Majesty's sincerity moved Heaven and Earth and your deep repentance touched gods and men, so that all spirits brought peace and the people returned to loyalty.

sentences.zh: 茍不如此，自古何嘗有捐棄宮闕，失守宗祧，繼逆於赴難之師，再遷於蒙塵之日，不逾半歲，而復興大業者乎！

translations.literal: If it had not been thus, since ancient times when was there one who abandoned the palace, lost the ancestral temple, followed the army going to difficulty, moved twice on days of dust on the robe, and within half a year restored the great enterprise?
translations.idiomatic: Had it not been so, when in all history has an emperor who abandoned his palace, lost his ancestral shrines, fled with the army in crisis, and moved his court twice in disgrace restored the dynasty in less than half a year?

sentences.zh: 今渠魁始平，法駕將返，近自郊甸，遠周寰瀛，百役疲瘵之氓，重戰傷殘之卒，皆忍死扶病，傾耳聳肩，想聞德聲，翹望聖澤。

translations.literal: Now the ringleader is just pacified, the imperial carriage is about to return; from the near suburbs to the far reaches of the realm, the myriad laborers weary and afflicted, the heavily wounded soldiers from repeated battles—all endure death and support illness, prick up ears and raise shoulders, longing to hear virtuous sound and crane their necks for sage grace.
translations.idiomatic: Now the chief rebel has just been subdued and the imperial procession is about to return. From the capital suburbs to the farthest provinces, exhausted commoners and battle-worn soldiers—all who have endured death and sickness strain to hear your virtuous rule and await your benevolent care.

sentences.zh: 陛下固當感上天悔禍之眷，荷列祖垂裕之休，念將士鋒刃之殃，湣黎元塗炭之酷。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should indeed feel Heaven's favor in repenting of calamity, bear the ancestors' overflowing blessing, think of the soldiers' blade calamity, and pity the people's charcoal torment.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should be grateful for Heaven's mercy in turning aside disaster, mindful of the blessings left by your ancestors, considerate of the soldiers' wounds, and compassionate toward the people's suffering.

sentences.zh: 以致寇為戒，以居上為危，以務理為憂，以復宮為急。

translations.literal: Take causing bandits as warning, taking occupying the heights as peril, taking striving for order as worry, and taking restoring the palace as urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Let the rebellion be a warning, high station a source of caution, good governance your chief concern, and the restoration of the palace your most urgent task.

sentences.zh: 損之又損，尚懼汰侈之易滋；

translations.literal: Reduce again and again, yet still fear that extravagance will easily grow;
translations.idiomatic: Even after repeated retrenchment, one must still guard against the return of luxury;

sentences.zh: 艱之惟艱，猶患戒慎之難久。

translations.literal: Treat hardship as hardship, yet still worry that vigilance will be hard to maintain long.
translations.idiomatic: even in hardship one must still fear that caution cannot long endure.

sentences.zh: 謀始盡善，克終已稀；

translations.literal: Planning the beginning with full goodness—completing the end is already rare;
translations.idiomatic: Many begin well; few finish well;

sentences.zh: 始而不謀，終則何有！

translations.literal: If one does not plan at the beginning, what will there be at the end!
translations.idiomatic: and if one does not plan from the start, what can one hope for at the end?

sentences.zh: 夫以內人為號，蓋是中壺末流。

translations.literal: Taking palace women as the call is roughly the lowest stream of the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Making palace women the first concern belongs to the least important affairs of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 天子之尊，富有宮掖，如此等輩，固繁有徒，但恐傷多，豈憂乏使！

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's honor—rich with palace attendants—such as these are indeed numerous; one only fears there are too many, how worry about lack of attendants!
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's household is already full of attendants; there are more than enough. The concern is having too many, not too few!

sentences.zh: 翦除元惡，曾未浹辰，奔賀往來，道途如織。

translations.literal: Cutting out the chief villain has not yet reached ten days; those rushing to congratulate come and go, the roads like weaving.
translations.idiomatic: The chief villain was eliminated less than ten days ago, and congratulatory traffic already fills the roads.

sentences.zh: 何必自虧君德，首訪婦人，又令資裝速赴行在！

translations.literal: Why must you yourself diminish sovereign virtue, first visiting women, and also order supplies to hurry to the mobile court!
translations.idiomatic: Why diminish your own moral authority by making women your first concern and ordering supplies to rush them to the imperial camp?

sentences.zh: 萬目閱視，眾口流傳，恐非所以答慶賴之心，副惟新之望也。

translations.literal: Ten thousand eyes viewing, myriad mouths spreading word—I fear this is not how to answer the heart of those who rely on celebration, nor fulfill the hope for renewal.
translations.idiomatic: With all eyes watching and all tongues wagging, I fear this will not answer the people's hopes for celebration nor fulfill their expectation of renewal.

sentences.zh: 夫事有先後，義有重輕，重者宜先，輕者宜後。

translations.literal: Affairs have precedence and sequence; righteousness has weight and lightness—the weighty should come first, the light should come after.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs have their order, and duties their priorities. The weighty should come first, the light afterward.

sentences.zh: 武王克殷，有未及下車而為之者，有下車而為之者，蓋美其不失先後之宜也。

translations.literal: When King Wu conquered Yin, there were matters he undertook before descending from the chariot and matters after descending—praising that he did not lose the fitness of before and after.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu conquered the Shang, some tasks he performed before even stepping down from his chariot and some afterward—because he honored the proper order of priorities.

sentences.zh: 自翠華播越，萬姓靡依，清廟震驚，三時乏祀，當今所務，莫大於斯。

translations.literal: Since the imperial splendor was driven abroad, the myriad people have no support; the clear temple was shaken, three seasons lacked sacrifice—what is to be done today is nothing greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Emperor was driven into exile, the people have been left adrift; the ancestral temple was shaken and sacrifices have been neglected for seasons. Nothing today is more urgent than this.

sentences.zh: 誠宜速遣大臣，馳傳先往，迎復神主，修整郊壇，展禋享之儀，申告謝之意。

translations.literal: Truly one should quickly dispatch great ministers, post-horses going first, to welcome and restore the spirit tablets, repair the suburban altars, unfold the rites of solemn offering, and declare the meaning of report and thanksgiving.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should swiftly send senior ministers ahead by relay to recover the spirit tablets, restore the suburban altars, perform the sacrificial rites, and offer thanks to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 然後吊恤死義，慰犒有功，綏輯黎蒸，優問耆耋。

translations.literal: Then mourn and comfort those who died for righteousness, comfort and reward those with merit, soothe and gather the people, and kindly inquire of the aged.
translations.idiomatic: Then mourn the loyal dead, reward the meritorious, reassure the people, and inquire after the elderly.

sentences.zh: 安定反側，寬宥脅從；

translations.literal: Stabilize those who turned, pardon those coerced to follow;
translations.idiomatic: Pacify those who wavered, pardon those forced into rebellion;

sentences.zh: 宣暢郁堙，褒獎忠直；

translations.literal: Proclaim and clear blocked grievances, praise and reward the loyal and upright;
translations.idiomatic: give voice to suppressed grievances, and honor the loyal and upright;

sentences.zh: 官失職之士，復廢業之人。

translations.literal: Officials who lost their posts, people who abandoned their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: restore officials displaced from office and people driven from their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 是皆宜先，不可後也。

translations.literal: These all should come first and cannot come after.
translations.idiomatic: All of these should come first—not last.

sentences.zh: 至如崇飾服器，繕緝殿臺，備耳目之娛，選巾櫛之侍，是皆宜後，不可先也。

translations.literal: As for adorning robes and vessels, repairing and stitching halls and terraces, preparing entertainment for eyes and ears, selecting towel-and-comb attendants—these all should come after and cannot come first.
translations.idiomatic: Adorning robes and vessels, repairing palaces, providing diversions for eyes and ears, and selecting personal attendants—all of these should come later, not first.

sentences.zh: 散失內人，已經累月，既當離亂之際，必為將士所私。

translations.literal: The scattered lost palace women have already been many months; being in the time of separation and disorder, they must have been privately taken by officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The lost palace women have been missing for months. In the chaos of rebellion, they were surely taken privately by officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其人若稍有知，不求當自陳獻；

translations.literal: If such persons have a little understanding, not seeking them they will of themselves declare and present;
translations.idiomatic: If they have any sense, they will come forward on their own without being searched for;

sentences.zh: 其人若甚無識，求之適使憂虞。

translations.literal: If such persons are very without understanding, seeking them will just cause worry and anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: if they lack understanding, searching for them will only create alarm.

sentences.zh: 自因寇亂喪亡，頗有大於此者，一聞搜索，懷懼必多；

translations.literal: Since because of bandit disorder there were losses, many greater than this—once search is heard, those harboring fear will surely be many;
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos many have suffered losses far greater than this. Once a search is announced, countless people will be afraid;

sentences.zh: 余孽尚繁，群情未一，因而善撫，猶恐危疑，若又懼之，於何不有！

translations.literal: Remaining evils are still numerous, crowd sentiment is not yet unified—even thus kindly soothing, one still fears doubt and suspicion; if again one makes them afraid, what would there not be!
translations.idiomatic: rebel remnants are still numerous and public sentiment is not yet settled. Even with gentle handling people remain uneasy; if you frighten them further, what mischief might follow?

sentences.zh: 昔人所以掩絕纓而飲盜馬者，豈必忘其情愛，蓋知為君之體然也。

translations.literal: The reason men of old covered the horse's bridle and let the horse thief drink was not necessarily forgetting their affection— they simply knew the body of being ruler is thus.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients who covered a loose bridle and let a thief drink from their horse did not forget their own property—they understood what it means to be a ruler.

sentences.zh: 以小妨大，明者不為。

translations.literal: Letting the small obstruct the great— the enlightened do not do it.
translations.idiomatic: The wise do not let small matters obstruct great ones.

sentences.zh: 天下固多褻人，何必獨在於此。

translations.literal: Under Heaven there are indeed many lowly persons— why must they be only among these?
translations.idiomatic: There are servants enough in the realm; why fix on these alone?

sentences.zh: 所令撰賜渾瑊詔書，未敢順旨。

translations.literal: Regarding the ordered drafting of the edict to grant Hun Jian, I dare not follow the intent.
translations.idiomatic: As for the edict you ordered me to draft for Hun Jian, I dare not comply.

sentences.zh: 帝遂不降詔，但遣使而已。

translations.literal: The emperor then did not issue the edict but only sent an envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued no edict and sent only an envoy.

sentences.zh: 德宗還京，轉中書舍人，學士如故。

translations.literal: When Dezong returned to the capital, Zhi was transferred to Secretariat drafter, academician as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong returned to the capital, Lu Zhi was promoted to secretariat drafter while remaining Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 初，贄受張鎰知，得居內職；

translations.literal: At first, Zhi received Zhang Yin's recognition and was able to hold an inner post;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi had originally owed his inner-court appointment to Zhang Yin's patronage;

sentences.zh: 及鎰為盧杞所排，贄常憂惴；

translations.literal: When Yin was pushed aside by Lu Qi, Zhi often worried and feared;
translations.idiomatic: when Yin was ousted by Lu Qi, Lu Zhi lived in constant anxiety;

sentences.zh: 及杞貶黜，始敢上書言事。

translations.literal: When Qi was demoted and removed, he then dared to submit memorials on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: only after Qi was demoted did he dare to speak openly on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 德宗好文，益深顧遇。

translations.literal: Dezong loved literature and treated him with even deeper regard.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong loved literary talent and favored him all the more.

sentences.zh: 奉天解圍後，德宗言及違離宗廟，嗚咽流涕曰：「致寇之由，實朕之過。

translations.literal: After the siege of Fengtian was lifted, Dezong spoke of being separated from the ancestral temple, sobbed with flowing tears, and said: "The cause of bringing bandits was truly my fault.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege of Fengtian was lifted, Dezong spoke of having been torn from the ancestral temple and wept, saying, "The rebellion was truly my fault.

sentences.zh: 」贄亦流涕而對曰：「臣思致今日之患者，群臣之罪也。

translations.literal: " Zhi also wept with flowing tears and replied, saying: "Your subject thinks that what brought today's affliction was the crime of the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Zhi wept in reply, "Your Majesty, I believe today's calamity was the fault of your ministers.

sentences.zh: 」贄意蓋為盧杞、趙贊等也。

translations.literal: " Zhi's meaning was roughly for Lu Qi, Zhao Zan, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Lu Qi, Zhao Zan, and others in mind.

sentences.zh: 上欲掩杞之失，則曰：「雖朕德薄，致茲禍亂，亦運數前定，事不由人。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to cover Qi's fault and then said: "Although my virtue is thin and brought this calamity and disorder, it was also fate predetermined beforehand—the affair was not due to men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, wishing to shield Qi, said, "Though my virtue was insufficient and brought this disaster, it was also predestined fate—not the work of men.

sentences.zh: 」贄又極言杞等罪狀，上雖貌從，心頗不說。

translations.literal: " Zhi again spoke to the utmost of Qi and the others' crimes; the emperor though outwardly assented, in heart was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Zhi again pressed the crimes of Qi and his allies. Dezong assented outwardly but was displeased at heart.

sentences.zh: 吳通微兄弟俱在翰林，亦承德宗寵遇，文章才器不迨贄；

translations.literal: The Wu brothers Tongwei were both in the Hanlin; they also received Dezong's favor—literary talent and ability did not reach Zhi;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tongwei and his brother, both in the Hanlin Academy, also enjoyed Dezong's favor, though their literary talent fell short of Lu Zhi's;

sentences.zh: 而能交結權幸，共短贄於上前。

translations.literal: Yet they were able to connect with powerful favorites and together speak ill of Zhi before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: but they cultivated ties with powerful favorites and together slandered Lu Zhi before the throne.

sentences.zh: 故劉從一、姜公輔自卑品蒼黃之中，皆登輔相；

translations.literal: Therefore Liu Congyi and Jiang Gongfu, from low rank amid the yellow dust, all ascended to chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Liu Congyi and Jiang Gongfu rose from humble stations to become chief ministers;

sentences.zh: 而贄為朋黨所擠，同職害其能，加以言事激切，動失上之歡心，故久之不為輔相。

translations.literal: But Zhi was squeezed by factional cliques, colleagues harmed by his ability, and moreover because remonstrating on affairs was sharp and urgent, often losing the emperor's favor—therefore for long he was not made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: while Lu Zhi was squeezed out by factions, envied by colleagues for his talent, and—because his remonstrances were sharp and often offended the emperor—for long was never made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 其於議論應對，明練理體，敷陳剖判，下筆如神，當時名流，無不推挹。

translations.literal: In discussion and response, he was clear and practiced in principles; setting forth and analyzing, his writing was like a god's — notables of the time, none did not admire and defer to him.
translations.idiomatic: In debate and reply he was lucid on principle, his expositions incisive, his pen seemingly inspired; every leading figure of the age admired him without exception.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，李抱真入朝，從容奏曰：「陛下幸奉天、山南時，赦書至山東，宣諭之時，士卒無不感泣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, Li Baozhen came to court and calmly memorialized, saying: "When Your Majesty was at Fengtian and Shannan, the amnesty edict reached Shandong; when it was proclaimed, the soldiers none failed to be moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era, Li Baozhen came to court and said calmly, "When Your Majesty was at Fengtian and in the south, the amnesty reached Shandong; as it was read aloud, not a soldier failed to weep.

sentences.zh: 臣即時見人情如此，知賊不足平也。」

translations.literal: Your subject at once saw the people's feelings thus and knew the rebels were not enough to be subdued."
translations.idiomatic: I saw the mood of the men at once and knew the rebels could never be crushed."

sentences.zh: 時贄母韋氏在江東，上遣中使迎至京師，搢紳榮之。

translations.literal: At the time Lu Zhi's mother, the Lady Wei, was in Jiangdong; the emperor sent palace envoys to welcome her to the capital — the gentry took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi's mother, Lady Wei, was then in the lower Yangzi region; the emperor sent palace envoys to bring her to the capital, an honor the court took as a mark of distinction.

sentences.zh: 俄丁母憂，東歸洛陽，寓居嵩山豐樂寺。

translations.literal: Soon he suffered his mother's bereavement, returned east to Luoyang, and lodged at Fengle Temple on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered mourning for his mother, went east to Luoyang, and took lodging at Fengle Temple on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 籓鎮賻贈及別陳餉遺，一無所取。

translations.literal: Condolence gifts from regional commanders and separate offerings — he took not one.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted none of the condolence gifts sent by the regional commanders, nor any other offerings pressed upon him.

sentences.zh: 與韋臯布衣時相善，唯西川致遺，奏而受之。

translations.literal: He had been on good terms with Wei Gao since commoner days; only from Xichuan did he receive gifts, after memorializing and being permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He had been close to Wei Gao since their days as commoners; only gifts from Xichuan did he accept, and then only after memorializing the throne and receiving permission.

sentences.zh: 贄父初葬蘇州，至是欲合葬。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi's father had first been buried in Suzhou; at this time he wished a joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi's father had first been buried in Suzhou; he now wished to reinter him beside his mother.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使護其柩車至洛，其禮遇如此。

translations.literal: The emperor sent palace envoys to escort the coffin carriage to Luoyang — such was the treatment he received.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent palace envoys to escort the coffin to Luoyang — such was the honor shown him.

sentences.zh: 免喪，權知兵部侍郎，依前充學士。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed acting Vice Minister of War and continued as before as Hanlin scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he was named acting Vice Minister of War while retaining his post as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 申謝日，贄伏地而泣，德宗為之改容敘慰。

translations.literal: On the day he presented thanks, Lu Zhi prostrated himself weeping; Dezong for his sake changed expression and spoke words of comfort.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he presented his thanks, Lu Zhi prostrated himself in tears; Dezong's face softened and he spoke words of consolation.

sentences.zh: 恩遇既隆，中外屬意為輔弼，而宰相竇參素忌贄，贄亦短參之所為，言參黷貨，由是與參不平。

translations.literal: Favor having grown great, inside and outside the court looked to him as chief minister — but the chief minister Dou Can had long envied Lu Zhi; Lu Zhi also spoke ill of Can's conduct, saying Can was venal, and thus they were at odds with Can.
translations.idiomatic: His favor now ran so high that court and country alike looked to him as a future chief minister; yet the chief minister Dou Can had long resented him, and Lu Zhi in turn denounced Can's conduct as corrupt — so the two were estranged.

sentences.zh: 七年，罷學士，正拜兵部侍郎，知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was dismissed from the Hanlin, formally appointed Vice Minister of War, and put in charge of the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he left the Hanlin Academy, was formally appointed Vice Minister of War, and given charge of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 時崔元翰、梁肅文藝冠時，贄輸心於肅。

translations.literal: At the time Cui Yuanhan and Liang Su led all in literary arts; Lu Zhi opened his heart to Liang Su.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanhan and Liang Su then stood at the head of the age in letters; Lu Zhi gave Liang Su his full trust.

sentences.zh: 肅與元翰推薦藝實之士，升第之日，雖眾望不愜，然一歲選士，才十四五，數年之內，居臺省清近者十余人。

translations.literal: Liang Su and Yuanhan recommended men of genuine talent; on the day degrees were announced, though popular expectation was not satisfied, yet in one year's selection of scholars there were only fourteen or fifteen; within a few years more than ten held posts in the Secretariat and Censorate close to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Su and Yuanhan put forward men of real ability; when the results were announced, public opinion was disappointed, for only fourteen or fifteen candidates passed that year — yet within a few years more than ten of them held prestigious posts in the Secretariat and Censorate.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，竇參得罪，以贄為中書侍郎、門下同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year Dou Can was punished; Lu Zhi was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year Dou Can fell from power, and Lu Zhi was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 贄久為邪黨所擠，困而得位，意在不負恩獎，悉心報國，以天下事為己任。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, long squeezed by wicked factions, having gained office through hardship, intended not to betray grace and reward, devoted his heart to serving the state, and took affairs under Heaven as his personal charge.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, long blocked by hostile factions, had won office only after great struggle; he meant to repay the emperor's favor, serve the realm with all his heart, and treat the affairs of the empire as his own burden.

sentences.zh: 上即位之初，用楊炎、盧杞秉政，樹立朋黨，排擯良善，卒致天下沸騰，鑾輿奔播。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the emperor's reign, Yang Yan and Lu Qi held power, established cliques, expelled the good, and ultimately caused the realm to seethe and the imperial carriage to flee in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his reign the emperor had entrusted power to Yang Yan and Lu Qi, who built factions, drove out the worthy, and in the end brought the realm to uproar and the court itself to flight.

sentences.zh: 懲是之失，貞元已後，雖立輔臣，至於小官除擬，上必再三詳問，久之方下。

translations.literal: Learning from this failure, after Zhenyuan even when appointing chief ministers, for the appointment of minor offices the emperor must inquire repeatedly in detail, and only after long delay would issue orders.
translations.idiomatic: Chastened by that disaster, Dezong after the Zhenyuan era would question even the appointment of minor officials again and again before an order finally issued.

sentences.zh: 及贄知政事，請許臺省長官自薦屬官，仍保任之，事有曠敗，兼坐舉主。

translations.literal: When Lu Zhi took charge of governance, he requested that heads of the Secretariat and Censorate be allowed to recommend their own subordinates and still guarantee them — if affairs failed through neglect, the recommender would share punishment.
