translations.idiomatic: Once Lu Zhi entered the government, he asked that heads of the Secretariat and Censorate be permitted to nominate their own subordinates under personal guarantee — if an appointee failed in office, the nominator would share the penalty.

sentences.zh: 上許之，俄又宣旨曰：「外議云：『諸司所舉，多引用親黨，兼通賂遺，不得實才。

translations.literal: The emperor assented; soon he also issued an edict saying: "Outside talk says: 'What the various offices recommend mostly draws on kin and cliques, also involving bribes — real talent is not obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; but soon he issued a new order: "There is talk abroad that the offices' nominees are mostly kin and cronies, that bribes pass hands, and that true talent is not found.

sentences.zh: 』此法行之非便，今後卿等宜自選擇，勿用諸司延薦。

translations.literal: This law in practice is inconvenient; hereafter you ministers should choose yourselves — do not use the various offices' extended recommendations.'"
translations.idiomatic: This policy will not do. Hereafter you ministers must choose for yourselves and not rely on nominations from the departments.'"

sentences.zh: 」贄論奏曰：

translations.literal: " Lu Zhi submitted a memorial arguing:
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Zhi memorialized in reply:

sentences.zh: 臣實頑鄙，一無所堪，猥蒙任使，待罪宰相。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly dull and base, capable of nothing, yet has undeservedly received appointment and awaits punishment as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and unworthy, fit for nothing, yet I have undeservedly been placed among the chief ministers, holding office in fear of failure.

sentences.zh: 雖懷竊位之懼，且乏知人之明，自揣庸虛，終難上報。

translations.literal: Though I harbor fear of usurping a place and moreover lack the clarity to know men, measuring my own mediocrity and emptiness, in the end I can hardly repay Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I fear I hold a post beyond my merit and lack the discernment to know men; knowing my own inadequacy, I can scarcely hope to repay Your Majesty's trust.

sentences.zh: 唯知廣求才之路，使賢者各以匯征；

translations.literal: I only know to broaden the path of seeking talent, so that the worthy may each be gathered in recruitment;
translations.idiomatic: All I know is to widen the roads by which talent may be found, so that the worthy may be summoned from every quarter;

sentences.zh: 啟至公之門，令職司皆得自達。

translations.literal: open the gate of utmost fairness, and let every office reach the throne by its own merit.
translations.idiomatic: and open the gates of impartial selection, so that every office may bring forward its own candidates.

sentences.zh: 既蒙允許，即宜宣行。

translations.literal: Having received Your Majesty's permission, it should at once be proclaimed and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already approved this policy; it ought now to be put into effect.

sentences.zh: 南宮舉人，才至十數，或非臺省舊吏，則是使府佐僚，累經薦延，多歷事任。

translations.literal: The candidates from the southern palace numbered only a dozen or so; some were former clerks of the Secretariat and Censorate, others aides in commissioner offices — repeatedly recommended and promoted, most had long experience in office.
translations.idiomatic: The examination candidates numbered scarcely a dozen; some were veterans of the Secretariat and Censorate, others staff of commissioner offices — all repeatedly promoted, all tested in real service.

sentences.zh: 論其資望，既不愧於班行；

translations.literal: Judging their qualifications and standing, they were not ashamed among their ranks;
translations.idiomatic: By rank and reputation they were unexceptionable among their peers;

sentences.zh: 考其行能，又未聞於闕敗。

translations.literal: examining their conduct and ability, nothing had been heard of failure or neglect.
translations.idiomatic: and in conduct and competence nothing had been heard against them.

sentences.zh: 遽以騰口，上煩聖聰，道之難行，亦可知矣！

translations.literal: Suddenly on loose tongues it reached Your Majesty's sacred hearing — that the Way is hard to carry out is also knowable!
translations.idiomatic: Yet on mere rumor alone Your Majesty's ear has been troubled — from this one may see how hard it is to put good policy into practice!

sentences.zh: 陛下勤求理道，務徇物情，因謂舉薦非宜，復委宰臣揀擇。

translations.literal: Your Majesty diligently seeks the Way of governance and strives to follow the people's feelings; therefore you say recommendation is unsuitable and again entrust selection to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty earnestly seeks good government and wishes to heed public sentiment; hearing that nomination was improper, you have again entrusted selection to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 其為崇任輔弼，博采輿詞，可謂聖德之盛者。

translations.literal: In honoring and trusting chief ministers and broadly gathering public opinion, this may be called the fullness of sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In honoring your ministers and heeding broad counsel, Your Majesty shows the greatness of a sage ruler.

sentences.zh: 然於委任責成之道，聽言考實之方，閑邪存誠，猶恐有闕。

translations.literal: Yet in the Way of entrusting office and demanding results, and in the method of hearing words and examining facts — guarding against evil and preserving sincerity — I still fear there are gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the matter of entrusting responsibility and holding men to account, of hearing counsel and testing its truth — in guarding against deceit and keeping faith with the upright — I fear something is still lacking.

sentences.zh: 陛下既納臣言而用之，旋聞橫議而止之，於臣謀不責成，於橫議不考實，此乃謀失者得以辭其罪，議曲者得以肆其誣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty having accepted my words and used them, then on hearing reckless talk stopped them — not demanding results from my plan, not examining facts in reckless talk — this allows those whose plans fail to excuse their guilt, and those whose talk is crooked to indulge their slander.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty accepted my proposal and then, on hearing reckless criticism, set it aside — holding my plan to no account while giving no scrutiny to the critics. Thus those whose counsel fails may excuse their failure, and the dishonest may slander at will.

sentences.zh: 率是而行，觸類而長，固無必定之計，亦無必實之言。

translations.literal: If this principle is followed and each kind grows by contact, there will naturally be no settled plan, nor words that must be true.
translations.idiomatic: If this pattern continues, category by category, there will be no firm policy and no word that can be trusted.

sentences.zh: 計不定則理道難成，言不實則小人得誌。

translations.literal: If plans are unsettled, the Way of governance is hard to accomplish; if words are untrue, petty men get their will.
translations.idiomatic: Without settled policy good government cannot be achieved; without truth in counsel petty men prevail.

sentences.zh: 國家之病，常必由之。

translations.literal: The state's afflictions constantly must come by this path.
translations.idiomatic: The afflictions of the state have again and again sprung from just such causes.

sentences.zh: 昔齊桓公問管仲害霸之事，對曰：「得賢不能任，害霸也；

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi asked Guan Zhong what harmed hegemony; he replied: "Obtaining the worthy but not being able to employ them harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: Once Duke Huan of Qi asked Guan Zhong what destroys hegemony. He answered, "To find worthy men and fail to use them destroys hegemony;

sentences.zh: 用而不能終，害霸也；

translations.literal: employing but not seeing them through to the end harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: to use them but not see the matter through destroys hegemony;

sentences.zh: 與賢人謀事，而與小人議之，害霸也。

translations.literal: consulting with worthy men on affairs but discussing them with petty men harms hegemony."
translations.idiomatic: to take counsel with worthy men and then debate it with petty men destroys hegemony."

sentences.zh: 」為小人者，不必悉懷險诐，故覆邦家。

translations.literal: " Those who are petty men need not all harbor treacherous deceit and therefore overturn state and family.
translations.idiomatic: " Petty men need not all be treacherous schemers bent on ruin;

sentences.zh: 蓋以其意性回邪，趣向狹促，以沮議為出眾，以自異為不群，趨近利而昧遠圖，效小信而傷大道，況又言行難保，恣其非心者乎！

translations.literal: It is rather that their disposition is crooked and perverse, their bent narrow and cramped — taking obstruction of counsel as standing out, taking being different as not joining the crowd, rushing toward near profit while blind to far-reaching plans, showing small trust while harming the great Way — how much more when words and conduct are hard to guarantee and they indulge their wrongful hearts!
translations.idiomatic: rather, their natures are twisted and cramped: they make obstruction their distinction, contrariness their pride; they grasp at immediate gain and lose sight of the larger design, offer petty proofs of loyalty and wound the greater good — and when words and deeds cannot be trusted, what limit is there to their malice?

sentences.zh: 伏以宰輔，常制不過數人，人之所知，固有限極，不有遍諳諸士，備閱群才。

translations.literal: I submit that chief ministers by regular rule are no more than a few persons; what men know naturally has limits — they cannot be thoroughly acquainted with all scholars or fully review all talent.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers are by custom only a few in number; human knowledge has its limits — no minister can know every candidate or review all talent himself.

sentences.zh: 若令悉命群官，理須展轉詢訪，是則變公舉為私薦，易明易攵為暗投。

translations.literal: If ordered to command all officials, they must by reason make roundabout inquiries — this then changes public recommendation into private nomination, and open selection into secret submission.
translations.idiomatic: If ministers must appoint every official themselves, they will necessarily rely on roundabout inquiry — turning open nomination into private favor and transparent selection into back-room dealing.

sentences.zh: 儻如議者之言，所舉多有情故，舉於君上，且未絕私；

translations.literal: If, as the critics say, what is recommended mostly involves personal ties, recommending to the sovereign still does not end favoritism;
translations.idiomatic: If, as the critics claim, nominations are tainted by personal ties, then even nomination to the throne has not eliminated private interest;

sentences.zh: 薦於宰臣，安肯無詐！

translations.literal: recommending to chief ministers — how could there be no fraud!
translations.idiomatic: and recommendation to a chief minister — how could fraud be absent!

sentences.zh: 失人之弊，必又甚焉。

translations.literal: The harm of losing the right men must be even greater.
translations.idiomatic: The harm of appointing the wrong men would be greater still.

sentences.zh: 所以承前命官，罕有不涉私謗，雖則秉鈞不一，或自行情，亦由私訪所親，轉為所賣。

translations.literal: Therefore in carrying out prior appointments of officials, rarely was there none involved in private slander; though those holding the scale were not uniform, some acting on personal inclination — this too came from privately inquiring of those close and being in turn sold by them.
translations.idiomatic: That is why past appointments have so often drawn charges of favoritism: though chief ministers differ in character and some act from private motive, the root cause is private inquiry among one's own circle — and being misled by those one trusts.

sentences.zh: 其弊非遠，聖鑒明知。

translations.literal: This harm is not distant — Your Majesty's sacred insight clearly knows it.
translations.idiomatic: This evil is no distant matter; Your Majesty's clear sight already knows it.

sentences.zh: 今又將徇浮言，專任宰臣除吏，宰臣不遍諳識，踵前須訪於人。

translations.literal: Now again you would follow floating words and exclusively entrust chief ministers to dismiss and appoint officials; chief ministers cannot be thoroughly acquainted with all — following precedent they must inquire of others.
translations.idiomatic: Now, yielding again to loose talk, you would leave all appointments to the chief ministers; unable to know every candidate, they must as before consult others.

sentences.zh: 若訪親朋，則是悔其覆車，不易故轍；

translations.literal: If they inquire of kin and friends, this is regretting the overturned cart but not changing the old track;
translations.idiomatic: If they consult kin and friends, you repeat the old mistake without changing course;

sentences.zh: 若訪於朝列，則是求其私薦，不如公舉之愈也。

translations.literal: if they inquire among the court ranks, this is seeking their private recommendations — not as good as public nomination.
translations.idiomatic: if they consult within the court, they seek private recommendations — which is worse than open nomination.

sentences.zh: 二者利害，惟陛下更詳擇焉。

translations.literal: Of the two, the harm and benefit — may Your Majesty examine and choose more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Between these two courses, the harm and the benefit — I ask Your Majesty to weigh them again with care.

sentences.zh: 恐不如委任長官，慎揀僚屬，所揀既少，所求亦精，得賢有鑒識之名，失實當暗謬之責。

translations.literal: I fear it is not as good as entrusting department heads, carefully selecting subordinates — what is selected being few, what is sought also refined; gaining the worthy brings a name for discernment, missing the mark brings blame for hidden error.
translations.idiomatic: Surely it would be better to entrust department heads to choose their own staffs carefully — fewer nominees, higher standards; success would bring credit for discernment, failure would bring blame for error.

sentences.zh: 人之常性，莫不愛身，況於臺省長官，皆是當朝華選，孰肯徇私妄舉，以傷名取責者耶！

translations.literal: It is human nature that none fail to cherish themselves — how much more for heads of the Secretariat and Censorate, all splendid selections of the present court; who would willingly act on private favor and reckless nomination, harming their reputation and inviting blame!
translations.idiomatic: All men naturally cherish their reputations — and these department heads are the court's finest appointments; who among them would risk his name with reckless favoritism!

sentences.zh: 所謂臺省長官，即僕射、尚書、左右丞、侍郎及御史大夫、中丞是也。

translations.literal: What are called heads of the Secretariat and Censorate are the Grand Counselors, Ministers, Left and Right Vice Directors, Vice Ministers, and the Censor-in-Chief and Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: By department heads I mean the Grand Counselors, Ministers, Vice Directors, Vice Ministers, Censor-in-Chief, and Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 陛下比擇輔相，多亦出於其中。

translations.literal: Your Majesty in recent selection of chief ministers has mostly drawn from among them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has lately chosen most of your chief ministers from these same ranks.

sentences.zh: 今之宰臣，則往日臺省長官也；

translations.literal: Today's chief ministers are yesterday's heads of the Secretariat and Censorate;
translations.idiomatic: Today's chief ministers were yesterday's department heads;

sentences.zh: 今之臺省長官，乃將來之宰臣也，但是職名暫異，固非行業頓殊。

translations.literal: today's heads of the Secretariat and Censorate are the chief ministers of the future — only the titles differ for a time; their conduct and calling are not suddenly different.
translations.idiomatic: today's department heads are tomorrow's chief ministers — the titles differ for a time, but their character and capacity are not suddenly transformed.

sentences.zh: 豈有為長官之時不能舉一二屬吏，居宰臣之位則可擇千百具僚，物議悠悠，其惑斯甚。

translations.literal: How could it be that when serving as department head they could not recommend one or two subordinate clerks, yet occupying the chief minister's place they could choose hundreds and thousands of officials — public talk drifts on, and the confusion is very great.
translations.idiomatic: How can the same men who, as department heads, could nominate only a handful of subordinates suddenly, as chief ministers, be trusted to choose hundreds of officials? Public murmuring shows how deep the confusion runs.

sentences.zh: 夫求才貴廣，考課貴精。

translations.literal: In seeking talent, breadth is prized; in examination and assessment, precision is prized.
translations.idiomatic: In seeking talent, breadth matters; in testing performance, precision matters.

sentences.zh: 求廣在於各舉所知，長吏之薦擇是也；

translations.literal: Breadth in seeking lies in each recommending those he knows — department heads' recommendation and selection is this;
translations.idiomatic: Breadth comes when each man recommends those he knows — that is the role of department heads;

sentences.zh: 貴精在於按名責實，宰臣之序進是也。

translations.literal: Precision is prized in matching name to reality and demanding results — chief ministers' ordered advancement is this.
translations.idiomatic: precision comes when names are matched to deeds and responsibility enforced — that is the role of chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 往者則天太后踐祚臨朝，欲收人心，尤務拔擢，弘委任之意，開汲引之門，進用不疑，求訪無倦，非但人得薦士，亦許自舉其才。

translations.literal: Formerly when Empress Wu Zetian ascended the throne and held court, wishing to win hearts, she especially strove to elevate men — expanding the intent of entrusting office, opening the gate of drawing up talent, promoting without doubt, seeking and inquiring without weariness; not only could men recommend scholars, they were also permitted to recommend their own talent.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu held the throne, eager to win loyalty, she promoted men with special vigor — broad delegation, open recruitment, appointment without hesitation, search without rest; not only might others recommend talent, men might recommend themselves.

sentences.zh: 所薦必行，所舉輒試，其於選士之道，豈不傷於容易哉！

translations.literal: What was recommended was always carried out, what was nominated was promptly tested — in the Way of selecting scholars, was this not harmed by being too easy!
translations.idiomatic: Every nominee was appointed, every appointee promptly tested — was not her method of selection perhaps too lenient!

sentences.zh: 而課責既嚴，進退皆速，不肖者旋黜，才能者驟升，是以當代謂知人之明，累朝賴多士之用。

translations.literal: Yet assessment and responsibility being strict, advancement and removal were all swift — the unworthy were quickly dismissed, the capable suddenly promoted; therefore the age called it clarity in knowing men, and successive reigns relied on the use of many scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because accountability was strict and promotion and dismissal swift, the unworthy were quickly removed and the able quickly advanced — so her age was praised for discernment, and later reigns benefited from the abundance of talent she produced.

sentences.zh: 此乃近於求才貴廣，考課貴精之效也。

translations.literal: This then approximates the effect of prizing breadth in seeking talent and precision in examination.
translations.idiomatic: This was close to the ideal of broad recruitment joined to rigorous assessment.

sentences.zh: 陛下誕膺寶歷，思致理平，雖好賢之心，有逾於前哲，而得人之盛，未迨於往時。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has received the precious succession and thinks to achieve order and peace; though the heart that loves the worthy surpasses former sages, the fullness of obtaining men has not reached former times.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has inherited the throne and seeks good order; though your love of talent exceeds that of earlier rulers, you have not yet matched past ages in gathering able men.

sentences.zh: 蓋由賞鑒獨任於聖聰，搜擇頗難於公舉，仍啟登延之路，罕施練核之方。

translations.literal: It is because judgment and discernment rest solely on the sage ear, search and selection are quite difficult through public nomination, yet the path of summoning and extending is opened while methods of careful verification are rarely applied.
translations.idiomatic: This is because selection rests too much on the emperor's personal judgment, open nomination has been made difficult, the door to office stands open, yet rigorous testing is rarely applied.

sentences.zh: 遂使先進者漸益雕訛，後來者不相接續，施一令則謗沮互起，用一人則瘡磐立成。

translations.literal: Thus those who advanced first gradually grew more corrupted, those who came later did not connect in succession; issuing one order then mutual slander and obstruction arose, employing one man then sores and troubles immediately formed.
translations.idiomatic: Those promoted early have grown ever more corrupt, new talent fails to follow in their stead; every order provokes mutual slander, every appointment breeds fresh trouble.

sentences.zh: 此乃失於選才太精，制法不一之患也。

translations.literal: This is the affliction of failing through selecting talent too precisely and making regulations not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: This is the harm of selecting talent too narrowly and governing by inconsistent rules.

sentences.zh: 則天舉用之法，傷易而得人；

translations.literal: Empress Wu's method of nomination and employment, though harmed by ease, obtained men;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu's method, though perhaps too lenient, did produce able men;

sentences.zh: 陛下慎揀之規，太精而失士。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's rule of careful selection is too precise and loses scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's rule of cautious selection is so strict that talent is lost.

sentences.zh: 陛下選任宰相，必異於庶官；

translations.literal: Your Majesty in selecting and appointing chief ministers must differ from common officials;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rightly treats the choice of chief ministers differently from lesser appointments;

sentences.zh: 精擇長官，必愈於末品。

translations.literal: carefully selecting department heads must be even more so than for the lowest ranks.
translations.idiomatic: and the careful selection of department heads with even greater care than low officials is also right.

sentences.zh: 及至宰相獻規，長吏薦士，陛下即但納橫議，不稽始謀。

translations.literal: Yet when chief ministers offer plans and department heads recommend scholars, Your Majesty then only accepts reckless talk and does not examine the original counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when chief ministers offer policy and department heads nominate talent, Your Majesty hears only reckless criticism and does not weigh the original proposal.

sentences.zh: 是乃任以重者輕其言，待以輕者重其事，且又不辨所毀之虛實，不校所試之短長。

translations.literal: This then is entrusting the heavy yet treating their words lightly, treating the light with heaviness in their affairs — moreover not distinguishing the truth or falsehood of what is slandered, not comparing the strengths and weaknesses of what is tested.
translations.idiomatic: Thus you treat weighty advisers lightly and light matters heavily — and you do not test the truth of slander, nor weigh the success or failure of those appointed.

sentences.zh: 人之多言，何所不至，是將使人無所措其手足，豈獨選任之道失其端而已乎！

translations.literal: When men speak much, what is there they will not reach — this will make men have nowhere to place hands and feet; is it only that the Way of selection and appointment loses its beginning!
translations.idiomatic: When rumor runs free, nothing is beyond its reach; men will not know where to turn — and the damage will extend far beyond the selection of officials alone!

sentences.zh: 上雖嘉其所陳，長官薦士之詔，竟追寢之。

translations.literal: The emperor though he praised what was set forth, the edict on department heads recommending scholars was in the end pursued and shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his argument, but the edict permitting department heads to nominate subordinates was withdrawn in the end.

sentences.zh: 國朝舊制，吏部選人，每年調集。

translations.literal: The dynasty's old system was that the Ministry of Personnel selected candidates and gathered them for assignment every year.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system of the dynasty, the Ministry of Personnel convened candidates for assignment every year.

sentences.zh: 自乾元已後，屬宿兵於野。

translations.literal: From Qianyuan onward, garrison troops were stationed in the field.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qianyuan era, troops were kept under field garrison.

sentences.zh: 歲或兇荒，遂三年一置選。

translations.literal: Years sometimes brought famine and disaster, and thus selection was held once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine and hardship, examinations were held only once every three years.

sentences.zh: 由是選人停擁，其數猥多，文書不接，真偽難辨，吏緣為奸，註授乖濫，而有十年不得調者。

translations.literal: From this candidates piled up in accumulation, their number excessively great; documents did not connect, truth and falsehood were hard to distinguish; clerks used this to commit fraud, registration and assignment went awry and excessive, and there were those ten years without assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates therefore accumulated in vast numbers; records fell out of sequence, credentials could not be verified, clerks exploited the confusion, and assignments grew arbitrary — some men waited ten years without a posting.

sentences.zh: 贄奏吏部分內外官員為三分，計闕集人，每年置選。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi memorialized that the Ministry of Personnel divide inner and outer officials into three parts, calculate vacancies and gather men, and hold selection every year.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi proposed that the Ministry divide civil and military vacancies into three categories, tally the backlog, and restore annual selection.

sentences.zh: 故選司之弊，十去七八，天下稱之。

translations.literal: Thus the abuses of the selection office were seven or eight tenths removed; all under Heaven praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The abuses of the selection office were thereby reduced by seven or eight tenths, and the realm applauded the reform.

sentences.zh: 贄與賈耽、盧邁、趙憬同知政事，百司有所申覆，皆更讓不言可否。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, together with Jia Dan, Lu Mai, and Zhao Jing, jointly managed governance; when the hundred offices had submissions for review, all deferred to one another and did not say yes or no.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi served with Jia Dan, Lu Mai, and Zhao Jing as associate chief ministers; when offices submitted business for decision, each deferred to the others and none would rule yea or nay.

sentences.zh: 舊例，宰臣當旬，秉筆決事，每十日一易，贄請準故事，令秉筆者以應之。

translations.literal: By old precedent, chief ministers on duty in rotation held the brush and decided affairs, changing every ten days; Lu Zhi requested following precedent and having the one who held the brush respond.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the chief minister on weekly rotation held the brush and decided affairs, the duty changing every ten days; Lu Zhi asked that precedent be restored so that the officer holding the brush would answer for decisions.

sentences.zh: 又以河隴陷蕃已來，西北邊常以重兵守備，謂之防秋，皆河南、江淮諸鎮之軍也，更番往來，疲於戍役。

translations.literal: Also, since Hexi and Longyou fell to Tibet, the northwest frontier was constantly guarded by heavy troops — called autumn defense — all armies from the Henan and Jiang-Huai commanderies, rotating back and forth, exhausted by garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that since Hexi and Longyou had fallen to Tibet, the northwest frontier had been held by heavy garrisons in what was called autumn defense — troops drawn from the Henan and Jiang-Huai regions, rotated in endless relays, worn down by frontier service.

sentences.zh: 贄以中原之兵，不習邊事，及扞虜戰賊，多有敗衄，又苦邊將名目太多，諸軍統制不一，緩急無以應敵，乃上疏論其事曰：

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, because central plain troops were unpracticed in frontier affairs, and in resisting barbarians and fighting bandits often suffered defeat, and also because frontier generals' titles were too many and the various armies' command was not uniform — in urgency and ease there was no means to respond to the enemy — therefore submitted a memorial discussing the matter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Central troops, Lu Zhi argued, were unused to frontier warfare and often suffered defeat against barbarians and rebels; frontier commands were too fragmented and armies lacked unified control, so that in crisis they could not respond effectively. He therefore memorialized on the matter, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣歷觀前代書史，皆謂鎮撫四夷，宰相之任，不揆闇劣，屢敢上言。

translations.literal: Your subject has repeatedly viewed the books and histories of former ages — all say that pacifying and soothing the four barbarians is the chief minister's charge; not measuring my own darkness and inferiority, I have repeatedly dared to speak upward.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the histories of past ages, I find that pacifying the frontier peoples has always been the chief minister's charge; unworthy though I am, I have ventured to speak on it repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 誠以備邊禦戎，國家之重事；

translations.literal: Truly because preparing the frontier and defending against barbarians is a weighty affair of the state;
translations.idiomatic: Frontier defense is indeed a weighty matter for the state;

sentences.zh: 理兵足食，備禦之大經。

translations.literal: ordering troops and filling granaries is the great constant of defense.
translations.idiomatic: and ordering the armies and filling the granaries is the great foundation of defense.

sentences.zh: 兵不治則無可用之師，食不足則無可固之地。

translations.literal: If troops are not ordered, there are no usable armies; if food is insufficient, there is no ground that can be held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Without disciplined armies there are no forces fit for use; without adequate provisions no territory can be held.

sentences.zh: 理兵在制置得所，足食在斂導有方。

translations.literal: Ordering troops lies in disposition being appropriate; filling granaries lies in collection and guidance having method.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline depends on proper disposition of forces; provisions depend on wise methods of collection and distribution.

sentences.zh: 陛下幸聽愚言，先務積谷，人無加賦，官不費財，坐致邊儲，數逾百萬。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has fortunately listened to my foolish words, first striving to accumulate grain — men without added taxation, offices without wasted funds — and sitting achieved frontier stores numbering more than a million.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has graciously heeded my counsel and made grain accumulation the first priority — without new taxes on the people or waste of public funds — so that frontier stores now exceed a million measures.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮收糴，今已向終，分貯軍城，用防艱急，縱有寇戎之患，必無乏絕之憂。

translations.literal: The various commanderies' grain purchases are now nearing completion; divided and stored in garrison cities for use against hardship and urgency — even if there is the affliction of bandits and barbarians, there will certainly be no worry of shortage and exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: The commanderies' grain purchases are nearly complete; stores are being distributed to garrison towns against emergency — even if barbarian raids come, there need be no fear of shortage.

sentences.zh: 守此成規，以為永制，常收冗費，益贍邊農，則更經二年，可積十萬人三歲之糧矣。

translations.literal: Keeping this established rule as an eternal institution, constantly collecting redundant expenditures to increase support for frontier farmers — then after two more years, one could accumulate three years' grain for a hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: If this policy is kept as permanent rule, and surplus expenditures are redirected to support frontier agriculture, within two more years stores sufficient for three years' supply to a hundred thousand men could be accumulated.

sentences.zh: 足食之原粗立，理兵之術未精，敢議籌量，庶備采擇。

translations.literal: The foundation of filling granaries is roughly established; the method of ordering troops is not yet refined — I dare discuss planning and calculation, hoping to prepare material for selection.
translations.idiomatic: The foundation for adequate provisions is roughly in place; the methods for ordering the armies are not yet perfected — I venture these calculations in hope that Your Majesty may find something worth adopting.

sentences.zh: 伏以戎狄為患，自古有之，其於制禦之方，得失之論，備存史籍，可得而言。

translations.literal: I humbly submit that the Rong and Di have been a scourge since antiquity; as for methods of control and defense, and discussions of gain and loss, these are fully preserved in historical records and may be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully observe that the nomadic peoples of the frontier have been a menace since ancient times. Historical records preserve full accounts of how to control and repel them, and of the debates over what succeeds and what fails — and these may still instruct us today.

sentences.zh: 大抵尊即序者，則曰「非德無以化要荒」，曾莫知威不立，則德不能馴也。

translations.literal: Generally those who honor bringing into order say, "Without virtue there is no means to transform the distant wilds" — yet they never know that if authority is not established, virtue cannot tame.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, those who champion moral suasion declare that only virtue can transform the far periphery — yet they fail to grasp that without established authority, virtue alone cannot bring wild lands to heel.

sentences.zh: 樂武威者，則曰「非兵無以服兇獷」，曾莫知德不修，則兵不可恃也。

translations.literal: Those who delight in martial prestige say, "Without arms there is no means to subdue the fierce and untamed" — yet they never know that if virtue is not cultivated, arms cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Those who exult in military might insist that only force can subdue the fierce and unruly — yet they never see that without moral cultivation, arms alone cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 務和親者，則曰「要結可以睦鄰好」，曾莫知我結之而彼復解也。

translations.literal: Those who devote themselves to marriage alliances say, "Treaty bonds can harmonize relations with neighbors" — yet they never know that though we bind them, they again unravel.
translations.idiomatic: Those committed to marriage alliances argue that treaty bonds can keep peace with neighboring peoples — yet they never reckon with how quickly such bonds are tied only to be broken again.

sentences.zh: 美長城者，則曰「設險可以固邦國而扞寇仇」，曾莫知力不足，兵不堪，則險之不能有也。

translations.literal: Those who praise the Long Walls say, "Establishing defenses can fortify the state and repel enemy raiders" — yet they never know that if strength is insufficient and troops inadequate, defenses cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: Those who admire the Great Wall claim that fortified barriers can secure the realm and hold off invaders — yet they never consider that if power is too weak and armies too thin, no barrier can be held.

sentences.zh: 尚薄伐者，則曰「驅遏可以禁侵暴而省征徭，」曾莫知兵不銳，壘不完，則遏之不能勝，驅之不能去也。

translations.literal: Those who esteem limited punitive campaigns say, "Driving and blocking can forbid aggression and reduce levies and corvée" — yet they never know that if troops are not sharp and fortifications incomplete, blocking cannot prevail and driving cannot remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who favor limited punitive expeditions say that driving the enemy back can check raids and spare the people heavy taxes and corvée — yet they never see that if troops lack edge and fortifications are incomplete, blocking fails and driving them off proves impossible.

sentences.zh: 議邊之要，略盡於斯，雖互相譏評，然各有偏駁。

translations.literal: The essentials of discussing the frontier are largely exhausted in this; though each side ridicules the other, each is one-sided and flawed.
translations.idiomatic: The main points of frontier policy debate are largely covered here. Though each camp mocks the other, every position is partial and incomplete.

sentences.zh: 聽一家之說，則例理可征；

translations.literal: Listening to one school's doctrine, then precedents and logic can be verified;
translations.idiomatic: Heed any single school of thought, and its precedents and logic seem compelling;

sentences.zh: 考歷代所行，則成敗異效。

translations.literal: Examining what successive dynasties practiced, then success and failure show different effects.
translations.idiomatic: but examine what successive dynasties actually did, and success and failure tell a different story.

sentences.zh: 是由執常理以禦其不常之勢，徇所見而昧於所遇之時。

translations.literal: This is because one clings to ordinary principles to resist extraordinary circumstances, and follows what one has seen while blind to the times one encounters.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that men cling to fixed principles against shifting circumstances, and follow what they have seen while blind to the age they actually face.

sentences.zh: 夫中夏有盛衰，夷狄有強弱，事機有利害，措置有安危，故無必定之規，亦無長勝之法。

translations.literal: The Central Lands have rise and decline; the barbarians have strength and weakness; opportunities have benefit and harm; measures have security and danger — therefore there is no fixed rule, nor any method of lasting victory.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland waxes and wanes; the barbarians grow strong and grow weak; circumstances bring advantage and disadvantage; policy brings safety and peril. There is therefore no fixed rule, and no strategy that always wins.

sentences.zh: 夏後以序戎而聖化茂，古公以避狄而王業興；

translations.literal: The Xia brought the Rong into order and sage transformation flourished; Lord Tai avoided the Di and royal enterprise rose;
translations.idiomatic: Yu of Xia brought the Rong into order, and sage rule flourished; Lord Tai fled the Di, and his royal enterprise took root;

sentences.zh: 周城朔方而獫狁攘，秦築臨洮而宗社覆；

translations.literal: Zhou walled Shuofang and the Xianyun raided; Qin built at Lintao and the altars of state were overturned;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou fortified Shuofang, and the Xianyun raided unchecked; Qin built walls at Lintao, and the dynasty fell;

sentences.zh: 漢武討匈奴而貽悔，太宗征突厥而致安；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han attacked the Xiongnu and bequeathed regret; Emperor Taizong campaigned against the Turks and achieved peace;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han pursued the Xiongnu to exhaustion and left regret behind; Emperor Taizong campaigned against the Turks and brought the realm peace;

sentences.zh: 文、景約和親而不能弭患於當年，宣、元弘撫納而足以保寧於累葉。

translations.literal: Wen and Jing pledged marriage alliances yet could not quell afflictions in their own day; Xuan and Yuan broadly soothed and received them and sufficed to preserve tranquility for successive generations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Wen and Jing relied on marriage alliances yet could not still the troubles of their own age; Emperors Xuan and Yuan pursued conciliation and acceptance, and secured peace for generations.

sentences.zh: 蓋以中夏之盛衰異勢，夷狄之強弱異時，事機之利害異情，措置之安危異便。

translations.literal: This is because the rise and decline of the Central Lands differ in circumstance, the strength and weakness of barbarians differ in time, the benefit and harm of opportunities differ in situation, and the security and convenience of measures differ in fit.
translations.idiomatic: For the heartland's rise and fall follow different circumstances; barbarian strength and weakness shift with the times; the calculus of opportunity changes with each crisis; and what makes policy safe or perilous depends on how well it fits the moment.

sentences.zh: 知其事而不度其時則敗，附其時而不失其稱則成。

translations.literal: To know the affair but not measure the time is defeat; to attach to the time without losing what is fitting is success.
translations.idiomatic: To know the right policy but misread the moment is to fail; to align with the moment without abandoning what is fitting is to succeed.

sentences.zh: 形變不同，胡可專一！

translations.literal: Forms change and are not the same — how can one be devoted to a single method!
translations.idiomatic: Conditions shift without cease — how can any one method suffice!

sentences.zh: 夫以中國強盛，夷狄衰微，而能屈膝稱臣，歸心受制，拒之則阻其向化，威之則類於殺降，安得不存而撫之，即而序之也？

translations.literal: When China is strong and barbarians are weak, and they can bend the knee as subjects and turn their hearts to submission — to reject them blocks their turning toward civilization, to overawe them resembles killing those who surrender — how can one not preserve and soothe them, and bring them into order?
translations.idiomatic: When the empire is strong and the barbarians weak, and they come kneeling as subjects with hearts turned toward submission — to reject them blocks their conversion to civilization; to terrorize them is little better than slaughtering the surrendered. How then can the court fail to preserve, soothe, and bring them into order?

sentences.zh: 又如中國強盛，夷狄衰微，而尚棄信奸盟，蔑恩肆毒，諭之不變，責之不懲，安得不取亂推亡，息人固境也？

translations.literal: Again, when China is strong and barbarians are weak, yet they still abandon faith and break alliances, scorn kindness and unleash cruelty — admonished they do not change, reproved they are not chastened — how can one not seize disorder to push toward ruin, rest the people and secure the borders?
translations.idiomatic: Again: when the empire is strong and the barbarians weak, yet they break faith, spurn alliances, despise kindness, and unleash cruelty — when persuasion fails and punishment avails nothing — how can the court fail to exploit their disorder, hasten their collapse, give the people rest, and secure the frontier?

sentences.zh: 其有遇中國喪亡之弊，當夷狄強盛之時，圖之則彼釁未萌，禦之則我力不足，安得不卑詞降禮，約好通和，啖之以親，紓其交禍？

translations.literal: When one encounters China's affliction of ruin, at a time when barbarians are strong — to scheme against them, their provocation is not yet sprouted; to resist them, our strength is insufficient — how can one not use humble words and lowered ceremony, covenant friendship and open peace, entice them with kinship, and relieve mutual calamity?
translations.idiomatic: When the empire is in decline and the barbarians are ascendant — to plot against them before their provocation has ripened is premature; to resist them outright exceeds our strength. What choice remains but humble words and lowered ceremony, covenants of friendship, overtures of peace, enticements of kinship, and every means to avert mutual ruin?

sentences.zh: 縱不必信，且無大侵，雖非禦戎之善經，蓋時事亦有不得已也。

translations.literal: Even if trust is not assured, and there is no great invasion — though this is not the excellent constant of defending against barbarians, the circumstances of the time also have what cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Even when such overtures cannot be fully trusted and no great invasion is imminent, this is not ideal frontier policy — yet there are moments when no better course is possible.

sentences.zh: 儻或夷夏之勢，強弱適同，撫之不寧，威之不靖；

translations.literal: If perhaps the power of barbarians and Chinese is evenly matched in strength and weakness, soothing does not bring tranquility and overawing does not bring peace;
translations.idiomatic: When barbarian and Chinese strength are evenly matched, conciliation brings no lasting peace and intimidation brings no lasting calm;

sentences.zh: 力足以自保，不足以出攻，得不設險以固軍，訓師以待寇，來則薄伐以遏其深入，去則攘斥而戒於遠追？

translations.literal: Strength suffices for self-preservation but not for outward attack — must one not establish defenses to secure the army, train troops to await raiders, when they come launch limited punitive campaigns to block deep penetration, and when they depart drive them off while guarding against distant pursuit?
translations.idiomatic: when strength suffices only to defend and not to strike outward, must the court not fortify defenses, drill the army, meet incursions with limited punitive strikes to block deep penetration, and when the enemy withdraws drive them off while refraining from reckless pursuit?

sentences.zh: 雖為安邊之令圖，蓋勢力亦有不得不然也。

translations.literal: Though this is the excellent plan for securing the frontier, circumstances of power also have what cannot be otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: Though this is the soundest plan for securing the frontier, there are times when power itself leaves no alternative.

sentences.zh: 故夏之即序，周之於攘，太宗之翦亂，皆乘其時而善用其勢也。

translations.literal: Therefore Xia's bringing into order, Zhou's repelling, and Taizong's cutting down disorder — all rode their times and skillfully used their circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Xia policy of orderly submission, the Zhou policy of active repulse, and Taizong's suppression of rebellion all seized their moment and wielded circumstance to advantage.

sentences.zh: 古公之避狄，文、景之和親，神堯之降禮，皆順其時而不失其稱也。

translations.literal: Lord Tai's avoiding the Di, Wen and Jing's marriage alliances, and Divine Yao's lowered ceremony — all followed their times without losing what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Tai's flight from the Di, the marriage alliances of Wen and Jing, and Gaozu's lowered ceremony all conformed to their times without abandoning propriety.

sentences.zh: 秦皇之長城，漢武之窮討，皆知其事而不度其時者也。

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin's Long Walls and Emperor Wu of Han's exhaustive campaigns — both knew the affair but did not measure the time.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor's Great Wall and Emperor Wu's relentless campaigns both understood the policy but misread the moment.

sentences.zh: 向若遇孔熾之勢，行即序之方，則見侮而不從矣！

translations.literal: If one had encountered circumstances of extreme rampancy and applied the method of bringing into order, one would have been insulted and they would not have obeyed!
translations.idiomatic: Had moral ordering been attempted when the enemy was at its most rampant, the court would have been mocked and the barbarians would not have submitted!

sentences.zh: 乘可取之資，懷畏避之誌，則失機而養寇矣！

translations.literal: Riding resources that could be seized while harboring a will of fear and avoidance — then one loses opportunity and nourishes bandits!
translations.idiomatic: To hold the advantage yet shrink from action is to forfeit opportunity and nurture the enemy!

sentences.zh: 有攘卻之力，用和親之謀，則示弱而勞費矣！

translations.literal: Having the power to repel yet employing marriage-alliance schemes — then one shows weakness and wastes resources!
translations.idiomatic: To possess the strength to drive the enemy back yet resort to marriage alliances is to show weakness and squander treasure!

sentences.zh: 當降屈之時，務翦伐之略，則召禍而危殆矣！

translations.literal: At a time of submission and humiliation, devoting oneself to strategies of cutting down and attacking — then one summons calamity and faces peril!
translations.idiomatic: To pursue aggressive campaigns when the court must bow and submit is to invite disaster and court destruction!

sentences.zh: 故曰：知其事而不度其時則敗，附其時而不失其稱則成。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: to know the affair but not measure the time is defeat; to attach to the time without losing what is fitting is success.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the maxim: to know the right policy but misread the moment is to fail; to align with the moment without abandoning what is fitting is to succeed.

sentences.zh: 是無必定之規，亦無長勝之法，得失著效，不其然歟！

translations.literal: Thus there is no fixed rule, nor any method of lasting victory — gain and loss show their effects: is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: There is no fixed rule and no eternally victorious strategy — outcomes prove the point. Is this not plainly so?

sentences.zh: 至於察安危之大情，計成敗之大數，百代之不變易者，蓋有之矣。

translations.literal: As for discerning the great truth of security and danger, and calculating the great reckoning of success and failure — what does not change across a hundred generations, perhaps there is such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in discerning the deeper truth of safety and peril, and reckoning the larger pattern of success and failure, there may be principles that hold across the ages.

sentences.zh: 其要在於失人肆欲則必蹶，任人從眾則必全，此乃古今所同，而物理之所壹也。

translations.literal: Its essentials lie in: losing the people and indulging desires then one must stumble; employing people and following the multitude then one must be preserved — this is what ancient and modern share alike, and what the nature of things unifies.
translations.idiomatic: The essential lesson is this: a ruler who alienates the people and indulges his desires will surely fall; one who employs the worthy and heeds broad counsel will surely endure. This truth is unchanged from antiquity to the present — it is the one constant in the nature of affairs.

sentences.zh: 國家自祿山構亂、河隴用兵以來，肅宗中興，撤邊備以靖中邦，借外威以寧內難。

translations.literal: Since the state, from An Lushan's rebellion and the use of troops in Hexi and Longyou, when Emperor Suzong restored the dynasty — frontier defenses were withdrawn to pacify the central realm, and foreign prestige was borrowed to settle internal crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Since An Lushan's rebellion and the wars in Hexi and Longyou, the court — even after Emperor Suzong restored the dynasty — has withdrawn frontier defenses to pacify the heartland and borrowed foreign military power to quell internal strife.

sentences.zh: 於是吐蕃乘釁，吞噬無厭；

translations.literal: Thereupon Tibet seized the opportunity, swallowing and devouring without satiety;
translations.idiomatic: Tibet seized the opening and swallowed territory without end;

sentences.zh: 回紇矜功，憑陵亦甚。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs vaunted their merit, and their bullying was also extreme.
translations.idiomatic: the Uyghurs flaunted their contributions, and their arrogance knew little bounds.

sentences.zh: 中國不遑振旅，四十余年。

translations.literal: China had no leisure to restore the armies — more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: For more than forty years the empire has lacked the strength to rebuild its armies.

sentences.zh: 使傷耗遺氓，竭力蠶織，西輸賄幣，北償馬資，尚不足塞其煩言，滿其驕誌。

translations.literal: This made the surviving people suffer depletion; they strained at sericulture, sent tribute westward, paid for horses northward — yet still could not stop their clamor or satisfy their proud ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: The surviving populace has been drained dry, taxed to the limit of silk production, sending tribute westward and paying for horses northward — yet still unable to silence their complaints or satisfy their pride.

sentences.zh: 復乃遠征士馬，列戍疆陲，猶不能遏其奔沖，止其侵侮。

translations.literal: Then again distant campaigns of troops and horses were launched, garrisons lined the borders — yet still they could not block their rushing assaults or stop their invasions.
translations.idiomatic: Even when troops were dispatched on distant campaigns and garrisons lined the frontier, the court still could not halt their raids or stop their incursions.

sentences.zh: 小入則驅略黎庶，深入則震驚邦畿。

translations.literal: Small incursions then drove and plundered the common people; deep incursions then shook and alarmed the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Minor raids plundered the countryside; major incursions shook the capital itself.

sentences.zh: 時有議安邊策者，多務於所難而忽於所易，勉於所短而略於所長。

translations.literal: At the time those who discussed policies for securing the frontier mostly strove at what was difficult while neglecting what was easy, exerted themselves in what was short while overlooking what was long.
translations.idiomatic: Those who debated frontier policy at the time mostly pursued the hard course while neglecting the easy, and strained at their weaknesses while ignoring their strengths.

sentences.zh: 遂使所易所長者，行之而其要不精；

translations.literal: Thus what was easy and long — when practiced, its essentials were not refined;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the easy and advantageous measures, when attempted, were never executed with precision;

sentences.zh: 所難所短者，圖之而其功靡就。

translations.literal: What was difficult and short — when plotted, its achievement was never realized.
translations.idiomatic: while the difficult and ill-suited ones, when pursued, never came to fruition.

sentences.zh: 憂患未弭，職斯之由。

translations.literal: That afflictions were not quelled — the office lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: That troubles remain unabated — this is the reason.

sentences.zh: 夫制敵行師，必量事勢，勢有難易，事有先後。

translations.literal: In controlling enemies and deploying armies, one must measure circumstances; circumstances have difficulty and ease, affairs have priority and sequence.
translations.idiomatic: To subdue enemies and move armies, one must weigh circumstances. Circumstances differ in difficulty; priorities must be ordered.

sentences.zh: 力大而敵脆，則先其所難，是謂奪人之心，暫勞而永逸者也；

translations.literal: When strength is great and the enemy is brittle, then first take what is difficult for them — this is called seizing the enemy's heart; temporary toil for lasting ease;
translations.idiomatic: When one's strength is great and the enemy weak, strike first at what is hardest for him — this means seizing the initiative; brief exertion for lasting peace;

sentences.zh: 力寡而敵堅，則先其所易，是謂固國之本，觀釁而後動者也。

translations.literal: When strength is few and the enemy is firm, then first take what is easy — this is called the foundation of securing the state; observing provocation before acting.
translations.idiomatic: when one's strength is limited and the enemy formidable, begin with what is easiest — this means securing the foundations of the state; watch for openings before moving.

sentences.zh: 頃屬多故，人勞未瘳，而欲廣發師徒，深踐寇境，復其侵地，攻其堅城，前有勝負未必之虞，後有饋運不繼之患。

translations.literal: Recently there have been many disturbances; the people's toil is not yet healed — yet one wishes broadly to dispatch armies, deeply tread enemy territory, recover invaded lands, and attack their strong cities — before there is the worry of uncertain victory and defeat; behind there is the affliction of supply lines not continuing.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years turmoil has been unceasing and the people are not yet recovered — yet some propose to mobilize vast armies, penetrate deep into enemy territory, recover lost lands, and assault fortified cities. Ahead lies uncertain victory; behind, the peril of broken supply lines.

sentences.zh: 儻或撓敗，適所以啟戎心而挫國威，以此為安邊之謀，可謂不量事勢而務於所難矣！

translations.literal: If perhaps one is defeated and thwarted, this precisely opens barbarian hearts and bruises national prestige — to take this as a plan for securing the frontier may be called not measuring circumstances while striving at what is difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Should such campaigns fail, they would only embolden the barbarians and shatter the empire's prestige. To call this frontier policy is to ignore circumstances while pursuing the hardest course imaginable!

sentences.zh: 天之授者，有分事，無全功；

translations.literal: What Heaven grants has divided tasks, not complete merit;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven assigns each people its portion — not every gift in full measure;

sentences.zh: 地之產者，有物宜，無兼利。

translations.literal: What Earth produces has suited things, not combined benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Earth endows each land with what suits it — not every advantage combined.

sentences.zh: 是以五方之俗，長短各殊。

translations.literal: Therefore the customs of the five directions each differ in strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the peoples of the four quarters differ in what they do well and what they do poorly.

sentences.zh: 長者不可逾，短者不可企；

translations.literal: What is long cannot be exceeded; what is short cannot be reached for;
translations.idiomatic: Strengths cannot be surpassed by force; weaknesses cannot be wished away;

sentences.zh: 勉所短而敵其所長必殆，用所長而乘其所短必安。

translations.literal: Exerting what is short to match the enemy's long leads to peril; using what is long to ride upon the enemy's short leads to security.
translations.idiomatic: to strain at weakness against the enemy's strength is to court disaster; to wield strength against the enemy's weakness is to secure safety.

sentences.zh: 強者，乃以水草為邑居，以射獵供飲茹，多馬而尤便馳突，輕生而不恥敗亡，此戎狄之所長也。

translations.literal: The strong ones take water and grass as dwelling places, take hunting and shooting to supply food and drink; they have many horses and are especially suited to sudden charges; they hold life lightly and do not shame defeat and death — this is what the Rong and Di are long at.
translations.idiomatic: The nomads live by pasture and water, sustain themselves by hunting; they keep many horses and excel at sudden cavalry charges; they hold life cheap and do not fear defeat or death — these are the barbarians' strengths.

sentences.zh: 戎狄之所長，乃中國之所短；

translations.literal: What the Rong and Di are long at is what China is short at;
translations.idiomatic: What the barbarians do well is precisely what China does poorly;

sentences.zh: 而欲益兵蒐乘，角力爭驅，交鋒原野之間，決命尋常之內，以此為禦寇之術，可謂勉所短而校其所長矣！

translations.literal: Yet wishing to increase troops and gather chariots, contest strength and compete in driving, cross blades in open country, and decide life and death within ordinary reach — to take this as the method of defending against raiders may be called exerting what is short and matching their long!
translations.idiomatic: yet to mass infantry, gather chariots, and meet them in open country for a contest of raw force and speed — to call this frontier defense is to strain at weakness and compete on the enemy's own terms!

sentences.zh: 務所難，勉所短，勞費百倍，終於無成。

translations.literal: Striving at what is difficult, exerting what is short — labor and expense a hundredfold, ending in no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Pursue the hard course, strain at weakness — and labor and expense multiply a hundredfold while success never comes.

sentences.zh: 雖果成之，不挫則廢，豈不以越天授而違地產，虧時勢以反物宜者哉！

translations.literal: Even if one indeed achieves it, if not thwarted then abandoned — is it not because one oversteps Heaven's grant, violates Earth's production, and damages the circumstances of the time contrary to what things suit!
translations.idiomatic: Even if such efforts succeed, they collapse unless constantly reinforced — for they defy Heaven's apportionment, violate Earth's natural endowment, and run counter to the fitness of things and the logic of the times!

sentences.zh: 將欲去危就安，息費從省，在慎守所易，精用所長而已。

translations.literal: If one wishes to leave danger and approach safety, rest expenditure and follow economy — it lies in carefully guarding what is easy and skillfully using what is long, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: To move from peril toward safety, and from waste toward thrift, the answer lies in steadfastly holding what is easy and skillfully deploying what we do best — nothing more.

sentences.zh: 若乃擇將吏以撫寧眾庶，修紀律以訓齊師徒，耀德以佐威，能邇以柔遠；

translations.literal: As for selecting generals and officials to soothe and settle the multitude, repairing discipline to train and align troops and masters, displaying virtue to assist authority, using ability with the near to soften the far;
translations.idiomatic: Choose capable generals and officials to govern the people; enforce discipline to drill the armies; let virtue reinforce authority and competence at home win trust abroad;

sentences.zh: 禁侵抄之暴以彰吾信，抑攻取之議以安戎心；

translations.literal: Forbid the violence of raiding and plundering to display our good faith, suppress proposals of attack and seizure to settle barbarian hearts;
translations.idiomatic: forbid predatory raids to demonstrate good faith; restrain talk of conquest to reassure the barbarians;

sentences.zh: 彼求和則善待而勿與結盟，彼為寇則嚴備而不務報復，此當今之所易也。

translations.literal: When they seek peace then treat them well but do not form alliances with them; when they become raiders then prepare strictly but do not pursue revenge — this is what is easy in the present age.
translations.idiomatic: when they sue for peace, receive them generously but bind them with no formal alliance; when they raid, fortify defenses but seek no vengeance — these are the measures readily at hand today.

sentences.zh: 賤力而貴智，惡殺而好生，輕利而重人，忍小以全大，安其居而後動，俟其時而後行。

translations.literal: Value wisdom over force, hate killing and love life, value people over profit, endure the small to preserve the great, settle one's dwelling before acting, await the time before proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: Esteem strategy over brute force; abhor killing and cherish life; prize people over profit; endure small losses to secure great gains; secure one's position before acting; wait for the right moment before moving.

sentences.zh: 是以修封疆，守要害，塹蹊隧，壘軍營，謹禁防，明斥候，務農以足食，練卒以蓄威，非萬全不謀，非百克不鬥。

translations.literal: Therefore repair borders, guard strategic points, trench paths and tunnels, fortify camps, strictly forbid and defend, clearly post scouts, strive at agriculture to fill granaries, drill soldiers to store prestige — if not wholly secure, do not plan; if not a hundredfold assured of victory, do not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Thus: repair the frontier, hold key passes, trench roads and defiles, build fortified camps, tighten patrols, post clear scouts, promote farming to fill granaries, drill troops to build deterrence — plan nothing without full security; fight only when victory is virtually assured.

sentences.zh: 寇小至則張聲勢以遏其入，寇大至則謀其人以邀其歸；

translations.literal: When raiders come in small numbers then display force to block their entry; when raiders come in great numbers then plot against their leaders to intercept their return;
translations.idiomatic: When raids are small, display strength to block entry; when raids are large, target their leaders to cut off retreat;

sentences.zh: 據險以乘之，多方以誤之。

translations.literal: Hold strategic terrain to ride upon them; use many stratagems to confuse them.
translations.idiomatic: hold advantageous ground against them; employ varied stratagems to confound them.

sentences.zh: 使其勇無所加，眾無所用；

translations.literal: Make their courage have nowhere to apply, their multitudes have nothing to use;
translations.idiomatic: Render their valor useless and their numbers impotent;

sentences.zh: 掠則靡獲，攻則不能；

translations.literal: When they plunder they gain nothing; when they attack they cannot succeed;
translations.idiomatic: let plunder yield no spoils and assault meet no success;

sentences.zh: 進有腹背受敵之虞，退有首尾難救之患，所謂乘其弊，不戰而屈人之兵，此中國之所長也。

translations.literal: Advancing they have the worry of enemies front and rear; retreating they have the affliction of head and tail hard to rescue — what is called riding their weakness, subduing the enemy's army without battle: this is what China is long at.
translations.idiomatic: advance, and they face enemies on every side; retreat, and they cannot save themselves — this is what it means to exploit their weakness and defeat their armies without battle: China's own strength.

sentences.zh: 我之所長，乃戎狄之所短；

translations.literal: What we are long at is what the Rong and Di are short at;
translations.idiomatic: What we do well is precisely what the barbarians do poorly;

sentences.zh: 我之所易，乃戎狄之所難。

translations.literal: What is easy for us is what is difficult for the Rong and Di.
translations.idiomatic: what comes easily to us is hard for them.

sentences.zh: 以長制短，則用力寡而見功多；

translations.literal: Using the long to control the short, then effort is few and visible achievement is many;
translations.idiomatic: Wield strength against weakness, and little effort yields great results;

sentences.zh: 以易敵難，則財不匱而事速就。

translations.literal: Using the easy to oppose the difficult, then funds are not exhausted and affairs are quickly accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: take the easy path against their difficulty, and treasury and manpower are spared while success comes swiftly.

sentences.zh: 舍此不務，而反為所乘，斯謂倒持戈矛，以钅尊授寇者也！

translations.literal: Abandon this and not devote oneself to it, yet on the contrary be ridden by them — this is called holding spears and halberds backward, offering a dull blade to raiders!
translations.idiomatic: To neglect this and instead play to the enemy's advantage is to hold one's weapons backward and hand the blade to the foe!

sentences.zh: 今則皆務之矣，猶且守封未固，寇戎未懲者，其病在於謀無定用，眾無適從。

translations.literal: Now all have devoted themselves to it, yet still the frontier defense is not secure and the barbarian raiders are not chastened — the disease lies in plans having no fixed application, and the multitude having no one to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Today all these measures are nominally pursued, yet the frontier remains unsecured and the barbarians undeterred — because policy lacks consistent application and no one knows which course to follow.

sentences.zh: 所任不必才，才者不必任；

translations.literal: Those appointed are not necessarily talented; the talented are not necessarily appointed;
translations.idiomatic: Those in office are not always capable; the capable are not always in office;

sentences.zh: 所聞不必實，實者不必聞；

translations.literal: What is heard is not necessarily true; what is true is not necessarily heard;
translations.idiomatic: what reaches the throne is not always true; what is true does not always reach the throne;

sentences.zh: 所信不必誠，誠者不必信；

translations.literal: Those trusted are not necessarily sincere; the sincere are not necessarily trusted;
translations.idiomatic: those trusted are not always loyal; the loyal are not always trusted;

sentences.zh: 所行不必當，當者未必行。

translations.literal: What is done is not necessarily fitting; what is fitting is not necessarily done.
translations.idiomatic: what is done is not always right; what is right is not always done.

sentences.zh: 故令措置乖方，課責虧度；

translations.literal: Therefore orders are misplaced and measures miss their mark;
translations.idiomatic: Hence policies are misdirected and accountability fails;

sentences.zh: 財匱於兵眾，力分於將多，怨生於不均，機失於遙制。

translations.literal: Funds are exhausted by too many troops; strength is divided by too many generals; resentment arises from inequality; opportunity is lost through remote control.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury is drained by excessive troop numbers; force is scattered among too many commanders; resentment breeds from unfair treatment; and timely response is lost to distant micromanagement.

sentences.zh: 臣請為陛下粗陳六者之失，惟明主慎聽而熟察之：

translations.literal: Your subject requests to roughly set forth for Your Majesty the failures of these six matters — may the enlightened sovereign listen carefully and examine them thoroughly:
translations.idiomatic: Your subject begs leave to outline for Your Majesty the six fundamental failures — may the wise sovereign hear them with care and weigh them with full attention:

sentences.zh: 臣聞工欲善其事，必先利其器；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that if a craftsman wishes to do his work well, he must first sharpen his tools;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that a craftsman who wishes to do fine work must first sharpen his tools;

sentences.zh: 武欲勝其敵，必先練其兵。

translations.literal: If one wishes in warfare to overcome the enemy, one must first drill one's troops.
translations.idiomatic: a commander who wishes to defeat the enemy must first drill his troops.

sentences.zh: 練兵之中，所用復異。

translations.literal: Within drilling troops, the uses again differ.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even among trained troops, their uses differ.

sentences.zh: 用之於救急，則權以紓難；

translations.literal: Using them for urgent rescue, then expedient measures relieve crisis;
translations.idiomatic: Troops deployed for emergency relief rely on expedient measures to resolve crisis;

sentences.zh: 用之於暫敵，則緩以應機。

translations.literal: Using them for temporary enemies, then gradual methods respond to opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: troops deployed against a passing threat rely on flexible timing to seize opportunity.

sentences.zh: 故事有便宜，而不拘常制；

translations.literal: Therefore affairs have what is expedient, and one is not bound by ordinary institutions;
translations.idiomatic: Affairs admit expedient action, unconstrained by ordinary rules;

sentences.zh: 謀有奇詭，而不徇眾情。

translations.literal: Plans have what is strange and devious, and one does not follow the multitude's sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: plans may require unorthodox stratagems, undeterred by popular opinion.

sentences.zh: 進退死生，唯將所命，此所謂攻討之兵也！

translations.literal: Advance and retreat, life and death — only the general commands — this is what is called troops for attack and punitive campaigns!
translations.idiomatic: Advance, retreat, life, and death — all at the general's command. These are the troops of offensive campaign!

sentences.zh: 用之於屯戍，則事資可久；

translations.literal: Using them for garrison defense, then affairs rely on what can last;
translations.idiomatic: Troops assigned to garrison duty must be suited to long service;

sentences.zh: 勢異從權，非物理所愜不寧，非人情所欲不固。

translations.literal: Circumstances differ and one follows expedient authority — what the nature of things does not satisfy cannot bring tranquility; what human sentiment does not desire cannot bring stability.
translations.idiomatic: circumstances vary and policy must adapt — what runs against nature cannot endure; what the soldiers do not willingly accept cannot hold.

sentences.zh: 夫人情者，利焉則勸，習焉則安，保親戚則樂生，顧家業則忘死，故可以理術馭，不可以法制驅，此所謂鎮守之兵也。

translations.literal: As for human sentiment — where there is profit then one is encouraged; where there is habit then one is at ease; protecting kin brings joy in life; looking to family estate makes one forget death — therefore one can be governed by reason and method, but cannot be driven by law and institutions — this is what is called garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Human nature responds to reward and settles into routine; soldiers fight gladly when their families are protected, and hold the line when their livelihoods are secure — they may be guided by reason, but cannot be driven by coercion alone. These are garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 夫欲備封疆，禦戎狄，非一朝一夕之事，固當選鎮守之兵以置焉。

translations.literal: If one wishes to prepare the frontier and defend against barbarians — this is not the affair of a single morning and evening; one should certainly select garrison troops to place there.
translations.idiomatic: Securing the frontier against barbarian incursion is no short-term undertaking; it requires troops specifically chosen and stationed for garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 古之善選置者，必量其性習，辨其土宜，察其伎能，知其欲惡。

translations.literal: Those skilled in selection and placement in antiquity necessarily measured their natures and habits, distinguished what suited their native soil, observed their skills and abilities, and knew their desires and aversions.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient masters of recruitment weighed each man's temperament and habits, matched him to suitable terrain, assessed his skills, and understood his inclinations.

sentences.zh: 用其力而不違其性，齊其俗而不易其宜；

translations.literal: Using their strength yet not violating their nature; aligning their customs yet not changing what suited them;
translations.idiomatic: They deployed men's strength without violating their nature, harmonized their customs without forcing them into unsuitable roles;

sentences.zh: 引其善而不責其所不能，禁其非而不處其所不欲。

translations.literal: Draw forth their strengths yet do not blame them for what they cannot do; forbid their wrongdoing yet do not impose what they do not desire.
translations.idiomatic: Encourage what they do well without faulting what they cannot do; restrain what is wrong without forcing what they reject.

sentences.zh: 而又類其紀伍，安其室家，然後能使之樂其居，定其誌，奮其氣勢，結其恩情。

translations.literal: Moreover group them in like companies, settle their households and families — only then can one make them delight in their dwelling, fix their resolve, rouse their fighting spirit, and bind their bonds of affection.
translations.idiomatic: Group them with suitable comrades, secure their families — only then will they find contentment in their posts, hold steady purpose, fight with full spirit, and forge genuine loyalty.

sentences.zh: 撫之以惠，則感而不驕；

translations.literal: Comforting them with kindness, then they are grateful yet not arrogant;
translations.idiomatic: Treat them with kindness, and they will feel gratitude without growing arrogant;

sentences.zh: 臨之以威，則肅而不怨。

translations.literal: Facing them with authority, then they are solemn yet not resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Govern them with firm authority, and they will stand in awe without nursing resentment.

sentences.zh: 靡督課而人自為用，弛禁防而眾自不攜。

translations.literal: Without overseeing and inspecting duties yet people of themselves exert themselves; loosening prohibitions and safeguards yet the multitude of themselves do not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Without constant supervision, men apply themselves willingly; with relaxed restrictions, the ranks hold together without desertion.

sentences.zh: 故出則足兵，居則足食，守則固，戰則強。

translations.literal: Therefore when they go out there are sufficient troops, when they dwell there is sufficient food, when they defend they are firm, when they fight they are strong.
translations.idiomatic: Deploy them and the army is sufficient; station them and supplies hold; hold a position and the defense is solid; enter battle and the force is formidable.

sentences.zh: 其術無他，便於人情而已矣！

translations.literal: The method has nothing else — it is simply convenient to human sentiment, that is all!
translations.idiomatic: The secret is nothing other than working with human nature — that is all!

sentences.zh: 今者散征士卒，分戍邊陲，更代往來，以為守備。

translations.literal: Now one dispersedly conscripts soldiers, divides them to garrison the frontier borders, rotates replacements coming and going, taking this as defense preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Today men are conscripted from every district, split into detachments for frontier garrison duty, rotated in and out on relay tours — and this is called border defense.

sentences.zh: 是則不量性習，不辨土宜，邀其所不能，強其所不欲。

translations.literal: This then does not measure natures and habits, does not distinguish what suits the soil; demands what they cannot do, forces what they do not desire.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is weighed of temperament or custom, nothing matched to local conditions — men are asked to do what they cannot and forced to accept what they reject.

sentences.zh: 求廣其數而不考其用，將致其力而不察其情，斯可以為羽衛之儀，而無益於備禦之實也。

translations.literal: Seeking to broaden their numbers yet not examining their usefulness; wishing to deploy their strength yet not discerning their sentiments — this may serve as the appearance of imperial guard, but is of no benefit to the substance of defensive preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Numbers are expanded without testing fitness for use; strength is summoned without reading men's hearts. Such a system may suffice for ceremonial guard duty, but it cannot meet the real demands of frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 窮邊之地，千里蕭條，寒風裂膚，驚沙慘目；

translations.literal: In lands at the utter frontier — a thousand li of desolation; cold winds split the skin; startled sand afflicts the eyes with misery;
translations.idiomatic: The far frontier is a thousand li of desolation — biting winds flay the skin, whipping sand stings the eyes;

sentences.zh: 與豺狼為鄰伍，以戰鬥為嬉遊；

translations.literal: Taking wolves and jackals as neighboring companies; taking battle as mirth and play;
translations.idiomatic: wolves and jackals are one's nearest neighbors, and combat is the daily diversion;

sentences.zh: 晝則荷戈而耕，夜則倚烽而覘；

translations.literal: By day one shoulders halberds while plowing; by night one leans on beacon-fires while scouting;
translations.idiomatic: by day they farm with weapons in hand; by night they stand watch at the beacon towers;

sentences.zh: 日有剽害之慮，永無休暇之娛，地惡人勤，於斯為甚！

translations.literal: Daily there is fear of sudden harm; forever without leisure for pleasure — vile land and toilsome men — nowhere is this more extreme!
translations.idiomatic: each day brings fear of raid and slaughter, never a moment's rest — in harshness of terrain and severity of labor, nothing surpasses it!

sentences.zh: 自非生於其域，習於其風，幼而睹焉，長而安焉，不見樂土而遷焉，則罕能寧其居而狎其敵也。

translations.literal: Unless one is born in that region, accustomed to its winds, seeing it from youth and growing up secure in it, not having seen better lands and moved away — rarely can one settle in their dwelling and become familiar with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Unless a man is native to such country, reared in its ways, raised from childhood in its hardships and never tempted elsewhere by gentler lands, he can scarcely settle contentedly or grow accustomed to facing the enemy.

sentences.zh: 關東之地，百物阜殷，從軍之徒，尤被優養。

translations.literal: In the lands east of the passes, all goods are abundant and plentiful; those who join the army are especially given generous maintenance.
translations.idiomatic: East of the passes all goods abound, and soldiers there enjoy especially generous provisions.

sentences.zh: 慣於溫飽，狎於歡康，比諸邊隅，若異天地。

translations.literal: Accustomed to warmth and fullness; familiar with comfort and ease — compared with the frontier corners, it is as though different heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Accustomed to comfort and plenty, they know only ease and pleasure — compared with the borderlands, it might be another world.

sentences.zh: 聞絕塞荒陬之苦，則辛酸動容；

translations.literal: When they hear of the hardships of utterly blocked passes and desolate frontiers, then bitter sorrow moves their countenance;
translations.idiomatic: Mention the miseries of blocked passes and barren frontiers, and their faces twist with distress;

sentences.zh: 聆強蕃勁虜之名，則懾駭奪氣。

translations.literal: When they listen to the names of powerful frontier tribes and fierce barbarians, then fear and terror seize their breath.
translations.idiomatic: speak the names of powerful tribes and fierce enemies, and terror drains the courage from their veins.

sentences.zh: 而乃使之去親族，舍園廬，甘其所辛酸，抗其所懾駭，將冀為用，不亦疏乎！

translations.literal: Yet one would have them leave their kin, abandon their homes and cottages, endure what they find bitter, confront what they fear — and expect to employ them profitably — is this not far-fetched!
translations.idiomatic: Yet these same men are sent from their families, from their homes, to endure what appalls them and face what terrifies them — and we expect them to serve effectively. How misplaced is that hope!

sentences.zh: 矧又有休代之期，無統帥之馭，資奉若驕子，姑息如倩人，進不邀之以成功，退不處之以嚴憲。

translations.literal: Moreover there are terms for rest and rotation, no commanding general's control; provisions like for spoiled children, indulgence like for hired strangers; on advance not inviting them with success, on retreat not treating them with strict law.
translations.idiomatic: To make matters worse: rotation schedules promise release but no commander truly governs them; provisions are lavished like on favored sons while discipline is lax as with hired labor; no reward awaits success in the field, no penalty follows failure in retreat.

sentences.zh: 其來也鹹負得色，其止也莫有固心，屈指計歸，張頤待飼。

translations.literal: When they arrive all wear a countenance of having gained; when they stop none have steadfast hearts; counting fingers calculating return, opening mouths awaiting feed.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival they swagger as if winning a prize; once posted they hold no firm loyalty — counting days till rotation, mouths open waiting to be fed.

sentences.zh: 僥倖者猶患還期之賒緩，常念戎醜之充斥；

translations.literal: Even the lucky still worry the return date is slow and deferred; constantly they think of barbarian enemies swarming abroad;
translations.idiomatic: Even the fortunate fret that rotation comes too slowly, while constantly brooding on the enemy hordes abroad;

sentences.zh: 王師挫傷，則將乘其亂離，布路東潰，情誌且爾，得之奚為？

translations.literal: When the imperial army is defeated and wounded, then they will seize the disorderly dispersion, scatter along the road eastward in rout — sentiments and resolve being thus, what use is gaining them?
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial army suffers defeat, they will seize the moment of confusion and scatter eastward in flight — with hearts and minds like these, what good are they?

sentences.zh: 平居則殫耗資儲以奉浮冗之眾，臨難則拔棄城鎮以搖遠近之心，其弊豈惟無益哉！

translations.literal: In normal times they exhaust stores and reserves to support a floating redundant multitude; facing crisis they abandon towns and fortresses to shake the hearts of far and near — its harm is not only without benefit!
translations.idiomatic: In peacetime they drain the treasury feeding a useless host; in crisis they abandon fortresses and shake confidence near and far — the harm goes far beyond mere uselessness!

sentences.zh: 固亦將有所撓也。

translations.literal: Indeed it will also cause some undermining.
translations.idiomatic: It actively undermines the defense as well.

sentences.zh: 復有抵犯刑禁，謫徙軍城，意欲增戶實邊，兼令展效自贖。

translations.literal: Again there are those who violate criminal prohibitions, banished and relocated to military cities — the intent is to increase households and fill the frontier, and also to have them display merit to redeem themselves.
