translations.idiomatic: Criminals condemned to frontier garrison are sent to swell border populations and redeem themselves through service.

sentences.zh: 既是無良之類，且加懷土之情，思亂幸災，又甚戍卒。

translations.literal: Being already a class without virtue, and moreover possessed of attachment to homeland feeling — thinking of disorder and rejoicing in disaster — this is worse than garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: These are men of bad character to begin with, further burdened with homesickness — they pray for chaos and welcome disaster — worse even than ordinary garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 適足煩於防衛，諒無望於功庸，雖前代時或行之，固非良算之可遵者也。

translations.literal: They merely suffice to trouble defense; surely one cannot hope for merit — though former ages at times applied this, it is truly not a good plan that can be followed.
translations.idiomatic: They burden the defenders without yielding any military gain — though earlier dynasties tried this at times, it is no sound policy to repeat.

sentences.zh: 復有擁旄之帥，身不臨邊，但分偏師，俾守疆場。

translations.literal: Again there are commanders bearing insignia — their persons do not approach the border; they only divide partial armies and cause them to guard the frontier fields.
translations.idiomatic: Then there are commanders with imperial banners who never go to the border themselves, sending only partial detachments to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 大抵軍中壯銳，元戎例選自隨，委其疲羸，乃配諸鎮。

translations.literal: Generally in the army the strong and sharp — the commander-in-chief habitually selects for his own following; abandoning the weary and weak, these are then assigned to the various garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, the strongest troops stay with the commanding general; the worn and weak are farmed out to the border posts.

sentences.zh: 節將既居內地，精兵祗備紀綱，遂令守要禦沖，常在寡弱之輩。

translations.literal: Since the frontier general already dwells in the interior, elite troops serve only for regulation and order — thus causing defense of key points and warding of strategic passes always to fall to the few and weak.
translations.idiomatic: With the commander safe inland, his crack troops reserved for parade and protocol, the vital passes are always left to thin, weak detachments.

sentences.zh: 寇戎每至，乃勢不支，入壘者才足閉關，在野者悉遭劫執，恣其芟蹂，盡其搜驅。

translations.literal: When barbarian raiders each time arrive, then strength cannot support — those entering fortifications barely suffice to close the passes; those in the open all suffer seizure and capture; the raiders indulge in mowing and trampling, exhaustively searching and driving off.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders strike, the garrison cannot hold — those who make it inside barely shut the gates; those caught outside are seized wholesale, fields ravaged, people rounded up and driven away.

sentences.zh: 比及都府聞知，虜已克獲旋返。

translations.literal: By the time the metropolitan command hears and knows, the barbarians have already taken their spoils and returned spinning back.
translations.idiomatic: By the time headquarters learns of the attack, the enemy has taken what they came for and withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 且安邊之本，所切在兵，理兵若斯，可謂措置乖方矣！

translations.literal: Moreover the root of securing the frontier — what is urgently needed lies in the troops; managing troops like this — one may say the placement is misdirected!
translations.idiomatic: Securing the frontier depends above all on the army — and to manage troops thus is to misdirect policy entirely!

sentences.zh: 夫賞以存勸，罰以示懲，勸以懋有庸，懲以威不恪。

translations.literal: Rewards exist to preserve encouragement; punishments exist to show chastisement — encouragement by which meritorious service is exalted; chastisement by which the undisciplined are awed.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards exist to encourage merit; punishments to deter wrongdoing — the one to honor achievement, the other to intimidate the disobedient.

sentences.zh: 故賞罰之於馭眾也，猶繩墨之於曲直，權衡之揣重輕，輗軏之所以行車，銜勒之所以服馬也。

translations.literal: Therefore rewards and punishments in governing the multitude are like inked lines for straight and crooked, scales for weighing heavy and light, the yoke-bar and linchpin by which chariots move, the bit and bridle by which horses are subdued.
translations.idiomatic: In command of men, reward and punishment are what the carpenter's line is to straight and crooked, what the scale is to weight, what axle and yoke are to the chariot, what bit and bridle are to the horse.

sentences.zh: 馭眾而不用賞罰，則善惡相混而能否莫殊；

translations.literal: Governing the multitude yet not using rewards and punishments — then good and evil mix together and the capable and incapable are undistinguished;
translations.idiomatic: Command troops without reward and punishment, and good and bad blur together until no one can be told apart;

sentences.zh: 用之而不當功過，則奸妄寵榮而忠實擯抑。

translations.literal: Using them yet not matching merit and fault — then the treacherous and rash are favored and honored while the loyal and steadfast are pushed aside and suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: Apply them without matching merit to reward and fault to penalty, and the reckless win favor while the faithful are cast aside.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，若聰明可衒，律度無章，則用與不用，其弊一也。

translations.literal: If matters are thus — though intelligence may be displayed and regulations without order — then using or not using them, the harm is one and the same.
translations.idiomatic: Either way — whether reward and punishment are abandoned or applied without consistent rule — the result is the same ruin.

sentences.zh: 自頃權移於下，柄失於朝，將之號令，既鮮克行之於軍，國之典章，又不能施之於將，務相遵養，茍度歲時。

translations.literal: Recently power has shifted downward, the handle lost at court; the general's orders — already rarely able to be carried out in the army; the state's institutions — also unable to be applied to generals; each strives to follow and indulge, passing the years perfunctorily.
translations.idiomatic: Lately power has slipped to lower ranks while the court has lost the reins — generals' orders scarcely reach the ranks, and state law cannot bind the commanders; all parties merely indulge one another and let the years slide by.

sentences.zh: 欲賞一有功，翻慮無功者反側；

translations.literal: Wishing to reward one who has merit, one instead worries those without merit will waver in discontent;
translations.idiomatic: To reward one man of merit is to fear rebellion from those without;

sentences.zh: 欲罰一有罪，復慮同惡者憂虞。

translations.literal: Wishing to punish one who has guilt, one again worries those of shared evil will be anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: To punish one guilty man is to dread unrest among his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 罪以隱忍而不彰，功以嫌疑而不賞，姑息之道，乃至於斯。

translations.literal: Crimes are concealed and tolerated so they are not made manifest; merit is held in suspicion and not rewarded — the way of indulgence has reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes are hushed up rather than exposed; merit is withheld on suspicion — indulgence has sunk to this level.

sentences.zh: 故使忘身效節者，獲誚於等夷；

translations.literal: Therefore those who forget self and display loyalty are mocked by their peers;
translations.idiomatic: Those who risk all in loyal service are mocked by their peers;

sentences.zh: 率眾先登者，取怨於士卒；

translations.literal: Those who lead the multitude and mount first draw resentment from the soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: those who lead charges draw hatred from the ranks;

sentences.zh: 僨軍蹙國者，不懷於愧畏；

translations.literal: Those who ruin the army and constrain the state feel no shame or fear;
translations.idiomatic: those who ruin armies and endanger the realm feel no shame or fear;

sentences.zh: 緩救失期者，自以為智能。

translations.literal: Those who tardily rescue and miss the deadline consider themselves intelligent.
translations.idiomatic: those who arrive late to save the day congratulate themselves on their cleverness.

sentences.zh: 褒貶既闕而不行，稱毀復紛然相亂，人雖欲善，誰為言之？

translations.literal: Praise and blame being already lacking and not enforced, acclaim and slander again chaotically mixed — though people wish to do good, who will speak for them?
translations.idiomatic: With neither praise nor blame enforced, rumor and slander swirl without order — though a man wishes to do right, who will speak up for him?

sentences.zh: 況又公忠者，直己而不求於人，反罹困厄；

translations.literal: Moreover public-spirited and loyal ones — upright in themselves and not seeking from others — instead suffer hardship;
translations.idiomatic: The upright and loyal, who ask nothing of others, are the ones who suffer hardship;

sentences.zh: 敗撓者，行私而茍媚於眾，例獲優崇。

translations.literal: Defeatists and weaklings — pursuing private ends and flattering the multitude — routinely receive generous honor.
translations.idiomatic: while cowards who serve private ends and flatter the ranks routinely win favor and promotion.

sentences.zh: 此義士所以痛心，勇夫所以解體也。

translations.literal: This is why men of principle ache in the heart, why brave warriors lose cohesion of body and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: This is what breaks the hearts of men of principle and dissolves the courage of the brave.

sentences.zh: 又有遇敵而所守不固，陳謀而其效靡成；

translations.literal: Again there are those who meet the enemy yet what they defend is not firm, present plans yet their effects never achieved;
translations.idiomatic: There are those who fail to hold when the enemy strikes, who offer plans that never succeed;

sentences.zh: 將帥則以資糧不足為詞，有司復以供給無闕為解。

translations.literal: Generals cite insufficient funds and grain as their plea; responsible offices in turn cite unbroken supply as their defense.
translations.idiomatic: commanders blame insufficient supplies; the quartermasters insist nothing was lacking.

sentences.zh: 既相執證，理合辨明，朝廷每為含糊，未嘗窮究曲直。

translations.literal: Since they mutually hold evidence, reason demands clarification — yet the court each time acts vaguely, never thoroughly investigating right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: With conflicting accounts on the table, the matter ought to be settled — yet the court equivocates and never pursues the truth.

sentences.zh: 措理者吞聲而靡訴，誣善者罔上而不慚。

translations.literal: Those who set things in order swallow their voices without appeal; those who slander the good deceive superiors without shame.
translations.idiomatic: The honest swallow their grievances in silence; the deceitful mislead their superiors without a blush.

sentences.zh: 馭眾若斯，可謂課責虧度矣！

translations.literal: Governing the multitude like this — one may say accountability has missed its measure!
translations.idiomatic: To command troops thus is to abandon accountability entirely!

sentences.zh: 課責虧度，措置乖方，將不得竭其材，卒不得盡其力，屯集雖眾，戰陣莫前。

translations.literal: Accountability missing its measure, placement misdirected — generals cannot exhaust their talent, soldiers cannot fully exert their strength; though massed in garrison they are many, in battle formation none advance.
translations.idiomatic: With accountability gone and policy misdirected, generals cannot use their full talent nor soldiers their full strength — though armies mass in number, none advance when battle comes.

sentences.zh: 虜每越境橫行，若涉無人之地；

translations.literal: Barbarians each time cross the border and rampage sideways, as though treading land without people;
translations.idiomatic: The enemy crosses the border at will, as though marching through empty land;

sentences.zh: 遞相推倚，無敢誰何，虛張賊勢上聞，則曰兵少不敵。

translations.literal: Each in turn pushes and leans on others, none daring to confront them; when falsely inflating the bandits' strength to report upward, they say troops are few and cannot match the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: commanders pass the burden to one another, none daring to act; when they must report upward they inflate the enemy's strength and plead that their own numbers are too few.

sentences.zh: 朝廷莫之省察，惟務征發益師，無裨備禦之功，重增供億之弊。

translations.literal: The court does not examine this; it only strives to levy and dispatch additional troops — no help to defensive achievement, heavily adding the harm of supply burdens.
translations.idiomatic: The court never examines the facts, only conscripts more troops — which adds nothing to defense while multiplying the burden of supply.

sentences.zh: 閭井日耗，征求日繁，以編戶傾家破產之資，兼有司榷鹽稅酒之利，總其所入，半以事邊，制用若斯，可謂財匱於兵眾矣！

translations.literal: Villages and households daily are depleted; levies daily grow numerous — using registered households' resources that ruin families and bankrupt estates, together with offices' monopoly profits on salt and tax on wine — totaling their intake, half is used for the frontier; managing expenditure like this — one may say finances are exhausted by too many troops!
translations.idiomatic: Villages empty day by day, levies multiply — draining registered households to ruin, together with monopolies on salt and taxes on wine, half of all revenue goes to the frontier. Such is the management of funds — the treasury is drained by excessive troop numbers!

sentences.zh: 今四夷之最強盛為中國甚患者，莫大於吐蕃，舉國勝兵之徒，才當中國十數大郡而已。

translations.literal: Now among the four barbarians, the strongest and most flourishing — greatest affliction to China — none is greater than Tibet; the whole nation's fit-for-war men only equal a dozen or so large commanderies of China.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the barbarian powers that threaten China today, none is greater than Tibet — yet its entire army scarcely equals the fighting men of a dozen large Chinese prefectures.

sentences.zh: 其於內虞外備，亦與中國不殊，所能寇邊，數則蓋寡。

translations.literal: Their internal caution and external defense are also not different from China; what they can do in raiding the frontier — in numbers they are probably few.
translations.idiomatic: They face internal worries and external threats much as China does, and the forces they can mount for border raids are relatively few.

sentences.zh: 且又器非犀利，甲不堅完，識迷韜鈐，藝乏趫敏。

translations.literal: Moreover their weapons are not sharp, armor not solid and complete; their knowledge is confused in military stratagem, their arts lacking in agility.
translations.idiomatic: Their weapons are not keen, their armor not strong, their commanders ignorant of strategy, their soldiers lacking skill and agility.

sentences.zh: 動則中國畏其眾而不敢抗，靜則中國憚其強而不敢侵，厥理何哉？

translations.literal: When they move, China fears their multitude and dares not resist; when they are still, China dreads their strength and dares not invade — what is the reason for this?
translations.idiomatic: When they move, China fears their numbers and dares not resist; when still, China dreads their strength and dares not attack — why is this?

sentences.zh: 良以中國之節制多門，蕃醜之統帥專一故也。

translations.literal: Truly because China's command has many gates, while the barbarian enemy's commander is unified — that is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Because China's military command is fragmented among many hands, while the barbarian leader's authority is unified.

sentences.zh: 夫統帥專則人心不分，人心不分則號令不貳，號令不貳則進退可齊，進退可齊則疾徐如意，疾徐如意則機會靡愆，機會靡愆則氣勢自壯！

translations.literal: When the commander is unified then hearts of men are not divided; hearts not divided then orders are not twofold; orders not twofold then advance and retreat can be aligned; advance and retreat aligned then fast and slow accord with intent; fast and slow accord with intent then opportunities are not missed; opportunities not missed then fighting spirit naturally grows strong!
translations.idiomatic: Unified command means unified purpose; unified purpose means undivided orders; undivided orders mean coordinated movement; coordinated movement means control of pace; control of pace means seizing every opportunity; and seizing opportunity means spirit naturally rises!

sentences.zh: 斯乃以少為眾，以弱為強，變化翕辟，在於反掌之內。

translations.literal: This then is making few into many, weak into strong — transformation contracting and expanding within the turn of the palm.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the few become as many, the weak as strong — transformation at a snap of the fingers.

sentences.zh: 是猶臂之使指，心之制形，若所任得人，則何敵之有！

translations.literal: It is like the arm commanding the fingers, the heart controlling the form — if those appointed are the right men, then what enemy could there be!
translations.idiomatic: Like the arm directing the fingers, the mind governing the body — appoint the right men and what enemy could stand against you!

sentences.zh: 夫節制多門則人心不一，人心不一則號令不行，號令不行則進退難必，進退難必則疾徐失宜，疾徐失宜則機會不及，機會不及則氣勢自衰！

translations.literal: When command has many gates then hearts of men are not one; hearts not one then orders are not carried out; orders not carried out then advance and retreat cannot be ensured; advance and retreat not ensured then fast and slow miss their fit; fast and slow miss their fit then opportunities are not reached; opportunities not reached then fighting spirit naturally declines!
translations.idiomatic: Fragmented command splits purpose; split purpose means orders fail; failed orders mean movement cannot be coordinated; uncoordinated movement means mistimed action; mistimed action means lost opportunities; and lost opportunities mean spirit collapses!

sentences.zh: 斯乃勇廢為尪，眾散為弱，逗撓離析，兆乎戰陣之前。

translations.literal: This then is courage discarded becoming frailty, multitude scattered becoming weakness — procrastination, delay, and dissolution foreshadowed before the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Courage turns to weakness, numbers to scattering — hesitation and fracture appear before battle is even joined.

sentences.zh: 是猶一國三公，十羊九牧，欲令齊肅，其可得乎？

translations.literal: It is like three dukes in one state, nine shepherds for ten sheep — wishing to make them uniformly disciplined, can this be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Like three rulers in one kingdom, nine shepherds for ten sheep — can uniformity and discipline come of that?

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶之間，控禦西北兩蕃，唯朔方、河西、隴右三節度而已，猶慮權分勢散，或使兼而領之。

translations.literal: Between Kaiyuan and Tianbao, controlling and defending against the two frontier barbarians of northwest — only three military commissions: Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou — yet still they worried power would divide and force scatter, sometimes having one man hold them jointly.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, defense against the two northwestern powers rested on only three commands — Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou — and even then the court worried about divided authority, sometimes appointing one man to hold several at once.

sentences.zh: 中興已來，未遑外討，僑隸四鎮於安定，權附隴右於扶風，所當西北兩蕃，亦朔方、涇原、隴右、河東節度而已，關東戍卒，至則屬焉。

translations.literal: Since the Restoration, without leisure for external punitive campaigns — the four garrisons were provisionally subordinated at Anding, Longyou was temporarily attached at Fufeng — what faced the two northwest barbarians was also only the Shuofang, Jingyuan, Longyou, and Hedong military commissions; when eastern garrison soldiers arrived they were then subordinated there.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Restoration, with no capacity for external campaigns, the four western garrisons were lodged at Anding and Longyou temporarily attached to Fufeng — defense against the northwest still fell to Shuofang, Jingyuan, Longyou, and Hedong; eastern garrison troops, when dispatched, reported to them.

sentences.zh: 雖委任未盡得人，而措置尚存典制。

translations.literal: Although appointments were not all the right men, placement still preserved the institutional system.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments were not always ideal, but the institutional framework still held.

sentences.zh: 自頃逆泚誘涇、隴之眾叛，懷光汙朔方之軍，割裂誅鋤，所余無幾。

translations.literal: Recently the rebel Zhu Ci lured the masses of Jing and Long to defect; Huai Guang defiled the Shuofang army — carved up and purged, what remained was not much.
translations.idiomatic: Lately Zhu Ci lured Jing and Long troops into rebellion; Huai Guang corrupted the Shuofang army — after purges and partition, little remained.

sentences.zh: 而又分朔方之地，建牙擁節者，凡三使焉。

translations.literal: Moreover they divided Shuofang territory — those who raised banners and bore insignia numbered three commissioners in all.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang itself was split among three separate commanders with imperial banners.

sentences.zh: 其余鎮軍，數且四十，皆承特詔委寄，各降中貴監臨，人得抗衡，莫相稟屬。

translations.literal: The remaining garrison armies, numbering nearly forty — all received special edict appointments; each was sent an eunuch supervisor; men could counterbalance one another, none subordinated to another.
translations.idiomatic: Other frontier armies, nearly forty in number, each held a special imperial commission with an eunuch overseer — commanders stood as equals, subordinate to none.

sentences.zh: 每俟邊書告急，方令計會用兵，既無軍法下臨，唯以客禮相待。

translations.literal: Each time only when frontier reports came urgent were they ordered to plan and assemble troops — with no military law descending from above, only guest courtesy toward one another.
translations.idiomatic: Only when frontier dispatches report crisis are they summoned to coordinate forces — with no superior military law over them, only mutual courtesy among equals.

sentences.zh: 是乃從容拯溺，揖讓救焚，冀無阽危，固亦難矣！

translations.literal: This then is leisurely saving the drowning, bowing and yielding to rescue from fire — hoping to avoid peril on the brink, indeed this is hard!
translations.idiomatic: This is like saving a drowning man without haste, or fighting a fire with polite ceremony — to hope for safety from peril in such fashion is impossible!

sentences.zh: 夫兵，以氣勢為用者也，氣聚則盛，散則消；

translations.literal: As for troops — they use fighting spirit as their function; spirit gathered then flourishes, scattered then dissipates;
translations.idiomatic: An army lives by its spirit — gathered it is formidable, scattered it evaporates;

sentences.zh: 勢合則威，析則弱。

translations.literal: Force combined then is formidable, divided then weak.
translations.idiomatic: united in force it is powerful, divided it is weak.

sentences.zh: 今之邊備，勢弱氣消，建軍若斯，可謂力分於將多矣。

translations.literal: Today's frontier preparations — force weak, spirit dissipated; establishing armies like this — one may say strength is divided by too many generals.
translations.idiomatic: Today's border defense is weak in force and broken in spirit — to organize armies thus is to scatter strength among too many commanders.

sentences.zh: 理戎之要，最在均齊，故軍法無貴賤之差，軍實無多少之異，是將所以同其誌而盡其力也。

translations.literal: The essential of managing troops lies most in evenness and balance — therefore military law has no distinction of noble and base rank; military provisions have no difference of more and less — this is how generals unite their resolve and exhaust their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The key to governing troops is equity — hence military law makes no distinction of rank in duty, and provisions no arbitrary difference in amount — this is how commanders align purpose and extract full effort.

sentences.zh: 如或誘其誌意，勉其藝能，則當閱其材，程其勇，校其勞逸，度其安危，明申練覆優劣之科，以為衣食等級之制。

translations.literal: If one would draw their resolve and intent, encourage their arts and ability — then one ought to examine their talent, measure their courage, compare their toil and rest, gauge their danger and safety; clearly declare standards for drilling and reviewing excellence and inferiority, making this the system of grades for food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: If one would inspire resolve and cultivate skill, one must assess talent, test courage, weigh hardship against ease and risk against safety — establish clear standards for training review and merit, and from these derive graded provision of food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 使能者企及，否者息心，雖有薄厚之殊，而無觖望之釁。

translations.literal: Make the capable aspire to reach higher; the incapable quiet their hearts — though there are differences of thin and thick, there will be no resentment and cause for dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Let the able strive upward and the less able accept their place — though provisions differ in degree, none will harbor grievance or cause for mutiny.

sentences.zh: 蓋所謂日省月試，餼稟均事，如權量之無情於物，萬人莫不安其分而服其平也。

translations.literal: This is what is called daily examination, monthly testing, rations and grain measured equally — like scales and weights without partiality toward things — ten thousand men none failing to rest in their allotted portion and submit to its fairness.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by daily inspection and monthly review, equal measure in rations — like scales impartial to all objects — so that every man accepts his station and trusts the fairness of the system.

sentences.zh: 今者窮邊之地，長鎮之兵，皆百戰傷夷之余，終年勤苦之劇，角其所能則練習，度其所處則孤危，考其服役則勞，察其臨敵則勇。

translations.literal: Now in lands at the utter frontier, long-garrisoned troops — all are remnants after a hundred battles and wounds, the severity of year-round toil and hardship; compare their abilities then they are practiced; gauge their situation then it is isolated and perilous; examine their service then it is toilsome; observe them facing the enemy then they are brave.
translations.idiomatic: Today's far-frontier garrisons are veterans of a hundred battles, men who toil without respite — skilled in arms, isolated in position, exhausted in service, brave before the enemy.

sentences.zh: 然衣糧所給，唯止當身，例為妻子所分，常有凍餒之色。

translations.literal: Yet the clothing and grain supplied reaches only their own person, habitually divided with wife and children — constantly bearing the color of freezing and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their rations cover only themselves, habitually shared with wives and children — they wear the look of cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 而關東戍卒，歲月踐更，不安危城，不習戎備，怯於應敵，懈於服勞。

translations.literal: Yet eastern garrison soldiers, month by month fulfilling rotation — not dwelling in perilous fortresses, not practiced in military readiness; timid in facing the enemy, slack in bearing toil.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern garrison troops, rotated year by year, never hold dangerous posts, never drill for war — timid in battle, slack in labor.

sentences.zh: 然衣糧所頒，厚逾數等，繼以茶藥之饋，益以蔬醬之資。

translations.literal: Yet the clothing and grain distributed is thicker by several grades; followed by gifts of tea and medicine; further augmented by provisions of vegetables and sauce.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their rations exceed those of frontier men by several grades, supplemented with tea and medicine, vegetables and condiments.

sentences.zh: 豐約相形，懸絕斯甚。

translations.literal: Abundance and scarcity mutually compared — the gap is extremely vast.
translations.idiomatic: Abundance beside want — the disparity is staggering.

sentences.zh: 又有素非禁旅，本是邊軍，將校詭為媚詞，因請遙隸神策，不離舊所，唯改虛名，其於稟賜之饒，遂有三倍之益。

translations.literal: Again there are those never belonging to the imperial guard, originally frontier troops — officers craftily use flattering words and thereby request distant subordination to the Shence Army; not leaving their old location, only changing empty title — their share of gifts and grants then has triple the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Some frontier troops, never part of the palace guard, persuade their officers with flattery to nominally join the Shence Army — staying in the same post under a new title, they triple their stipends.

sentences.zh: 此儔類所以忿恨，忠良所以憂嗟，疲人所以流亡，經費所以褊匱。

translations.literal: This is why fellow soldiers grow resentful, the loyal and good sigh in worry, weary men flee and wander, and budget funds become narrow and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Hence resentment among comrades, grief among the loyal, desertion among the worn, and exhaustion of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 夫事業未異，而給養有殊，人情之所不能甘也，況乎矯佞行而稟賜厚，績藝劣而衣食優，茍未忘懷，能無慍怒！

translations.literal: Duties not different yet provisions have distinctions — what human sentiment cannot accept; moreover when crafty flattery advances and gifts and grants are thick, when achievement and skill are inferior yet food and clothing superior — if not yet forgotten in the heart, can there be no angry resentment!
translations.idiomatic: Same service, unequal pay — what human nature cannot accept; how much worse when flatterers feast while the skilled go hungry — who could bear it without anger!

sentences.zh: 不為戎首，則已可嘉，而欲使其協力同心，以攘寇難，雖有韓、白、孫、吳之將，臣知其必不能焉。

translations.literal: Not to become ringleaders of war — that already can be praised; yet wishing to make them cooperate in heart, united in purpose to repel bandit difficulty — though there were generals like Han, Bai, Sun, and Wu — your subject knows they certainly cannot.
translations.idiomatic: If they refrain from leading mutiny, that alone is praise-worthy — yet to expect united effort against the enemy, even with commanders like Han Xin, Bai Qi, Sun Wu, or Wu Qi, your subject knows it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 養士若斯，可謂怨生於不均矣！

translations.literal: Nourishing soldiers like this — one may say resentment arises from inequality!
translations.idiomatic: To maintain troops thus is to breed resentment from inequality!

sentences.zh: 凡欲選任將帥，必先考察行能，然後指以所授之方，語以所委之事，令其自揣可否，自陳規模。

translations.literal: Generally, when wishing to select and appoint generals and commanders, one must first investigate conduct and ability; then point out the direction to be entrusted, speak of the affairs to be delegated — have them themselves weigh whether they can or cannot, themselves declare their plan.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever selecting commanders, one must first examine character and capacity; then specify the territory assigned and the tasks entrusted — let each man judge for himself whether he is fit, and state his own plan.

sentences.zh: 須某色甲兵，藉某人參佐，要若干士馬，用若干資糧，某處置軍，某時成績，始終要領，悉俾經綸，於是觀其計謀，校其聲實。

translations.literal: Require so many armored troops of a given color, rely on so-and-so for assistance, need so many soldiers and horses, use so much provisions — at such a place to deploy the army, at such a time to achieve results; the essentials from beginning to end — entrust all planning to him; then observe his stratagems, verify his words against reality.
translations.idiomatic: Specify the armor and troops required, the aides needed, the numbers of men and horses, the amount of supplies, where to camp the army and when results are expected — entrust the full plan from start to finish, then assess his strategy and weigh his promises against results.

sentences.zh: 若謂材無足取，言不可行，則當退之於初，不宜貽慮於其後也。

translations.literal: If one says talent is not worth taking, words cannot be carried out — then one ought to dismiss at the outset; it is not fitting to leave worries for afterward.
translations.idiomatic: If his talent is deemed inadequate or his plan impracticable, dismiss him at the start — do not let misgivings linger until later.

sentences.zh: 若謂志氣足任，方略可施，則當要之於終，不宜掣肘於其間也。

translations.literal: If one says spirit and resolve are sufficient to bear responsibility, strategy can be applied — then one ought to require completion to the end; it is not fitting to pull at the elbow in the midst.
translations.idiomatic: If his resolve is sound and his strategy viable, hold him accountable to the end — do not hamstring him midway.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，則疑者不使，使者不疑；

translations.literal: If it is so, then the doubting are not employed, the employed do not doubt;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the uncertain are never appointed, and those appointed are never doubted;

sentences.zh: 勞神於選才，端拱於委任。

translations.literal: Toil the spirit in selecting talent, sit upright with hands folded in delegation.
translations.idiomatic: Exhaust effort in choosing the right men, then sit with hands folded in trust once they are appointed.

sentences.zh: 既委其事，既足其求，然後可以核其否臧，行其賞罰。

translations.literal: Having delegated the affair, having fulfilled his requests — afterward one may examine success or failure, carry out rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Once the task is entrusted and resources provided, one may then judge success or failure and administer reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 受賞者不以為濫，當罰者無得而辭，付授之柄既專，茍且之心自息。

translations.literal: Those receiving reward do not consider it excessive; those deserving punishment have nothing wherewith to excuse themselves; since the handle of appointment and delegation is exclusive, the heart for makeshift expediency naturally ceases.
translations.idiomatic: The rewarded will not call it excessive; the punished will have no defense — with full authority vested in him, the impulse toward corner-cutting dies of itself.

sentences.zh: 是以古之遣將帥者，君親推轂而命之曰：「自閫以外，將軍裁之。

translations.literal: Therefore in ancient times, those dispatching generals and commanders — the ruler personally pushed the chariot wheel and commanded, saying: "From outside the gate onward, the general decides.
translations.idiomatic: Hence when ancient rulers sent forth their generals, the sovereign would push the chariot wheel and declare: "Beyond the camp gate, the general decides all.

sentences.zh: 」又賜鈇鉞，示令專斷。

translations.literal: " Again they bestowed axe and halberd, showing the order for exclusive judgment.
translations.idiomatic: " They also bestowed the battle-axe, signifying sole authority to command.

sentences.zh: 故軍容不入國，國容不入軍，將在軍，君命有所不受。

translations.literal: Therefore military deportment does not enter the state; state deportment does not enter the army — when the general is in the army, the ruler's commands are in some respects not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Military protocol stayed out of court, court protocol stayed out of camp — in the field, a general need not obey every royal order.

sentences.zh: 誠謂機宜不可以遠決，號令不可以兩從，未有委任不專，而望其克敵成功者也。

translations.literal: Truly it is said: opportune measures cannot be decided from afar; commands and orders cannot have two sources of obedience — never yet has there been one whose delegation was not exclusive yet who was expected to overcome the enemy and succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Critical decisions cannot be made from afar; orders cannot come from two masters — no commander given divided authority has ever defeated the enemy.

sentences.zh: 自頃邊軍去就，裁斷多出宸衷，選置戎臣，先求易制，多其部以分其力，輕其任以弱其心，雖有所懲，亦有所失。

translations.literal: Recently, frontier armies' coming and going — adjudication mostly issued from the imperial heart; in selecting and placing military ministers, one first seeks those easy to control — increase their departments to divide their strength, lighten their responsibilities to weaken their hearts; though in some respects there is restraint, in some respects there is also loss.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, every movement of frontier troops is decided by the throne; military officers are chosen for tractability — their commands multiplied to divide their power, their duties lightened to sap their authority. Some evils are checked, but much is lost.

sentences.zh: 遂令分閫責成之義廢，死綏任咎之誌衰，一則聽命，二亦聽命，爽於軍情亦聽命，乖於事宜亦聽命。

translations.literal: Thereupon the principle of dividing command with accountability is abandoned; the resolve to die holding the reins and bear blame fades — first it is obeying orders, second also obeying orders; contrary to military sentiment still obeying orders, contrary to the needs of affairs still obeying orders.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of divided command with full accountability is dead; the will to die at one's post rather than fail is gone — first they obey orders, then they obey orders again, even when military judgment or circumstances demand otherwise.

sentences.zh: 若所置將帥，必取於承順無違，則如斯可矣；

translations.literal: If the generals and commanders to be placed must be taken from those compliant and without opposition — then such as this will do;
translations.idiomatic: If commanders must be men of blind compliance, this approach suffices;

sentences.zh: 若有意平兇靖難，則不可。

translations.literal: If there is intent to pacify evil and settle difficulty — then it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: But if the aim is to subdue rebels and repel invaders, it will not do.

sentences.zh: 夫兩境相接，兩軍相持，事機之來，間不容息，蓄謀而俟，猶恐失之，臨時始謀，固已疏矣。

translations.literal: When two borders adjoin, two armies stand opposed — when opportunity comes, no interval permits a breath; storing plans and waiting, one still fears missing it; only at the moment beginning to plan, already it is lax.
translations.idiomatic: When two borders meet and two armies face each other, opportunity allows no pause — even prepared plans may be too late; improvisation on the spot is already too late.

sentences.zh: 況乎千里之遠，九重之深，陳述之難明，聽覽之不一，欲其事無遺策，雖聖者亦有所不能焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, a thousand li distant, the ninefold palace deep — difficult to make statements clear, not uniform in hearing and perusal — wishing that affairs be without omitted plans, even a sage has what he cannot do.
translations.idiomatic: How much worse across a thousand li, from the depths of the palace — reports are hard to make clear, audiences are inconsistent — to expect flawless strategy from afar exceeds even a sage's power.

sentences.zh: 設使謀慮能周，其如權變無及！

translations.literal: Even supposing planning and consideration can be comprehensive — how about flexibility and adaptation having no time to respond!
translations.idiomatic: Even if planning were perfect, there is no time for adaptation!

sentences.zh: 戎虜馳突，迅如風飈，驛書上聞，旬月方報。

translations.literal: Barbarian raiders charge and burst forth, swift as windstorm — dispatch reports reach the court, half a month or a month before there is reply.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian raiders strike swift as a gale — by the time a courier reaches court, a month may pass before any reply.

sentences.zh: 守土者以兵寡不敢抗敵，分鎮者以無詔不肯出師，逗留之間，寇已奔逼，托於救援未至，各且閉壘自全。

translations.literal: Those guarding the land, because troops are few dare not resist the enemy; those in divided commands, because there is no edict will not send out troops — in the delay, the bandits already press in pursuit; pleading that rescue has not arrived, each closes the fortress and preserves himself.
translations.idiomatic: Local defenders, too few to fight, dare not resist; neighboring commands, lacking imperial orders, refuse to march — while they delay, the raiders close in; claiming rescue has not arrived, each barricades his fortress and saves himself.

sentences.zh: 牧馬屯牛，鞠為椎剽；

translations.literal: Pastured horses, penned cattle — curled up into robbery by force;
translations.idiomatic: Horses and cattle are seized;

sentences.zh: 穡夫樵婦，罄作俘囚。

translations.literal: Reaping men and firewood-gathering women — entirely made captives.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers and woodcutters become prisoners.

sentences.zh: 雖詔諸鎮發兵，唯以虛聲應援，互相瞻顧，莫敢遮邀，賊既縱掠退歸，此乃陳功告捷。

translations.literal: Although edicts order the various commands to deploy troops, only with empty sound they respond in aid — mutually looking to one another, none dares intercept and block; once the bandits have finished plundering and withdrawn, then this is narrating merit and reporting victory.
translations.idiomatic: Though imperial orders summon troops from every command, they respond with empty gestures — watching one another, none dares intercept the enemy; when the raiders finish plundering and withdraw, they report victory.

sentences.zh: 其敗喪則減百而為一，其捃獲則張百而成千。

translations.literal: Their defeats and losses are reduced from a hundred to one; their gathered captures are expanded from a hundred to a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Defeats are reported as one in a hundred; booty inflated from hundreds to thousands.

sentences.zh: 將帥既幸於總制在朝，不憂於罪累；

translations.literal: Since generals and commanders already take fortune that overall control is in court, they do not worry about chains of guilt;
translations.idiomatic: Commanders, relieved that overall control rests at court, need not fear punishment;

sentences.zh: 陛下又以為大權由己，不究事情。

translations.literal: Your Majesty also considers that great power is in oneself, does not investigate the substance of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, satisfied that supreme authority is yours, does not examine the facts.

sentences.zh: 用師若斯，可謂機失於遙制矣！

translations.literal: Using troops like this — one may say the opportunity is lost through remote control!
translations.idiomatic: To wage war thus is to lose every advantage through remote command!

sentences.zh: 理兵而措置乖方，馭將而賞罰虧度，制用而財匱，建兵而力分，養士而怨生，用師而機失，此六者，疆場之蟊賊，軍旅之膏肓也。

translations.literal: Managing troops yet disposition is wrongly placed; controlling generals yet rewards and punishments fall short of measure; regulating expenditure yet funds are exhausted; building armies yet strength is divided; nourishing soldiers yet resentment arises; using troops yet opportunity is lost — these six are the crop pests of the frontier, the incurable affliction of the military.
translations.idiomatic: Misdeployment of forces, misjudgment in commanding and rewarding, depleted treasuries, divided military strength, resentful soldiers, lost opportunities in war — these six are pests devouring the frontier and maladies deep in the army's vitals.

sentences.zh: 蟊賊不除，而但滋之以糞溉，膏肓不療，而唯啖之以滑甘，適足以養其害，速其災，欲求稼穡豐登，膚革充美，固不可得也。

translations.literal: Crop pests not removed, yet only nourishing them with manure and irrigation; the incurable not treated, yet only feeding them with smooth sweetness — fitting only to nourish their harm, hasten their disaster; wishing to seek abundant harvest of grain, full and fair skin and hide — solidly cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Leave the pests and only add fertilizer; leave the disease untreated and only offer delicacies — you nourish the harm and hasten disaster. To expect rich harvests and flourishing prosperity is impossible.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂宜罷諸道將士番替防秋之制，率因舊數而三分之：其一分委本道節度使募少壯願住邊城者以徙焉；

translations.literal: Your subject in folly considers it fitting to abolish the system of rotation and autumn defense for troops of all circuits — generally following old numbers and dividing into three parts: one part — commission the circuit military governor to recruit young and strong willing to dwell in frontier fortresses to migrate there;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject proposes abolishing the rotational autumn-defense system for frontier garrisons and dividing existing force levels into three: one third — let each circuit governor recruit able-bodied men willing to settle on the frontier;

sentences.zh: 其一分則本道但供衣糧，委關內、河東諸軍州募蕃、漢子弟願傅邊軍者以給焉；

translations.literal: One part — then the circuit only supplies clothing and grain, commission the various army prefectures of Guannei and Hedong to recruit Tangut and Han youths willing to serve attached to frontier armies to supply them;
translations.idiomatic: One third — the home circuit provides rations while Guannei and Hedong recruit Han and non-Han youth willing to join frontier units;

sentences.zh: 又一分亦令本道但出衣糧，加給應募之人，以資新徙之業。

translations.literal: Again one part — also have the circuit only provide clothing and grain, additionally grant those who respond to recruitment, to support the enterprise of new migrants.
translations.idiomatic: A third portion — the home circuit again supplies rations, with additional grants to recruits to establish new settlements.

sentences.zh: 又令度支散於諸道和市耕牛，兼雇召工人，就諸軍城繕造器具。

translations.literal: Again command the Directorate of Public Revenue to distribute among the circuits to purchase plow oxen in the market, together with hiring craftsmen to repair and make implements at the various garrison fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Revenue should purchase plow oxen across the circuits and hire craftsmen to build equipment at each garrison.

sentences.zh: 募人至者，每家給耕牛一頭，又給田農水火之器，皆令充備。

translations.literal: When recruited men arrive, each household is given one plowing ox, further given farming and fire-water implements — all ordered fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Each arriving family should receive a plow ox and full farm implements.

sentences.zh: 初到之歲，與家口二人糧，並賜種子，勸之播植，待經一稔，俾自給家。

translations.literal: In the year of first arrival, grant rations for two family members, together bestow seed, encourage planting — wait until one harvest has passed, enable them to supply their own households.
translations.idiomatic: In their first year, provide rations for two dependents plus seed and encourage planting — after one harvest they should support themselves.

sentences.zh: 若有余糧，官為收糴，各酬倍價，務獎營田。

translations.literal: If there is surplus grain, the government purchases it, each paid double price — striving to encourage garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus grain should be bought by the state at double price to encourage frontier agriculture.

sentences.zh: 既息踐更征發之煩，且無幸災茍免之弊。

translations.literal: Both stopping the trouble of rotation and conscription, and also having none of the evil of rejoicing in disaster and casual evasion.
translations.idiomatic: This would end the burden of rotational service and eliminate the abuse of men who welcome disasters as excuses to shirk duty.

sentences.zh: 寇至則人自為戰，時至則家自力農。

translations.literal: When bandits come then each man fights for himself; when the season arrives then each household works the fields by itself.
translations.idiomatic: When enemies come, every man fights; when seasons turn, every household farms.

sentences.zh: 是乃兵不得不強，食不得不足，與夫倏來忽往，豈可同等而論哉！

translations.literal: This then is troops that cannot but be strong, provisions that cannot but be sufficient — compared with coming suddenly and going suddenly, how can they be spoken of as equal!
translations.idiomatic: Thus the army grows strong and provisions abundant — how can this compare with troops that appear and vanish like gusts of wind!

sentences.zh: 臣又謂宜擇文武能臣一人為隴右元帥，應涇、隴、鳳翔、長武城、山南西道等節度管內兵馬，悉以屬焉；

translations.literal: Your subject further considers it fitting to select one civil and military able minister as Longyou Marshal — responding to Jing, Long, Fengxiang, Changwucheng, Shannan West Circuit and other military governors' jurisdictions' troops and horses — entirely belong them to him;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject further proposes selecting one capable minister as Longyou commander-in-chief, placing all troops of Jing, Long, Fengxiang, Changwucheng, and Shannan West under his command;

sentences.zh: 又擇一人為朔方元帥，應鄜坊、邠寧、靈夏等節度管內兵馬，悉以屬焉；

translations.literal: Again select one person as Shuofang Marshal — responding to Fufang, Binning, Lingxia and other military governors' jurisdictions' troops and horses — entirely belong them to him;
translations.idiomatic: One as Shuofang commander, over troops of Fufang, Binning, Lingxia, and related commands;

sentences.zh: 又擇一人為河東元帥，河東、振武等節度管內兵馬，悉以屬焉。

translations.literal: Again select one person as Hedong Marshal — Hedong, Zhenwu and other military governors' jurisdictions' troops and horses — entirely belong them to him.
translations.idiomatic: One as Hedong commander, over Hedong, Zhenwu, and related commands.

sentences.zh: 三帥各選臨邊要會之州以為理所，見置節度，有非要者，隨所便近而並之。

translations.literal: The three marshals each select frontier key-junction prefectures as administrative seats; existing military governors — where not essential, according to convenience and proximity merge them.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the three commanders should establish headquarters at key frontier prefectures, merging existing commands where convenient and abolishing unnecessary ones.

sentences.zh: 唯元帥得置統軍，余並停罷。

translations.literal: Only the marshal may appoint army supervisors; the rest all cease and abolish.
translations.idiomatic: Only the commanders-in-chief may appoint army supervisors; all other such positions should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 其三帥部內太原、鳳翔等府及諸郡戶口稍多者，慎揀良吏以為尹守，外奉師律，內課農桑，俾為軍糧，以壯戎府。

translations.literal: Within the three marshals' departments, Taiyuan, Fengxiang and other prefectures and various commanderies with somewhat larger populations — carefully select good officials as prefects and magistrates; outwardly obey military discipline, inwardly assess agriculture and sericulture — enable them to serve as army grain, to strengthen the frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: In populous prefectures like Taiyuan and Fengxiang within each command, appoint capable magistrates who enforce military discipline outward and promote agriculture inward, building grain reserves to strengthen the frontier.

sentences.zh: 理兵之宜既得，選帥之授既明，然後減奸濫虛浮之費以豐財，定衣糧等級之制以和眾，弘委任之道以宣其用，懸賞罰之典以考其成。

translations.literal: The fitness of managing troops already obtained, the clarity of selecting marshals already established — afterward reduce corrupt, excessive, and empty expenditures to enrich finances, fix the system of clothing and grain grades to harmonize the masses, expand the way of delegation to display their use, hang the canon of rewards and punishments to examine their achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Once forces are properly organized and commanders clearly appointed, cut corrupt and wasteful spending to enrich the treasury, standardize rations to harmonize the ranks, extend full delegation to employ their talents, and establish clear rewards and punishments to measure results.

sentences.zh: 而又慎守中國之所長，謹行當今之所易，則八利可致，六失可除。

translations.literal: Moreover carefully hold to what China excels at, prudently carry out what is easy in the present age — then eight benefits can be attained, six failures can be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, hold fast to China's strengths and pursue reforms within reach — eight benefits will follow and the six failures be removed.

sentences.zh: 如是而戎狄不威懷，疆場不寧謐者，未之有也。

translations.literal: If so yet the Rong and Di are not awed and won over, the frontier is not peaceful and tranquil — never has there been such.
translations.idiomatic: If so, the barbarians will not fail to submit in awe, and the frontier will not fail to know peace.

sentences.zh: 諸侯軌道，庶類服從。

translations.literal: Feudal lords keep to the path, the myriad classes submit and obey.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords will keep to the path; the people will obey.

sentences.zh: 如是而教令不行，天下不理者，亦未之有也。

translations.literal: If so yet edicts and orders are not carried out, the realm is not governed — also never has there been such.
translations.idiomatic: If so, imperial commands will not go unheeded, and the realm will not fail to be governed.

sentences.zh: 以陛下之英鑒，民心之思安，四方之小休，兩寇之方靜，加以頻年豐稔，所在積糧，此皆天贊國家，可以立制垂統之時也。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's keen discernment, the people's hearts longing for peace, the four quarters' brief respite, the two bandits just quiet — added to years of abundant harvest, grain accumulated everywhere — all these are heaven aiding the state; it is the time to establish institutions and transmit them to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's keen judgment, the people's longing for peace, a brief respite on all sides, the two enemies temporarily quiet, and harvests abundant year after year with grain stored everywhere — heaven favors the state; this is the moment to establish enduring institutions.

sentences.zh: 時不久居，事不常兼，已過而追，雖悔無及。

translations.literal: Time does not long remain; affairs do not constantly coincide — once past and pursued, though regretting there is no reaching it.
translations.idiomatic: Favorable times do not linger; advantages rarely coincide — once past, regret avails nothing.

sentences.zh: 明主者，不以言為罪，不以人廢言，罄陳狂愚，惟所省擇。

translations.literal: A clear-sighted ruler does not take words as crime, does not discard words because of the person — fully set forth wild folly, only for Your Majesty's examination and choice.
translations.idiomatic: A wise sovereign does not punish honest speech or dismiss counsel because of the speaker — your subject lays out these crude thoughts for Your Majesty's consideration alone.

sentences.zh: 德宗極深嘉納，優詔褒獎之。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong extremely deeply praised and accepted, issued a gracious edict commending and rewarding him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong warmly approved and issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 贄在中書，政不便於時者，多所條奏。

translations.literal: Zhi, in the Secretariat, on policies not convenient for the times — many items memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: While Lu Zhi served in the Secretariat, he frequently memorialized on policies that harmed the times.

sentences.zh: 德宗雖不能皆可，而心頗重之。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong though could not approve all, yet in heart considerably valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong could not approve all his proposals, but held him in considerable regard.

sentences.zh: 初，竇參既貶郴州，節度使劉士寧餉參絹數千匹。

translations.literal: At first, after Dou Can was already demoted to Chenzhou, Military Governor Liu Shining presented Can several thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Dou Can was demoted to Chenzhou, Military Governor Liu Shining sent him several thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 湖南觀察使李巽與參有隙，具事奏聞，德宗不悅。

translations.literal: Hunan Observations Commissioner Li Xun had a rift with Can — fully reported the matter to the court; Emperor Dezong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan Observations Commissioner Li Xun, who bore a grudge against Dou Can, reported the matter in full; Emperor Dezong was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會右庶子姜公輔於上前聞奏，稱「竇參嘗語臣云：陛下怒臣未已」，德宗怒，再貶參，竟殺之。

translations.literal: It happened that Right Censor Jiang Gongfu before the throne heard and reported, saying "Dou Can once told your subject: 'Your Majesty's anger at your subject is not yet spent'" — Emperor Dezong was angry, again demoted Can, ultimately killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Right Censor Jiang Gongfu spoke before the throne, saying "Dou Can once told me: 'His Majesty's anger at me is not yet spent'" — the emperor's fury led to a second demotion and ultimately Dou Can's execution.

sentences.zh: 時議雲公輔奏竇參語得之於贄，雲參之死，贄有力焉。

translations.literal: Opinion at the time said Gongfu's memorial on Dou Can's words was obtained from Zhi; said Can's death — Zhi had force in it.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion at the time held that Jiang Gongfu had learned of Dou Can's words from Lu Zhi, and that Lu Zhi had played a part in Dou Can's death.

sentences.zh: 又素惡於公異、於邵，既輔政而逐之，談者亦以為厄。

translations.literal: Again, long at odds with Gong Yi and Yu Shao — once assisting in government then drove them out; discussants also considered it harsh.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been at odds with Gong Yi and Yu Shao; once in power he drove them out, which critics also regarded as harsh.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎、判度支裴延齡，奸宄用事，天下嫉之如仇。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue, acting Director of Public Revenue Pei Yanling — treacherous schemer wielding power; the realm hated him as an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling, Vice Minister of Revenue and acting director of the Directorate of Revenue, was a treacherous schemer in power — the world hated him as an enemy.

sentences.zh: 以得幸於天子，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Because he obtained favor from the Son of Heaven, none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Because he enjoyed the emperor's favor, no one dared speak against him.

sentences.zh: 贄獨以身當之，屢於延英面陳其不可，累上疏極言其弊。

translations.literal: Zhi alone with his person confronted it — repeatedly at Yanying Hall face to face stated its impossibility, repeatedly submitted memorials exhaustively stating its abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi alone stood in his path, repeatedly denouncing him before the throne in the Yanying Hall and submitting memorial after memorial on his abuses.

sentences.zh: 延齡日加譖毀。

translations.literal: Yanling daily added slander and defamation.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling daily added slanders against him.

sentences.zh: 十年十二月，除太子賓客，罷知政事。

translations.literal: Tenth year, twelfth month — appointed Guest of the Heir Apparent, dismissed from knowing government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the tenth year, Lu Zhi was appointed Guest of the Heir Apparent and removed from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 贄性畏慎，及策免私居，朝謁之外，不通賓客，無所過從。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was cautious and wary — once dismissed by edict and dwelling privately, beyond court audience he did not receive guests, had nowhere he went to associate.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi was by nature cautious; after his dismissal he stayed home, receiving no visitors beyond required court audiences.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，旱，邊軍芻粟不給，具事論訴；

translations.literal: Eleventh year, spring — drought; frontier armies' fodder and grain not supplied — fully reported the matter in petition;
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year, drought left frontier troops without fodder, and they petitioned in full detail;

sentences.zh: 延齡言贄與張滂、李充等搖動軍情，語在《延齡傳》。

translations.literal: Yanling said Zhi together with Zhang Pang, Li Chong and others stirred military sentiment — the account is in the 《Biography of Yanling》.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling charged that Lu Zhi, Zhang Pang, Li Chong, and others were stirring up military unrest — details are in the 《Biography of Yanling》.

sentences.zh: 德宗怒，將誅贄等四人，會諫議大夫陽城等極言論奏，乃貶贄為忠州別駕。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong was angry, about to execute Zhi and the four men — it happened that Remonstrance Counselor Yang Cheng and others exhaustively argued in memorials; then demoted Zhi to Assistant Administrator of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, enraged, was about to execute all four — but Remonstrance Counselor Yang Cheng and others argued fiercely before the throne, and Lu Zhi was demoted to Assistant Administrator of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 贄初入翰林，特承德宗異顧，歌詩戲狎，朝夕陪遊。

translations.literal: When Zhi first entered the Hanlin Academy, he specially received Emperor Dezong's exceptional regard — singing poems, jesting intimately, morning and evening accompanying in leisure.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zhi first entered the Hanlin Academy, he enjoyed Emperor Dezong's exceptional favor — singing, composing verses, jesting intimately, accompanying the emperor day and night.

sentences.zh: 及出居艱阻之中，雖有宰臣，而謀猷參決，多出於贄，故當時目為「內相」。

translations.literal: When they went out dwelling in hardship and peril — though there were chief ministers, yet counsel and deliberation mostly issued from Zhi; therefore contemporaries called him the "inner chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: During the hardships of the flight to Shanxi, though there were chancellors, most counsel and decisions came from Lu Zhi — contemporaries called him the "inner chancellor."

sentences.zh: 從幸山南，道途艱險，扈從不及，與帝相失，一夕不至，上喻軍士曰：「得贄者賞千金。

translations.literal: Following the fortune to Shannan — the road perilous and dangerous, the escort could not keep up, lost contact with the emperor, one night did not arrive — the emperor told the soldiers: "Whoever obtains Zhi will be rewarded a thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: During the journey to Shanxi, the road was perilous; Lu Zhi fell behind the escort and missed the emperor by a night. The emperor told the troops: "Whoever finds Lu Zhi will receive a thousand in gold.

sentences.zh: 」翌日贄謁見，上喜形顏色，其寵待如此。

translations.literal: " The next day Zhi paid audience — the emperor's joy showed in his countenance; such was the favor he received.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day Lu Zhi presented himself — the emperor's joy showed on his face. Such was the favor he received.

sentences.zh: 既與二吳不協，漸加浸潤，恩禮稍薄；

translations.literal: Once at odds with the two Wus, gradually slander was added, grace and courtesy slightly thinned;
translations.idiomatic: After falling out with the two Wus, slander gradually took effect and imperial kindness waned;

sentences.zh: 及通玄敗，上知誣枉，遂復見用。

translations.literal: When Tong Xuan was defeated, the emperor knew false accusation and wrong — then again he was employed.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Xuan's plot failed, the emperor recognized the false accusation and restored Lu Zhi to favor.

sentences.zh: 贄以受人主殊遇，不敢愛身，事有不可，極言無隱。

translations.literal: Zhi, because he received the ruler's exceptional treatment, dared not spare his person — when affairs were not acceptable, spoke to the utmost without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Having received the sovereign's extraordinary grace, Lu Zhi dared not spare himself — when something was wrong, he spoke without concealment.

sentences.zh: 朋友規之，以為太峻，贄曰：「吾上不負天子，下不負吾所學，不恤其他。

translations.literal: Friends admonished him, considering it too severe — Zhi said: "Above I do not fail the Son of Heaven, below I do not fail what I have learned — I do not care for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Friends warned him he was too severe. Lu Zhi replied: "Above, I do not fail the Son of Heaven; below, I do not fail what I have learned — I care for nothing else.

sentences.zh: 」精於吏事，斟酌決斷，不失錙銖。

translations.literal: " Skilled in administrative affairs, weighing and deciding, not missing a fraction of a grain.
translations.idiomatic: " He was skilled in administrative affairs, weighing every decision to the smallest fraction.

sentences.zh: 嘗以「詞詔所出，中書舍人之職，軍興之際，促迫應務，權令學士代之；

translations.literal: Once stated: "Proclamations and edicts issued — the duty of Secretariat Drafters; at the rise of war, urgent and pressed in responding to affairs, temporarily ordered academicians to substitute;
translations.idiomatic: He once argued: "Proclamations and edicts are properly the duty of Secretariat Drafters; in wartime urgency it was permitted to let academicians stand in temporarily;

sentences.zh: 朝野乂寧，合歸職分，其命將相制詔，卻付中書行譴。

translations.literal: Court and realm at peace and order — should return to proper duties; those appointing generals and chancellors and drafting edicts — instead entrust to the Secretariat to carry out and dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Now that court and country are at peace, those duties should revert — appointments of generals and chancellors and formal edicts should return to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 」又言「學士私臣，玄宗初令待詔，止於唱和文章而已」。

translations.literal: " Again stated: "Academicians are private retainers — Emperor Xuanzong initially ordered them to wait on edicts, stopping at composing and responding in literary works, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said: "Academicians are private retainers — Emperor Xuanzong initially had them wait on edicts merely to compose poetry in reply."

sentences.zh: 物議是之。

translations.literal: Public opinion approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 德宗以贄指斥通微、通玄，故不可其奏。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong, because Zhi pointed and reproached Tong Wei and Tong Xuan, therefore did not approve his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong rejected his memorial because it implicitly condemned Tong Wei and Tong Xuan.

sentences.zh: 贄在忠州十年，常閉關靜處，人不識其面，復避謗，不著書。

translations.literal: Zhi in Zhongzhou ten years — constantly closed the gate and dwelt quietly; people did not know his face; again avoiding slander, did not write books.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi spent ten years in Zhongzhou behind closed doors — so reclusive that people did not know his face; fearing slander, he wrote no books.

sentences.zh: 家居瘴鄉，人多癘疫，乃抄撮方書，為《陸氏集驗方》五十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: Dwelling in a malarial region, many people had pestilence — then copied and gathered formula books, made 《Lu's Collected Verified Formulas》 in fifty volumes, circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Living in a malarial region where pestilence was common, he compiled medical formulas into fifty volumes titled 《Lu's Collected Verified Formulas》, which circulated in his age.

sentences.zh: 初，贄秉政，貶駕部員外郎李吉甫為明州長史，量移忠州刺史。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhi held government, demoted Transport Office Vice Director Li Jiyuan to chief administrator of Mingzhou, transferred by measure to prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Lu Zhi held power, he had demoted Li Jiyuan, Vice Director of the Transport Office, to chief administrator of Mingzhou, later transferred to prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 贄在忠州，與吉甫相遇，昆弟、門人鹹為贄憂，而吉甫忻然厚禮，都不銜前事，以宰相禮事之，猶恐其未信不安，日與贄相狎，若平生交契者。

translations.literal: Zhi in Zhongzhou, meeting Jiyu — brothers, disciples and students all worried for Zhi; yet Jiyu gladly with thick courtesy, entirely bore no grudge for former matters, with chancellor's courtesy served him, still fearing he had not yet believed and was uneasy — daily kept close company with Zhi as if lifelong sworn friends.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zhi was in Zhongzhou and met Li Jiyuan, Lu's brothers, disciples, and students all feared for him — but Li Jiyuan received him warmly, bore no grudge, treated him with the courtesy owed a chancellor, and daily kept close company as if they had been friends all along.

sentences.zh: 贄初猶慚懼，後乃深交。

translations.literal: Zhi at first still ashamed and afraid; afterward then deep friendship.
translations.idiomatic: At first Lu Zhi was ashamed and afraid; afterward they became close friends.

sentences.zh: 時論以吉甫為長者。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time considered Jiyu a man of magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion hailed Li Jiyuan as a man of magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 後有薛延者，代吉甫為刺史，延朝辭日，德宗令宣旨慰安。

translations.literal: Later there was Xue Yan, who replaced Jiyu as prefect — on the day Yan took leave at court, Emperor Dezong ordered comforting words conveyed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xue Yan succeeded Li Jiyuan as prefect; on the day Xue took leave at court, Emperor Dezong had comforting words conveyed to Lu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 而韋臯累上表請以贄代己。

translations.literal: Yet Wei Gao repeatedly submitted memorials requesting to have Zhi replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wei Gao repeatedly memorialized asking that Lu Zhi replace him.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，與陽城、鄭余慶同詔征還。

translations.literal: Emperor Shunzong ascended — together with Yang Cheng and Zheng Yuqing, same edict summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong ascended, Lu Zhi was summoned back by edict along with Yang Cheng and Zheng Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 詔未至而贄卒，時年五十二，贈兵部尚書，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: The edict had not arrived when Zhi died — at the time age fifty-two; posthumously granted Minister of War, posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived, Lu Zhi died at fifty-two — posthumously honored as Minister of War, posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子簡禮，登進士第，累辟使府。

translations.literal: His son Jianli — passed the jinshi examination, repeatedly invited to commissioner staffs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jianli passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly invited to serve in provincial staffs.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：近代論陸宣公，比漢之賈誼，而高邁之行，剛正之節，經國成務之要，激切仗義之心，初蒙天子重知，末塗淪躓，皆相類也。

translations.literal: The historian says: In recent times discussing Lu Xuangong, comparing him to Han's Jia Yi — yet lofty conduct, upright integrity, the essentials of governing the state and accomplishing affairs, fierce devotion to righteousness — first receiving the Son of Heaven's deep trust, final path fallen and stumbled — all are alike.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: In recent times Lu Xuangong has been compared to Jia Yi of Han — in lofty conduct, upright integrity, mastery of statecraft, and fierce devotion to righteousness; first enjoying the emperor's deep trust, then suffering ruin at the end — they are alike in all this.

sentences.zh: 而誼止中大夫，贄及臺鉉，不為不遇矣。

translations.literal: Yet Yi stopped at Grand Master of the Palace; Zhi reached the terrace and halberd — not failing to meet with favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jia Yi reached only Grand Master of the Palace, while Lu Zhi attained the chancellorship — he was hardly ill-treated.

sentences.zh: 昔公孫鞅挾三策說秦王，淳于髡以隱語見齊君，從古以還，正言不易。

translations.literal: Formerly Gongsun Yang brought three plans to persuade the King of Qin; Chunyu Kun with hidden words gained audience with the King of Qi — from antiquity until now, straight words are not easy.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Gongsun Yang brought three plans to the King of Qin; Chunyu Kun won audience with the King of Qi through riddles — from antiquity onward, honest speech has never been easy.

sentences.zh: 昔周昭戒急論議，正為此也。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Zhao of Zhou warned against hasty debate — precisely for this.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao of Zhou warned against hasty debate — precisely for this reason.

sentences.zh: 贄居珥筆之列，調飪之地，欲以片心除眾弊，獨手遏群邪，君上不亮其誠，群小共攻其短，欲無放逐，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Zhi dwelt in the rank of brush behind the ear, the place of preparing counsel — wishing with a single heart to remove the multitude of abuses, alone with his hand to hold back the multitude of villains — the ruler above did not brighten his sincerity, petty men together attacked his faults — wishing not to be exiled, how could it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi stood among the draftsmen and stewards of counsel, seeking with his single heart to remove countless abuses and alone hold back the multitude of villains — the sovereign did not credit his sincerity, petty men together attacked his faults — how could exile have been avoided!

sentences.zh: 《詩》稱「其維哲人，告之話言」，又有「誨爾」、「聽我」之恨，此皆賢人君子，嘆言不見用也。

translations.literal: The Odes say, "Only the wise man—tell him plain speech," and again there is the regret of "I instruct you" and "hear me"—all these are worthy gentlemen lamenting that their words were not employed.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes praises the wise ruler who heeds frank counsel, and mourns the teacher whose words go unheeded—such is the lament of every worthy man whose advice is ignored.

sentences.zh: 故堯咨禹拜，千載一時，攜手提耳，豈容易哉！

translations.literal: Therefore when Yao consulted and Yu bowed—it was a moment once in a thousand years; taking hand and lifting ear—how could it be easy!
translations.idiomatic: When Yao sought counsel and Yu received it, that was a bond rare in a thousand years—hand in hand, whispering guidance. Such trust is not easily won!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：良臣悟主，我有嘉猷。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: A good minister enlightens his lord; I have a fine plan.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: The worthy minister enlightens his sovereign—I have a plan that will avail.

sentences.zh: 多僻之君，為善不周。

translations.literal: A lord of many perversities does good incompletely.
translations.idiomatic: The perverse ruler practices virtue only in part.

sentences.zh: 忠言救失，啟沃曰讎。

translations.literal: Loyal words rescue faults; nourishing counsel is called an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal counsel repairs error, yet frank guidance is treated as a foe.

sentences.zh: 勿貽天問，蒼昊悠悠。

translations.literal: Do not leave Heaven questioning; the azure vault stretches vast and far.
translations.idiomatic: Lest Heaven itself pose the question—under the endless sky.
